name: Pizza Delivery
nearest_infosys_question: Q0253 Distribute wealth to warehouses
brief: Courier goes from (Ax,Ay) to (Bx,By) with Manhattan moves and must visit n houses, all with Ax<x_i<Bx. Minimize total time.
key_idea: Sweep x left to right (horizontal cost Bx-Ax); in each column cover [minY,maxY] ending at bottom or top -> 2-state DP.
solution:
1. Group houses by x; for each distinct x (sorted) keep lo=min y, hi=max y.
2. Horizontal distance is always Bx-Ax (never go back in x).
3. State: (end at lo, end at hi) with best vertical cost; start y=Ay with cost 0.
4. For a column from previous y position py with cost c: endLo=c+|py-hi|+(hi-lo); endHi=c+|py-lo|+(hi-lo); take mins over both previous states.
5. Answer = (Bx-Ax) + min over states of cost+|y-By|. Use long long.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

name: Restaurant
nearest_infosys_question: Q0488 Machine Cooling and Task Scheduling
brief: n<=5e5 closed intervals [l_i, r_i]; choose the maximum number of pairwise non-overlapping intervals, where touching at an endpoint counts as overlapping.
key_idea: Classic activity selection: sort by right end and take an interval whenever its start is strictly greater than the last taken end.
solution:
1. Sort intervals by r ascending.
2. last = 0 (all l >= 1); cnt = 0.
3. For each interval: if l > last, take it: cnt++, last = r.
4. Strict '>' because sharing an instant is a conflict.
5. Print cnt.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

Take [1,2] (last=2); [2,3]: 2>2? no; take [3,4] (last=4); skip [4,5]; take [5,6].
Answer 3 (matches).

name: Mysterious Present
nearest_infosys_question: Q0230 Maximum gates taken (2D DP like LIS)
brief: Card w x h and n envelopes; build the longest chain of envelopes strictly increasing in both width and height, with the card fitting strictly inside the first. Print the length and indices (0 if none).
key_idea: Keep only envelopes larger than the card, sort by width then height, and run O(n^2) LIS with strict 2D comparison plus parent pointers.
solution:
1. Filter envelopes with w_i>w and h_i>h; if none print 0.
2. Sort by (w,h).
3. dp[i]=1+max dp[j] over j<i with w_j<w_i and h_j<h_i; store parent.
4. Take the best end, follow parents back, reverse and print original indices.

key_idea: Sort descending and close a team as soon as count*current(min) >= x.

name: K for the Price of One (Hard Version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0222 Hotel guests unhappiness
brief: n goods with prices a_i and p coins; buy one good for its price, or k goods for the price of the most expensive among them. Maximize goods bought.
key_idea: Sort ascending; dp[i]=dp[i-k]+a[i] (bundle ending at i), and for i<k dp[i]=dp[i-1]+a[i].
solution:
1. Sort prices ascending (cheapest goods are always optimal to take).
2. dp[i] = minimal cost to buy the i cheapest goods (1-indexed).
3. i<k: dp[i]=dp[i-1]+a[i] (single purchases as prefix); i>=k: dp[i]=dp[i-k]+a[i] (last k bought as one bundle).
4. Answer = largest i with dp[i]<=p (0 if none). Use long long.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

name: Road Optimization
nearest_infosys_question: Q0261 Group knapsack with no adjacent groups
brief: Road from 0 to l with n speed-limit signs (position d_i, a_i minutes per km, valid until next sign). Remove at most k signs (not the first) to minimize travel time.
key_idea: dp[i][r] = min time to reach kept sign i having removed r signs so far; transition from previous kept sign p removes the i-p-1 signs between.
solution:
1. Append a virtual sign n+1 at position l.
2. dp[1][0]=0; others INF.
3. For i=2..n+1, for p<i, removed between = i-p-1; for r: dp[i][r+i-p-1] = min(dp[p][r] + a_p*(d_i-d_p)) if r+i-p-1<=k.
4. Answer = min over r<=k of dp[n+1][r].
5. Values up to 1e9 fit in long long.

name: Phone Talks

brief: n<=4000 calls (start t_i, duration d_i, sorted), handled FIFO; you may ignore up to k calls. Maximise the longest free interval inside seconds 1..86400.
key_idea: dp[i][j] = earliest free second after the first i calls with j ignored; the best gap after state (i,j) is to ignore the next k-j calls entirely.
solution:
1. dp[0][0]=1 (first free second). Take call i+1: max(dp,t)+d; ignore: dp[i+1][j+1]=dp.
2. For each (i,j): next taken call is i+1+(k-j); gap = t_that - dp[i][j] (or 86401 - dp if none).
3. Answer = max gap (>=0). If k>=n answer 86400.
4. Ignoring consecutive calls is optimal for a single gap.

name: Woodcutters
nearest_infosys_question: Q0481 Temperature Cooling
brief: n trees at sorted distinct positions x_i with heights h_i. Each tree can be felled left [x-h,x], right [x,x+h], or left standing; segments may not contain any occupied point. Maximize felled trees.
key_idea: Scan left to right: prefer felling left (uses no future space), else fell right if it does not reach the next tree, else leave it; track the last occupied coordinate.
solution:
1. last = -inf, ans = 0.
2. For tree i: if x_i - h_i > last: fell left, ans++, last = x_i.
3. Else if i is the last tree or x_i + h_i < x_{i+1}: fell right, ans++, last = x_i + h_i.
4. Else last = x_i (stands).
5. Use long long for x+h. (DP with states left/stand/right gives the same.)

name: Buns
nearest_infosys_question: Q0232 Knapsack with additional constraints
brief: Have n grams of dough and m stuffings; bun type i needs b_i stuffing (a_i available) and c_i dough, worth d_i; plain bun needs c0 dough worth d0. Maximize earnings.
key_idea: Bounded knapsack over dough: stuffing i gives at most a_i/b_i copies; plain bun is unbounded.
solution:
1. dp[w] = max money using at most w grams of dough (init 0).
2. For each stuffing i, cnt=a_i/b_i; repeat cnt times a 0/1 pass: for w=n..c_i: dp[w]=max(dp[w], dp[w-c_i]+d_i).
3. Plain bun: unbounded pass for w=c0..n: dp[w]=max(dp[w], dp[w-c0]+d0).
4. Answer dp[n]. Sizes tiny (n<=1000, cnt<=100, m<=10).
complexity: O(n * sum cnt_i) ~ 1e6 time, O(n) space

nearest_infosys_question: Q0279 Last Stone Weight II with adjacency bonus R
brief: Paint n boards (heights h_i) red or green with total red area <= a and green area <= b. Minimize sum over adjacent different-colored boards of min(h_i, h_{i+1}); -1 if impossible. (Uses input.txt/output.txt.)
key_idea: dp[i][red area][color of board i] = min unattractiveness; green area is implied by prefix sum minus red area.
solution: 1) pre = prefix heights; dp[r][c] for current board (rolling). 2) Board 0: dp[h0][red]=0, dp[0][green]=0. 3) Board i: for each r, previous color pc, new color c: newR = r + (c==red ? h_i : 0); cost += (pc != c) ? min(h_{i-1}, h_i) : 0. 4) Answer = min over r <= a with pre[n] - r <= b of dp[r][*]; else -1. 5) Open input.txt/output.txt.

3. For each fruit, iterate a copy (0/1 knapsack): ndp[bal+w] = max(ndp[bal+w], dp[bal]+a_i).
4. Answer dp[OFF] if > 0 (non-empty since a_i >= 1) else -1.

2. For each item, for j from n down to 0: dp[min(n, j+t_i+1)] = min(.., dp[j] + c_i).

name: Serval and The Formula
nearest_infosys_question: Q0131 Maximize sum of (X XOR a[i]) for X in [0,K]
brief: Given positive x, y (<= 1e9), find k >= 0 (k <= 1e18) with (x+k) + (y+k) = (x+k) XOR (y+k), or print -1.
key_idea: Sum equals XOR iff the two numbers share no set bit. If x == y it's impossible. Otherwise push the larger one up to a power of two 2^p >= max: k = 2^p - max; the smaller becomes min + k < 2^p, so no common bits.
solution:
1. If x == y print -1.
2. p = smallest power of two with 2^p >= max(x, y).
3. k = 2^p - max(x, y). Then max+k = 2^p (single bit) and min+k < 2^p.
4. Print k (any valid answer is accepted).
complexity: O(log max) per test, O(1) space
dry_run:

Sample prints 1 (also valid); any answer accepted.
Sample 6 6 -> -1.

name: Party Lemonade
nearest_infosys_question: Q0131 Maximize sum of (X XOR a[i]) for X in [0,K]
brief: n bottle types; type i holds 2^(i-1) liters and costs c_i, unlimited supply. Find the minimum cost to buy at least L liters.
key_idea: Normalize c_i=min(c_i,2*c_{i-1}), then go from the largest bottle down, either filling greedily or overshooting with one extra bottle.
solution:
1. For i>=1: c[i]=min(c[i], 2*c[i-1]) (two smaller bottles may be cheaper).
2. cost=0; for i=n-1..0: k=L/2^i; cost+=k*c[i]; L-=k*2^i; ans=min(ans, cost + (L>0 ? c[i] : 0)).
3. ans=min(ans,cost) at the end (the overshoot option covers buying one extra bottle). Use long long (up to ~1e18).

name: Money Buys Happiness
nearest_infosys_question: Q0307 Powers of 2 and 5 subset product 10^z
brief: Salary x arrives at the end of each of m<=50 months; in month i you may buy happiness h_i once for cost c_i using only money earned before month i. Maximize total happiness (sum h <= 1e5).
key_idea: Costs are huge but happiness is small: dp[h] = minimum money spent to obtain happiness exactly h.
solution: 1) H = sum h_i; dp[0]=0, others INF. 2) For month i (1-indexed), budget = (i-1)*x. 3) For h from H down to h_i: if dp[h-h_i]+c_i <= budget, dp[h]=min(dp[h], dp[h-h_i]+c_i). 4) Answer = largest h with dp[h] < INF. 5) Use long long.
complexity: O(m * sum h) time, O(sum h) space

name: Extreme Subtraction
nearest_infosys_question: Q0281 Array Minimization Game
brief: Array a of positive ints. Operation: decrement the first k or the last k elements by 1. Can all elements become zero?
key_idea: a must split as p+s with p non-increasing (prefix ops) and s non-decreasing (suffix ops), both >= 0; greedily keep p as large as possible.
solution: 1) p=a[0], s=0. 2) For i=1..n-1: s = max(s, a[i]-p) (s must not decrease, and p cannot increase); p = a[i]-s. 3) If p<0 at any point -> NO. 4) Otherwise YES.

brief: n<=100 items: save time t_i, burn time d_i, value p_i. Save items sequentially; each must finish strictly before its d_i. Maximise value; print the chosen items in order.
key_idea: Any feasible set is feasible in order of increasing d (exchange argument); then 0/1 knapsack over finishing time.
solution:

2. dp[i][T] = max value using first i items finishing at time T.
3. Take item i at time T if T + t_i < d_i: dp[i+1][T+t_i] = dp[i][T] + p_i.

name: Covered Path
nearest_infosys_question: Q0481 Temperature Cooling
brief: Speed in second 1 is v1, in second t is v2, adjacent seconds differ by at most d. Maximize total distance (sum of speeds).
key_idea: Speed at second i is at most v1+(i-1)d and at most v2+(t-i)d; taking the min of both bounds is feasible and optimal.
solution:
1. For i=1..t: v_i = min(v1+(i-1)*d, v2+(t-i)*d).
2. Sum all v_i.
3. The pointwise min of two d-Lipschitz bounds is itself d-Lipschitz, so it is valid.

name: Coloring Trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0319 Pizza with 3N Slices and K Tolerance Tokens
brief: n trees, some precolored (0 = uncolored); painting tree i with color j costs p[i][j]. Color all uncolored trees so the number of same-color segments is exactly k, minimizing paint; -1 if impossible.
key_idea: dp[i][j][c] = min cost for first i trees with j segments and tree i of color c.
solution:
1. Allowed colors of tree i: only c_i if precolored (cost 0), else all 1..m with cost p[i][c].
2. dp[1][1][c] = cost(1,c).
3. dp[i][j][c] = cost(i,c) + min(dp[i-1][j][c], min over c'!=c of dp[i-1][j-1][c']).
4. Speed up with best and second-best of dp[i-1][j-1][*] (or plain O(n k m^2)=1e8).
5. Answer min_c dp[n][k][c], -1 if INF. Use long long.
complexity: O(n*k*m) time with best-two trick, O(n*k*m) space

name: Chef Monocarp
tags: dp, flows, graph matchings, greedy, math, sortings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0296 Hotel customers minimum unhappiness (Chef Monocarp)
brief: n<=200 dishes with optimal times t_i (<=n). Take them out at distinct positive integer minutes T; cost |T-t_i|. Minimize total cost.
key_idea: Sort t; dishes are taken out in sorted order at increasing times (exchange argument), and times never need to exceed 2n.
solution: 1) Sort t. 2) dp[i][T] = min cost to place first i dishes using minutes 1..T. 3) dp[0][T]=0; dp[i][T]=min(dp[i][T-1], dp[i-1][T-1]+|T-t_i|). 4) T up to 2n; answer dp[n][2n].
dry_run: Sample1: t=4 2 4 4 5 2 -> sorted 2 2 4 4 4 5. Best times 1,2,3,4,5,6 give costs 1,0,1,0,1,1 = 4. Output 4.

name: Messenger in MAC
tags: binary search, brute force, constructive algorithms, data structures, dp, greedy, sortings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0294 Kevin and Paul array game
brief: n messages (a_i,b_i). Choosing a set in some order costs sum a + sum |b| differences of consecutive ones. Max set size with cost <= l.
key_idea: Sorted by b, the b-part of cost is just b_max - b_min; fix the endpoints l..r and greedily keep the smallest a's in between.
solution: 1) Sort messages by b. 2) For each left L: clear a max-heap, sum=0. 3) For r=L..n-1: push a_r, sum+=a_r; while heap nonempty and sum + b_r - b_L > l: pop largest a. 4) ans = max(ans, heap size). Popping the largest is safe because cost only grows with r. 5) Use long long.
complexity: O(n^2 log n) per test (sum n^2 <= 4e6)

name: Winter Is Coming
nearest_infosys_question: Q0517 Min swaps to maximize product of pair sums
brief: n days with temperatures; summer tires only for t>=0, winter tires any day but at most k days total. Start on summer tires; minimize tire changes, or -1.
key_idea: Each block of negative days costs 2 changes; spare winter days can fill the gaps between blocks (saving 2 each, smallest gaps first) and possibly the tail after the last block (saving 1).
solution: 1) cnt = number of negative days; if cnt > k -> -1; if cnt == 0 -> 0. 2) rem = k - cnt; groups = number of negative blocks; ans = 2*groups. 3) gaps = lengths of non-negative stretches between blocks; tail = non-negative days after the last block. 4) Option A: fill sorted gaps greedily with rem (ans -= 2 each). Option B: if tail <= rem, cover tail first (ans -= 1) then fill gaps. 5) Answer = min of options.
dry_run: Sample -5 20 -3 0, k=3: cnt=2, rem=1, groups=2 -> 4. gap [1] filled -> 2. Option B: tail 1 -> 3, no rem left -> 3. Answer 2.

name: The Values You Can Make
nearest_infosys_question: Q0270 Split array into two subsequences with equal sum and equal count
brief: n coins (values <= 500), pay exactly k with a subset; list all x that can be formed as a sub-sum of some subset summing to k.
key_idea: 2D knapsack: dp[s] = bitset of sub-sums x achievable inside some subset with sum s; adding coin c: dp[s+c] |= dp[s] | (dp[s] << c).
solution: 1) dp[0] = {0}. 2) For each coin c, for s = k-c down to 0: dp[s+c] |= dp[s] | (dp[s] << c). 3) Output all x with dp[k][x] set, count first.
complexity: O(n * k * k / 64) time, O(k^2) bits
dry_run: Sample k=18 coins 5 6 1 10 12 2: subsets {5,1,12}, {6,10,2}, {5,1,10,2}... union of their sub-sums gives 16 values 0 1 2 3 5 6 7 8 10 11 12 13 15 16 17 18.

name: Education
nearest_infosys_question: Q0253 Distribute wealth to warehouses
brief: Positions 1..n pay a_i per day (non-decreasing). Each day either earn a_x, or pay b_x to move from x to x+1. Starting at position 1 with 0 money, find the minimum days to have at least c.
key_idea: Try 'stop at position i' for every i: track minimum days and leftover money to reach each position, then finish by earning there.
solution:
1. days=0, money=0, ans=INF.
2. For i=1..n: ans = min(ans, days + ceil(max(0,c-money)/a_i)).
3. If i<n: need = max(0, ceil((b_i-money)/a_i)) days of work; days += need+1; money += need*a_i - b_i.
4. Reaching each position as early as possible with the max leftover is optimal since moving earlier never hurts (a non-decreasing).
5. Use long long.
dry_run:
Sample 1: c=15,a=[1,3,10,11],b=[1,2,7].
i=1: ans=15; work 1 day, move: days=2,money=0.
i=2: ans=2+5=7; work 1 (money 3), move: days=4,money=1.
i=3: ans=4+ceil(14/10)=6; move: work 1 -> money 11-7=4, days=6.
i=4: 6+1=7. Answer 6.

name: Pictures with Kittens (easy version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0261 Group knapsack with no adjacent groups
brief: n<=200 pictures with beauty a_i; repost exactly x of them so that every k consecutive pictures contain a repost. Maximise total beauty or print -1.
key_idea: dp[i][j] = best sum with j reposts, last repost at i; previous repost must be within the last k positions.
solution:
1. dp[0][0]=0, others -INF (position 0 = virtual start).
2. dp[i][j] = a_i + max dp[p][j-1] for p in [max(0,i-k), i-1].
3. Answer = max dp[i][x] for i in [n-k+1, n] (no gap of k at the end); -1 if all -INF.
4. Use long long.
dry_run:
Sample n=5,k=2,x=3, a=5 1 3 10 1.
Chosen 1,3,4: gaps ok (<=1 between), last at 4 >= n-k+1=4.
Sum 5+3+10 = 18 (matches).

name: Wishing Cards
nearest_infosys_question: Q0261 Group knapsack with no adjacent groups
brief: Choose b_i with 0<=b_i<=a_i and sum b_i <= k (k<=360) to maximize the sum over j of max(b_1..b_j).
key_idea: Only positions where a_i is a strict prefix maximum need to start a new record, because moving a record earlier only helps. There are at most k+1 such positions. Run a DP over them with state (cards used, current max).
solution:
1. Collect the candidates P = positions where a_i > all earlier a.
2. dp[s][m] = best happiness so far using s cards with current max m. Start with dp[0][0]=0.
3. At candidate p: either skip it, or set a new max v in (m, a_p] with s+v<=k. Use a running prefix max over m<v.
4. Then add m*(next candidate position - p) to every state, using n for the last one. The answer is the max over all states.
complexity: O(k^3) per test, and the sum of k is <= 1800
dry_run:
Sample 3: a=1 0 4, k=4, candidates at positions 0 and 2.
Take b=1 at position 0: it adds 1*2. Then v=3 at position 2 (1+3=4 cards) adds 3, for a total of 5.
Other splits give less, e.g. v=4 alone gives 4.
Answer 5 (matches).

name: Bottles
nearest_infosys_question: Q0177 Coin change minimum coins (interactive)
brief: Bottle i holds a_i units of soda and has capacity b_i. Pour all the soda into the fewest bottles k, and among those choices minimize the amount poured, t.
key_idea: k comes from greedily taking the largest capacities until they hold all the soda. Then pick k bottles with total capacity >= the total soda while maximizing the soda already inside them. t = total - that maximum.
solution:
1. A = sum of a. Sort b in descending order and take the shortest prefix whose sum is >= A. Its length is k.
2. dp[j][v] = max sum of a using j chosen bottles with total capacity v. This is a 0/1 knapsack with j going down.
3. best = max of dp[k][v] for v >= A.
4. Output k and A-best.
dry_run:
Sample: A=13. The capacities sorted are 7,6,5,4, and 7+6=13 >= 13, so k=2.
Choosing bottles 2 and 3 (caps 7+6=13 >= 13) gives a=3+4=7.
t = 13-7 = 6. Output '2 6' (matches).

name: Ciel and Duel
nearest_infosys_question: Q0470 Minimum ATM Withdrawals
brief: Ciel attacks with ATK cards. Attacking a Jiro ATK card needs X>=Y and deals X-Y damage. Attacking a DEF card needs X>Y and deals 0. Once Jiro has no cards, attacks hit him directly for X. Maximize the damage.
key_idea: Only two plans can be optimal. (A) Pit Ciel's strongest cards against Jiro's weakest ATK cards, using some prefix. (B) Kill everything: beat each DEF with the smallest card that is strictly bigger, then the rest kill all ATK and hit directly, for damage = sum(remaining cards) - sum(ATK).
solution:
1. Sort everything.
2. Plan A: for i=0..: pair c[m-1-i] with atk[i] while c >= atk, and take the best prefix sum of (c-atk).
3. Plan B: for each DEF in ascending order, remove the smallest card > DEF from a multiset. If impossible, skip plan B.
4. Check that the largest |ATK| remaining cards can beat the ATK cards in sorted pairing. If so, the damage is sum(remaining) - sum(ATK).
5. Answer max(A, B).
dry_run:
Sample: ATK 2000, DEF 1700, three cards of 2500.
Plan A: 2500-2000 = 500.
Plan B: one 2500 kills the DEF. The other two give 5000-2000 = 3000.
Answer 3000 (matches).

name: Polycarp and Div 3
nearest_infosys_question: Q0646 Booster to maximise array product
brief: Given a digit string s (up to 2e5 digits), cut it into parts (no leading zeros unless the part is '0') to maximise the number of parts divisible by 3.
key_idea: Scan greedily: close a part as soon as the current digit is divisible by 3, the running digit sum is divisible by 3, or 3 digits accumulated (any 3 digits contain a divisible-by-3 suffix).
solution:
1. Keep sum (mod 3) and length of the current open part.
2. For each digit d: sum+=d, len++.
3. If d%3==0 or sum%3==0 or len==3: ans++, reset sum=len=0.
4. Leading zeros never arise because every 0 digit closes a part by itself.
5. Print ans.
dry_run:
Sample 3121:
'3': d%3==0 -> ans=1, reset.
'1': sum=1. '2': sum=3 -> ans=2, reset.
'1': sum=1, end. Answer 2.

name: Maximum Sum on Even Positions
tags: divide and conquer, dp, greedy, implementation
nearest_infosys_question: Q0281 Array Minimization Game
brief: Array a (0-indexed). Reverse at most one subarray to maximize the sum of elements at even indices.
key_idea: Only even-length reversals change the sum; they swap parities of pairs. Gain arrays: g1 = a[i+1]-a[i] for even i, g2 = a[i]-a[i+1] for odd i; answer = base + max(0, best Kadane subarray of g1 or g2).
solution:
1. base = sum of a[i] for even i.
2. g1: for i = 0,2,4,...: a[i+1] - a[i]. g2: for i = 1,3,...: a[i] - a[i+1].
3. Kadane max subarray sum on each (allow empty -> 0).
4. Answer base + max gain. Use long long.

name: Longest Simple Cycle
nearest_infosys_question: Q0281 Array Minimization Game
brief: n chains (simple paths of c_i vertices) are linked: chain i's first vertex joins vertex a_i of chain i-1 and its last vertex joins vertex b_i of chain i-1. Find the longest simple cycle length.
key_idea: cur = best path length that closes on chain i's left side; either close directly between a_i and b_i or extend the previous open cycle, minus the a-b segment.
solution:
1. Process chains i=2..n; d=|a_i-b_i|.
2. A cycle whose rightmost chain is i uses c_i-1 inner edges + 2 link edges = c_i+1, plus a path on chain i-1.
3. If i==2 or d==0: cur=c_i+1+d (can't extend through equal attach points).
4. Else cur=c_i+1+max(d, cur_prev-d) (go outward around previous cycle instead of directly).
5. ans=max over all cur; use long long.

name: Color with Occurrences
tags: brute force, data structures, dp, greedy, strings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0462 Largest Number from Array
brief: Text t (|t|<=100) and n<=10 strings; one step colors one occurrence of a string in t. Find the minimum number of steps to color all of t (print the steps) or -1.
key_idea: Interval covering: from the first uncovered position, pick the occurrence starting at or before it that reaches furthest right.
solution:
1. Enumerate all occurrences (start p, string w) by brute-force matching: intervals [p, p+|s_w|-1].
2. covered = 0 (first uncovered index). While covered < |t|:
3. Among occurrences with start <= covered, choose the one with maximum end; if max end < covered -> print -1.
4. Record (w+1, p+1), set covered = end+1. Steps count is minimal by the classic greedy exchange argument.
complexity: O(|t| * n * |s| ) to find occurrences, O(|t|^2 * n) greedy
dry_run:
Own example: t=bababa, s1=ba, s2=aba.
Occurrences: ba@0,2,4; aba@1,3.
covered=0: starts<=0 -> ba@0 end 1 -> covered=2.
covered=2: aba@1 end 3, ba@2 end 3, aba@... choose end 3 -> covered=4; then ba@4 end 5 -> done, 3 steps.

name: Standard Free2play
nearest_infosys_question: Q0281 Array Minimization Game
brief: Standing at height h on a cliff with platforms at heights p1=h > p2 > ... > pn 'out'; a lever at x toggles x and x-1; you may fall at most 2 safely. Each crystal toggles one platform. Find the minimum crystals to reach ground 0 (q queries, h<=1e9, sum n<=2e5).
key_idea: You always arrive at height p[i]+1; if the next out platform p[i+1] equals p[i]-1 you can land on it (fall of 2) and skip both, otherwise spend one crystal.
solution:
1. Append 0 (ground) as p[n].
2. i = 1 (index 0 is the top). While i < n:
3. If p[i]-1 == p[i+1]: you stand at p[i]+1, lever hides p[i], fall 2 onto p[i+1] safely; i += 2.
4. Else: need a crystal (hide p[i] or make p[i]-1 appear); ans++, i += 1.
5. Ground 0 counts as a safe landing, handled by the appended 0.
dry_run:
Own example: h=3, p=[3,1] -> [3,1,0].
i=1: p[1]-1=0 == p[2]=0 -> i=3, stop.
Answer 0 (3 -> lever -> 2 -> lever -> fall 2 to ground).
Own example: h=3, p=[3,2]: [3,2,0]; i=1: 1 != 0 -> ans=1.

name: Color Stripe
nearest_infosys_question: Q0281 Array Minimization Game
brief: Row of n cells (n<=5e5) colored with the first k letters (k>=2); repaint the minimum number of cells so no two neighbors share a color, and print the count and one resulting stripe.
key_idea: k=2: only ABAB.. or BABA.. are valid, pick the closer; k>=3: greedily repaint the second cell of each equal pair to a color different from both neighbours.
solution:
1. If k == 2: count mismatches against pattern starting with 'A' and starting with 'B'; output the smaller and that pattern.
2. If k >= 3: scan i = 1..n-1; if s[i] == s[i-1], set s[i] to a letter c (< 'A'+k) with c != s[i-1] and c != s[i+1] (if exists); count++.
3. Greedy is optimal: in a run of L equal letters you must change floor(L/2), which is exactly what alternate repainting does.
4. (General DP alternative: dp[i][c] = min changes with cell i colored c, O(n k^2) too slow-ish; greedy is enough.)
dry_run:
Sample 1: n=6,k=3, ABBACC.
i=2: B==B -> choose c!=B, c!=A -> C: ABCACC, cnt=1.
i=5: C==C -> c!=C (end) -> A: ABCACA, cnt=2.
Output 2 / ABCACA.

name: Make The Fence Great Again
nearest_infosys_question: Q0319 Pizza with 3N Slices and K Tolerance Tokens
brief: n boards with heights a_i; raising board i by 1 costs b_i. Make all adjacent heights different at minimum cost.
key_idea: Each board never needs to be raised more than 2; dp over (board, raise in {0,1,2}).
solution: 1) dp[i][x] = min cost for boards 1..i with board i raised by x (0..2). 2) dp[0][x]=x*b_0. 3) dp[i][x]=x*b_i + min over y with a_{i-1}+y != a_i+x of dp[i-1][y]. 4) Answer min dp[n-1][x]. 5) long long.

name: Easy Problem
nearest_infosys_question: Q0319 Pizza with 3N Slices and K Tolerance Tokens
brief: String s (n<=1e5) with deletion costs a_i. Delete characters with minimum total cost so that 'hard' is not a subsequence.
key_idea: dp[j] = min cost so far such that the longest matched prefix of 'hard' is exactly j (j=0..3).
solution: 1) dp=[0,INF,INF,INF]. 2) For char c = 'hard'[j]: if j<3, dp[j+1]=min(dp[j+1], dp[j]) (keep c, advance); then dp[j]+=a_i (delete c to stay at j). For j==3 just dp[3]+=a_i. 3) Other chars change nothing. 4) Answer min(dp). 5) long long.

name: Clique Problem
tags: data structures, dp, greedy, implementation, sortings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0488 Machine Cooling and Task Scheduling
brief: n points on a line with coordinate x_i and weight w_i; edge between i and j iff |x_i - x_j| >= w_i + w_j. Find the maximum clique size.
key_idea: Map each point to interval [x-w, x+w]; a clique is exactly a set of pairwise non-overlapping intervals (touching allowed) -> classic activity selection.
solution: 1) Build intervals (L=x-w, R=x+w). 2) Sort by R. 3) last = -INF; for each interval: if L >= last, take it, cnt++, last = R. 4) Print cnt. long long.

name: Logo Turtle
nearest_infosys_question: Q0319 Pizza with 3N Slices and K Tolerance Tokens
brief: Turtle commands F (move 1) and T (turn around); you must make exactly n changes (a command may be changed several times). Maximize final distance from start.
key_idea: Changing a command k times flips it iff k is odd; dp over (command index, changes used, direction) storing max and min position.
solution: 1) mx[j][d], mn[j][d] after processing a prefix with j changes and direction d (+1/-1); start mx[0][+]=mn[0][+]=0. 2) For each command and each extra change count k (0..n-j): effective = cmd flipped if k odd; F: pos += d; T: d = -d. Update max and min. 3) Answer = max(|mx[n][d]|, |mn[n][d]|) over d.
dry_run: Sample FT, n=1: change T to F -> FF -> distance 2.

name: LionAge II
nearest_infosys_question: Q0319 Pizza with 3N Slices and K Tolerance Tokens
brief: Name s (<=100 letters), change at most k letters. Euphony = sum of bonuses c(x,y) over adjacent letter pairs. Maximize euphony.
key_idea: dp[i][j][c] = best euphony of the first i letters using j changes with letter i equal to c.
solution: 1) bonus[26][26] from input (default 0). 2) dp[0][ (c!=s0) ][c] = 0 for all c (if within k). 3) dp[i][j + (c!=s_i)][c] = max over prev letter q of dp[i-1][j][q] + bonus[q][c]. 4) Answer = max over j<=k, c of dp[n-1][j][c]. 5) Use -INF for unreachable.
dry_run: Sample winner, k=4 -> 'looser': lo(13)+oo(8)+os(8)+se(7) = 36.

name: Hot Start Up (easy version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0319 Pizza with 3N Slices and K Tolerance Tokens
brief: Two CPUs; programs a_1..a_n run in order, each on either CPU. Program i costs hot_i if the previous program on that CPU was also i, else cold_i. Minimise total time (sum n, k <= 5000).
key_idea: After step i one CPU surely last ran a_i; the state is only the last program x on the other CPU: dp[x].
solution:
1. dp[0]=0 (0 = nothing yet), with previous program a_0 = 0.
2. For next program c with previous p=a_{i-1}: same-CPU cost c1 = (c==p ? hot_c : cold_c); new_dp[x] = dp[x] + c1 for all x.
3. Or run on the other CPU (last x): new_dp[p] = min over x of dp[x] + (x==c ? hot_c : cold_c).
4. Answer min over dp after all n programs. O(nk) total is fine.
dry_run:
Sample: a=1 2 2, cold=(3,2), hot=(2,1).
Step1 c=1: dp[0]=3.
Step2 c=2 (p=1): dp[0]=3+2=5; other CPU: dp[1]=min(3+cold2)=5.
Step3 c=2 (p=2): same CPU hot 1 -> dp[0]=6, dp[1]=6; answer 6 (matches).

name: Feed Cats
nearest_infosys_question: Q0297 Investment opportunities (non-overlapping range revenue)
brief: m cats, cat i present on steps [l_i, r_i] of n steps. Choose steps to feed so no cat is fed twice; maximise number of cats fed.
key_idea: dp[x] = best using steps <= x. If x is fed, the previous fed step must be before L[x] = min l over cats covering x; gain cnt[x] cats.
solution:
1. cnt[x] = number of cats covering x (difference array).
2. minl[r] = min l over cats ending at r; L[x] = suffix-min of minl over r >= x, then clamp L[x] = min(L[x], x).
3. dp[x] = max(dp[x-1], dp[L[x]-1] + cnt[x]).
4. Answer dp[n].
5. Cats covering x all start >= L[x], so any earlier fed step < L[x] never double-feeds them.
dry_run:
Own example: n=3, cats [1,2],[2,3],[3,3].
cnt=[1,2,2]; L=[1,1,2].
dp1=max(0,dp0+1)=1; dp2=max(1,dp0+2)=2; dp3=max(2,dp1+2)=3.
Answer 3 (feed steps 1 and 3).

name: Hills
nearest_infosys_question: Q0319 Pizza with 3N Slices and K Tolerance Tokens
brief: Hills can only be lowered, at 1 hour per unit. A house needs a hill strictly higher than both neighbours. For each k up to ceil(n/2), find the minimum hours to get k houses. n<=5000.
key_idea: Houses are never adjacent, and only the neighbours of a house get lowered. Use dp[i][j][s] with s=0 (i is not a house and neither is i-1), s=1 (i is a house), s=2 (i is not a house but i-1 is). Roll the i dimension to save memory.
solution:
1. g0 = min(f0, f2).
2. g1[j] = min(f0[j-1] + max(0, a[i-1]-a[i]+1), f2[j-1] + max(0, min(a[i-1], a[i-2]-1) - a[i] + 1)). In the second case, hill i-1 was already lowered to a[i-2]-1.
3. g2 = f1 + max(0, a[i]-a[i-1]+1), which lowers hill i below the house at i-1.
4. Handle i=1 and i=2 boundaries, where neighbours are missing. Output the min over s at i=n for each k.
dry_run:
Sample 1 1 1 1 1:
k=1: a house at hill 1 means lowering hill 2 by 1, cost 1.
k=2,3: houses at 1,3,5 means lowering hills 2 and 4, cost 2.
Output '1 2 2' (matches). The other two samples were also verified.

name: Grouping Increases
nearest_infosys_question: Q0498 Make Equal Elements Adjacent (min adjacent swaps)
brief: Split array a into two subsequences s and t; penalty p(b)=number of adjacent pairs with b_i<b_{i+1}. Minimize p(s)+p(t).
key_idea: Keep the last elements x<=y of the two subsequences; put a on the smaller top that is >= a; if a exceeds both, put it on the smaller top (pay 1).
solution:
1. x=y=INF (empty sequences), x<=y always.
2. If a<=x: x=a (no penalty, keep larger top y free).
3. Else if a<=y: y=a (no penalty).
4. Else (a>y): x=a, penalty++ (replace the smaller top, keep the bigger one).
5. Swap so x<=y after each step. Answer total penalty.

name: Sakurako's Field Trip
nearest_infosys_question: Q0446 Andy's Vacation
brief: Array of topics; you may swap a[i] with a[n-i+1] any number of times. Minimize the number of adjacent equal pairs.
key_idea: Process mirror pairs from outside in; for pair (i, n-1-i) swap if it reduces equalities with already-fixed outer neighbours a[i-1] and a[j+1].
solution:
1. 0-indexed, for i=1..n/2-1, j=n-1-i.
2. before=(a[i]==a[i-1])+(a[j]==a[j+1]); after=(a[j]==a[i-1])+(a[i]==a[j+1]).
3. If after<before swap a[i],a[j].
4. Finally count i with a[i]==a[i+1]. Inner middle pairs are unaffected by swapping (symmetric).
dry_run:
Sample 1: a=1 1 1 2 3, n=5. i=1,j=3: before=(1==1)+(2==3)=1, after=(2==1)+(1==3)=0 -> swap: 1 2 1 1 3.
Count equal adjacent: only (1,1) -> 1. Output 1.

name: Cirno and Number (Easy Version)
tags: binary search, brute force, dp, greedy, implementation
nearest_infosys_question: Q0478 Battery charge to make array strictly increasing
brief: Given a<=1e17 and two allowed digits d1<d2, find the minimum |a-b| over non-negative integers b written only with those digits (no leading zeros).
key_idea: The answer is either 0 (if allowed), the largest b with fewer digits, the smallest b with one more digit, or the predecessor/successor of a among same-length numbers built by 'match a prefix, then deviate down/up, then fill with max/min digit'.
solution:
1. Let A = decimal string of a, L = its length. Candidates go into a list (use __int128 since L+1 = 19 digits can exceed long long).
2. If d1==0 add 0. If L>1 add d2 repeated L-1 times. Add (d1>0?d1:d2) followed by L copies of d1.
3. Same length: for i=0..L: prefix A[0..i-1] must use only allowed digits; if i==L add a. Otherwise for each allowed d (not 0 at i=0 when L>1): if d<A[i] add prefix+d+d2..d2; if d>A[i] add prefix+d+d1..d1. Stop when A[i] is not allowed.
4. Answer = min |a - cand|.
dry_run:
Sample a=3333, d={6,7}:
Shorter: 777 -> diff 2556.
Same length, i=0: 6 > 3 -> 6666 diff 3333; 7 -> 7666.
Longer: 66666. Min = 2556.

name: Array Walk
nearest_infosys_question: Q0876 Max Balanced L/R Substrings after One Adjacent Swap
brief: Start at index 1 with score a_1; make exactly k moves, each right (+a_{x+1}) or left (+a_{x-1}), with at most z left moves and never two lefts in a row. Maximize the score (z <= 5).
key_idea: Fix the number of left moves t <= z. The final position is p = k - 2t; spend all left moves oscillating on the best adjacent pair (i, i+1) with i <= p.
solution:
1. For t = 0..z: p = k - 2t (0-indexed); stop if p < 0.
2. score = (a_0 + ... + a_p) + t * max_{i <= p, i+1 < n} (a_i + a_{i+1}).
3. Track the running prefix sum and the running max pair.
4. Answer = max over t.
complexity: O(n * z) per test, O(n) space

name: Running Miles
nearest_infosys_question: Q0497 Road lamps with dead posts and one generator truck
brief: Sights 1..n with beauties b_i; pick a range [l,r] with at least 3 sights, score = sum of the three largest beauties in it minus (r - l). Maximize.
key_idea: Optimal range has the two chosen outer sights as its endpoints, so maximize (b_i + i) + b_j + (b_k - k) over i<j<k with prefix and suffix maxima.
solution:
1. pre[j] = max_{i<j} (b_i + i).
2. suf[j] = max_{k>j} (b_k - k).
3. Answer = max over middle j (2..n-1) of pre[j] + b_j + suf[j].
4. Using any three indices is fine: their sum is <= the true top-3 sum of that range, and the true top-3 also appears among candidates.

b_i+i: 6 3 7 6 8; b_k-k: 4 -1 1 -2 -2.
j=3 (b=4): pre=6, suf=max(-2,-2)=-2 -> 8.
Other j give <= 8; answer 8 (matches).

name: Permute Digits
nearest_infosys_question: Q0517 Min swaps to maximize product of pair sums
brief: Rearrange the digits of a (up to 1e18) to get the largest number not exceeding b, without leading zeros; an answer is guaranteed.
key_idea: If a is shorter than b, sort digits descending; otherwise fix digits left to right choosing the largest digit that still allows the smallest completion to stay <= b.
solution:
1. If len(a)<len(b): print digits of a sorted descending.
2. Else (equal lengths): res=""; available multiset of digits.
3. For each position, try digits d from 9 down to 0 (available): candidate = res + d + (remaining digits sorted ascending); if candidate <= b (string compare, same length) accept d.
4. Leading zero can't win because a valid answer exists and larger digits are tried first.

name: Shaass and Bookshelf
nearest_infosys_question: Q0232 Knapsack with additional constraints
brief: n<=100 books with thickness t_i in {1,2} and width w_i. Upright books' total thickness must be >= total width of the books lying on top. Minimize total thickness of upright books.
key_idea: Condition sum_t(V) >= W_total - sum_w(V); knapsack dp[T] = max total width of upright books with thickness T.
solution:
1. W = sum of all widths, Tmax = sum of thicknesses (<=200).
2. dp[T] = max sum w over subsets with thickness exactly T (-inf if impossible), dp[0]=0; 0/1 knapsack iterate T downwards.
3. Answer = min T with dp[T] >= 0 and T + dp[T] >= W.
4. Choosing all books always works (T=Tmax).
complexity: O(n * sum t) time, O(sum t) space

name: Cow Program
nearest_infosys_question: Q0381 Graph + DP OA problem
brief: a_2..a_n given; for each a_1=i (1..n-1) run: x=1,y=0; repeat {y+=a_x, x+=a_x; then y+=a_x, x-=a_x} until x<=0 or x>n. Print final y or -1 if infinite.
key_idea: State (x, next step type) for x>=2 has a fixed outcome; memoize y-gain with cycle detection. Returning to x=1 always happens before an add step -> infinite.
solution:
1. After the first step from x=1: x=1+i, y=i, next step is 'subtract'.
2. val[x][d] = total y added from state (x, d) until exit, -1 if infinite: nx = x+a_x (d=0) or x-a_x (d=1); out of range -> a_x; nx==1 -> -1; else a_x + val[nx][1-d] (or -1).
3. Compute iteratively (explicit stack, 4e5 states) with colors; meeting an in-progress state = cycle -> -1.
4. Answer i: val[1+i][1]==-1 ? -1 : i + val[1+i][1]. Use long long.

name: Writing Code
nearest_infosys_question: Q0179 Count subsets with sum X
brief: n programmers, programmer i makes a_i bugs per line. Count plans (v_1..v_n >= 0, sum m) with total bugs <= b, modulo mod.
key_idea: Unbounded knapsack over programmers: dp[lines][bugs] counts plans; process programmers in order to count sequences not permutations.
solution: 1) dp[0][0]=1. 2) For each programmer i: for j=1..m, for k=a_i..b: dp[j][k] = (dp[j][k] + dp[j-1][k-a_i]) % mod (in-place forward = unbounded). 3) Answer = sum_k dp[m][k] % mod. 4) mod may be 1 -> print sum % mod.
dry_run: Sample: a=1,1,1, m=3, b=3. Every plan has 3 bugs <=3, so count = compositions of 3 into 3 parts = C(5,2) = 10.

name: Wooden Fence
nearest_infosys_question: Q0179 Count subsets with sum X
brief: n board types a x b (rotatable unless square). Count sequences forming a fence of total length l where consecutive boards differ in type and each board's length equals the previous board's width; mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: dp[len][type][orientation] = number of fences of total length len ending with that board placed that way; extend with a different type whose length equals the current width.
solution: 1) Orientation o gives (length, width) = (a,b) or (b,a); squares only one orientation. 2) dp[len_i][i][o] = 1 for every first board with length <= l. 3) For len ascending, for each (i,o) with count, for each j != i and orientation o2 with length(j,o2) == width(i,o) and len + length <= l: add. 4) Answer = sum of dp[l][*][*].
dry_run: Sample l=3, boards 1x2, 2x3: fences: [1x2 as length 1, width 2] + [2x3 length 2] = 3 ✓; [2x3 rotated: length 3] alone = 3 ✓. Answer 2.

name: Glass Half Spilled
nearest_infosys_question: Q0307 Powers of 2 and 5 subset product 10^z
brief: n ≤ 100 glasses with capacity a_i and water b_i. Pouring x units loses x/2. For each k, max total water collectable in k glasses.
key_idea: For a chosen set S, water = min(capA(S), (B + b(S))/2); knapsack over (count, total capacity) maximizing b(S).
solution:
1. B = total water. Pouring everything else into S yields b(S) + (B - b(S))/2.
2. dp[k][A] = max b-sum choosing k glasses with total capacity A (0/1 knapsack, iterate k and A downward).
3. Answer_k = max over A of min(A, (B + dp[k][A]) / 2).
4. Print with 10 decimals.
complexity: O(n^2 * sum a) ≈ 1e8 time, O(n * sum a) space

name: Mashmokh and ACM
nearest_infosys_question: Q0226 K-Perfectly Even Arrays
brief: Count sequences of length k with values in [1,n] where each element divides the next (non-decreasing), modulo 1e9+7. n,k<=2000.
key_idea: dp[len][v] = number of good sequences of length len ending in v; push to all multiples of v.
solution:
1. dp[1][v]=1 for all v.
2. For len=1..k-1, for v=1..n, for m=v,2v,..<=n: dp[len+1][m]+=dp[len][v] mod p.
3. Use two rolling arrays.
4. Answer sum dp[k][v].
complexity: O(k * n log n) time, O(n) space
dry_run:
Sample n=3,k=2: dp1=[1,1,1].
v=1 pushes to 1,2,3; v=2 to 2; v=3 to 3.
dp2=[1,2,2] -> sum 5.

name: Mathematical Problem
tags: brute force, dp, greedy, implementation, math, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0478 Battery charge to make array strictly increasing
brief: Digit string s (n<=20); insert exactly n-2 operators (+ or x) between digits (so exactly one adjacent pair forms a 2-digit number). Minimize the expression value.
key_idea: Try each of the n-1 positions for the 2-digit number; with the resulting numbers: any 0 -> answer 0, else add numbers >1 and multiply 1s in (cost 0); all 1s -> 1.
solution:
1. If n==2 print the number (stoi, drops leading zero).
2. For each k in 0..n-2: numbers = digits, with s[k]s[k+1] merged into one 2-digit number.
3. If any number is 0, value=0; else value = sum of numbers >1 (1s are multiplied onto a neighbour); if that sum is 0, value=1.
4. Answer min over k.

name: Increase Subarray Sums
nearest_infosys_question: Q0497 Road lamps with dead posts and one generator truck
brief: Array a (n<=5000) and x; for each k=0..n add x to exactly k distinct positions and report the maximum subarray sum (empty allowed).
key_idea: Precompute best[len] = max sum of a subarray of length len; answer(k) = max over len of best[len] + min(k,len)*x.
solution:
1. Prefix sums; best[0]=0, best[len]=max over starts of sum of length len (O(n^2)).
2. For each k=0..n: ans=max over len of best[len]+min(k,len)*x.
3. Extra +x positions outside the subarray don't hurt (x>=0 but not counted).
4. Print n+1 answers.

name: Cost of a Bracket Sequence
nearest_infosys_question: Q0876 Max Balanced L/R Substrings after One Adjacent Swap
brief: Cost of a bracket string = length of its longest regular subsequence. Delete at most k characters to minimize cost; output a 0/1 deletion mask.
key_idea: Max matched pairs M = min over split p of (#'(' before p + #')' from p on); pick the minimizing p and delete up to k of exactly those characters, each deletion lowers M by 1.
solution:
1. Compute f(p) = opens in s[0..p-1] + closes in s[p..n-1] for p=0..n; choose p* with minimum.
2. Each deletion lowers any matching by at most 1, so M-k (floored at 0) is optimal.
3. Mark for deletion up to k characters that are '(' at index < p* or ')' at index >= p*.
4. Print the mask.
dry_run:

Delete '(' at index 0 -> mask 1000 (remaining '))(' has cost 0).
Matches sample output 1000.

name: Masha and the Garland
tags: data structures, dp, greedy, implementation, math, number theory, strings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0876 Max Balanced L/R Substrings after One Adjacent Swap
brief: Binary string; for each query [l,r,k] decide if the segment can be made alternating using at most k subsegment flips.
key_idea: XOR with an alternating pattern; the segment splits into runs at positions where s_i==s_{i-1}. With R runs, the cheaper target needs floor(R/2) flips.
solution:
1. eq[i]=1 if s_i==s_{i-1} (i>=2); prefix sums P.
2. Query: c = P[r]-P[l] (equal pairs inside the segment), R=c+1.
3. Min flips = R/2 (flip every other run of the XOR-with-pattern string).
4. YES iff R/2 <= k.

Query 1 2 0: c=1, R=2 -> 1>0 NO.
Query 2 4 1: c=1 -> 1<=1 YES.

name: Letter
nearest_infosys_question: Q0087 Delayed Stock Settlement
brief: Given a string of upper/lowercase letters (length <= 1e5), change the case of the fewest letters so all uppercase letters come before all lowercase letters.
key_idea: Try every split point s: cost = lowercase letters in [0,s) + uppercase letters in [s,n); take the minimum.
solution:
1. upTotal = number of uppercase letters; cost at s=0 is upTotal.
2. Sweep s from 0 to n-1: if s[i] is lowercase, lowBefore++; else upAfter--.
3. After each step cost = lowBefore + upAfter; keep minimum.
4. Equivalent DP: dp_up/dp_low state machine.

s=0: 7. s=2 (after PR): 0+5=5. s=6 (after 'PRuvet'): 4+5=9...
s=12 (all upper): 5+0=5.
Minimum 5 -> output 5.

name: Backrooms Hill
tags: constructive algorithms, dp, greedy, sortings, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0475 Minimum steps to empty array
brief: Given a permutation a of 1..n, you may swap a_i and a_{i+2} any number of times. Can a become a hill (strictly increasing then strictly decreasing)?
key_idea: Each value keeps its position parity and can be placed anywhere of that parity. A hill is built by placing n, n-1, ... outward from the peak, so every even-length top set occupies a contiguous block with equal odd/even counts: values (n,n-1), (n-2,n-3), ... must each have different parities.
solution:
1. cls[v] = parity of the position where v currently sits.
2. Values in decreasing order fill a growing contiguous interval; an interval of even length has exactly half odd positions.
3. So for j = 0,2,4,... with j+1 < n: cls[n-j] must differ from cls[n-j-1]; otherwise NO.
4. If all pairs differ, a valid placement always exists -> YES (a leftover single value when n is odd is fine).
dry_run:
Sample [5,3,4,6,2,1]: parities 5o 3e 4o 6e 2o 1e.
Pairs: (6e,5o) ok, (4o,3e) ok, (2o,1e) ok -> YES.
Sample [4,1,3,2,6,5]: (6o,5e) ok, (4o,3o) same -> NO.

name: Boredom
nearest_infosys_question: Q0200 Word Break
brief: Given n numbers (values up to 1e5), repeatedly pick a value v, gain v points, and delete all elements equal to v-1 and v+1 (picking v again is allowed). Maximize total points.
key_idea: Group by value: taking value v means taking all copies (v*cnt[v]) and forbidding v-1, v+1 -> house-robber DP over values.
solution:
1. cnt[v] = frequency.
2. dp[0]=0, dp[1]=cnt[1].
3. dp[v] = max(dp[v-1], dp[v-2] + v*cnt[v]) for v = 2..1e5.
4. Answer dp[maxV]; use long long (up to 1e10).

name: Two Substrings
tags: brute force, dp, greedy, implementation, strings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0472 Maximum number after one segment digit mapping
brief: Given an uppercase string (length <= 1e5), decide whether it contains non-overlapping substrings 'AB' and 'BA' (any order).
key_idea: Take the first occurrence of one pattern and look for the other only from 2 positions after it; try both orders.
solution:
1. i = s.find("AB"); if found and s.find("BA", i+2) != npos -> YES.
2. j = s.find("BA"); if found and s.find("AB", j+2) != npos -> YES.
3. Otherwise NO.
4. Earliest first occurrence is optimal because it leaves the longest suffix for the second.

'BA' first at 0, 'AB' from 2: found at 4 -> YES.
Sample ABA: AB at 0, BA from 2: no; BA at 1, AB from 3: no -> NO.

name: Good String
tags: brute force, dp, greedy, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0511 Longest increasing sequence from array ends (CF 1157C2)
brief: A string is good if its left and right cyclic shifts are equal. Given a digit string (length <= 2e5), erase the minimum number of characters to make it good.
key_idea: Good strings are either one repeated digit or an even-length alternation abab...; try all 100 digit pairs (a,b) and greedily take the longest alternating subsequence.
solution:
1. For each pair (a, b) of digits: walk s, expecting a then b then a ...; take a char when it equals the expected one, flip expectation.
2. If a != b and the taken length is odd, subtract 1.
3. If a == b the count is just the occurrences of a (any length ok).
4. Answer = n - max length.

No pair does better (all digits distinct, single digit length 1).
Answer 5 - 2 = 3.

name: Maximum width
tags: binary search, data structures, dp, greedy, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0489 Lexicographically smallest single swap within distance K
brief: Strings s (n) and t (m), t is a subsequence of s. Choose positions p_1<...<p_m matching t; maximize max(p_{i+1} - p_i).
key_idea: L[i] = earliest position matching t[i] in a leftmost greedy match, R[i] = latest position in a rightmost greedy match; answer = max over i of R[i+1] - L[i].
solution:
1. Greedy from left: j over s, for i = 0..m-1 advance until s[j] == t[i]; L[i] = j.
2. Greedy from right similarly: R[i] = latest valid position.
3. Answer = max_{i<m-1} (R[i+1] - L[i]).
4. Valid because L[0..i] and R[i+1..] can be combined (L[i] < R[i+1]).

name: Did We Get Everything Covered?
tags: constructive algorithms, dp, greedy, shortest paths, strings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0472 Maximum number after one segment digit mapping
brief: Given n, k and a string s over the first k letters, decide whether every length-n string over those letters is a subsequence of s; if not, output one that is not.
key_idea: Greedily cut s into blocks that each contain all k letters; the letter that completes a block is the worst choice for an adversary. If fewer than n blocks, the completing letters + a letter missing from the leftover part form a non-subsequence.
solution:
1. Scan s with a set of seen letters; when its size reaches k, record the current char, count++, clear the set.
2. If count >= n print YES.
3. Else build ans = recorded chars (count of them) + any letter among first k not in the current partial set.
4. Pad with 'a' up to length n. Print NO and ans.
complexity: O(m + n) per test, O(k) space
dry_run:
Sample n=2,k=2,s=abb: 'a','b' -> block done at 'b', count=1; leftover {'b'}.
count 1 < 2 -> ans = 'b' + missing 'a' = 'ba'.
'ba' is not a subsequence of abb -> NO ba (sample prints aa; any valid accepted).

name: Backspace
nearest_infosys_question: Q0511 Longest increasing sequence from array ends (CF 1157C2)
brief: Type string s left to right; for each character either type it or press Backspace (deletes the last typed char). Can the final text be exactly t?
key_idea: Match from the end: if s[i] == t[j] take it; otherwise s[i] is unwanted: press Backspace instead of typing it, which also erases one earlier typed char, so skip two characters of s.
solution:
1. i = |s|-1, j = |t|-1.
2. While i >= 0 and j >= 0: if s[i] == t[j]: i--, j--; else i -= 2.
3. YES iff j < 0 (any leftover prefix of s can be wiped: backspace on empty text does nothing).
4. Greedy from the end is optimal because the last kept char must match t's last char.

s[3]='b'=t[0] -> j=-1 -> YES.
Sample s=ababa,t=bb: 'a'!='b' skip2 -> i=2 'a' skip -> i=0 'a' skip -> NO.

name: The Walkway
tags: brute force, dp, greedy, math, number theory
nearest_infosys_question: Q0876 Max Balanced L/R Substrings after One Adjacent Swap
brief: Benches 1..n, m cookie sellers at given benches. Walking from 1 to n, Petya eats at bench i if a seller is there, or it is his first cookie, or d minutes passed since the last one. Remove exactly one seller to minimize cookies; print the minimum and how many sellers achieve it.
key_idea: Add sentinels s_0 = 1-d and s_{m+1} = n+1. Cookies strictly between consecutive eating points a<b are (b-a-1)/d, so total T = m + sum f(s_i, s_{i+1}); removing seller i changes T by f(s_{i-1},s_{i+1}) - f(s_{i-1},s_i) - f(s_i,s_{i+1}) - 1.
solution:
1. Build s with sentinels 1-d and n+1; f(a,b) = (b-a-1)/d.
2. T = m + sum over i=0..m of f(s_i, s_{i+1}).
3. For each real seller i: val = T - f(s_{i-1},s_i) - f(s_i,s_{i+1}) - 1 + f(s_{i-1},s_{i+1}).
4. Track minimum and count. Use long long.

name: Gas Pipeline
nearest_infosys_question: Q0335 Maximum triplets (equal or consecutive)
brief: Road [0,n] given as binary string (1 = crossroad on that unit interval, needs pipe at height 2). Pipe starts/ends at height 1; pipe costs a per unit, pillars b per unit (height-2 pillars cost 2b). A height change over one interval costs an extra unit of pipe. Minimise total cost.
key_idea: dp[i][h] = min cost up to point i with the pipe at height h (1 or 2); crossroad intervals force height 2 at both ends.
solution:
1. dp[0][1] = b (pillar of height 1), dp[0][2] = INF.
2. For interval i (char s[i]): if s[i]=='1': dp[i+1][2] = dp[i][2] + a + 2b, dp[i+1][1] = INF.
3. Else: dp[i+1][1] = min(dp[i][1] + a + b, dp[i][2] + 2a + b); dp[i+1][2] = min(dp[i][2] + a + 2b, dp[i][1] + 2a + 2b).
4. Answer dp[n][1]. Use long long (answer up to ~1e14).

name: Dima and a Bad XOR
tags: bitmasks, brute force, constructive algorithms, dp
nearest_infosys_question: Q0132 Maximum XOR of Two Numbers
brief: n x m matrix (values <= 1023). Pick one entry per row so the XOR is > 0; print TAK and the chosen columns, or NIE.
key_idea: Take column 1 in every row. If the XOR is already nonzero, done. Otherwise changing a single row to any entry different from its first entry makes the XOR nonzero; if no such entry exists, answer NIE.
solution:
1. X = XOR of a[i][0] over all rows; choice = all 1s.
2. If X != 0 print TAK and choices.
3. Else find any (i, j) with a[i][j] != a[i][0]; set choice[i] = j+1 (new XOR = a[i][0] ^ a[i][j] != 0).
4. If none exists print NIE.

Row 2 col 3 has 10 != 7 -> choose it: 7 ^ 10 = 13 > 0.
Output TAK / 1 3. Sample 1 (all zeros) -> NIE.

name: Building a Fence
nearest_infosys_question: Q0281 Array Minimization Game
brief: Fence of n sections of height k; section i's base must be in [h_i, h_i+k-1] (exactly h_1 and h_n at the ends) and neighbors must overlap by at least 1. Decide if possible.
key_idea: Track the interval [lo,hi] of feasible base heights section by section.
solution:
1. lo=hi=h_1.
2. For i=2..n: lo=max(lo-(k-1), h_i), hi=min(hi+(k-1), h_i+k-1) (overlap means |base_i - base_{i-1}| <= k-1).
3. If lo>hi -> NO.
4. At the end require lo<=h_n<=hi (the last section must sit exactly on h_n).
dry_run:
Sample 3: k=2, h=3 0 2.
lo=hi=3.
i=2: lo=max(2,0)=2, hi=min(4,1)=1 -> lo>hi -> NO (matches).
Sample 2: k=3, h=0 2: lo=max(-2,2)=2, hi=min(2,4)=2; h_n=2 in [2,2] -> YES.

name: Bear and Blocks
tags: binary search, data structures, dp, math
nearest_infosys_question: Q0267 Hero Duel Intensity
brief: n towers of heights h_i; each operation removes all boundary blocks (a block missing any of its 4 neighbours, floor counts). Count operations until everything is destroyed.
key_idea: Tower i disappears after min(h_i, L_i, R_i) steps where L_i = min(h_i, L_{i-1}+1) and R_i symmetric; answer is the max of min(L_i, R_i).
solution:
1. Left pass: L[0] = 1 (outside is empty), L[i] = min(h[i], L[i-1] + 1).
2. Right pass: R[n-1] = 1, R[i] = min(h[i], R[i+1] + 1).
3. Tower i dies at time min(L[i], R[i]) (its top erodes 1 per step, and neighbours dying spreads 1 per step).
4. Answer = max_i min(L[i], R[i]).

name: Kavi on Pairing Duty
nearest_infosys_question: Q0238 Count Good Arrays (divisibility chain)
brief: Pair 2n points on a line into n segments so that any two segments are either nested or of equal length. Count such pairings mod 998244353.
key_idea: dp[n] = (sum of dp[1..n-1]) + d(n): either the outermost segment wraps a smaller good pairing, or all equal-length blocks tile, counted by divisors of n.
solution:
1. Case A: the longest segments are nested outer layers around a good pairing of k<n pairs in the middle; each k in 1..n-1 gives dp[k] ways -> dp[1]+...+dp[n-1].
2. Case B: all segments that are not nested have equal length, forcing a periodic structure: number = number of divisors d(n).
3. Sieve d(1..n) in O(n log n).
4. dp[n] = prefixSum(n-1) + d(n), mod p.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

name: Fake Plastic Trees
tags: dfs and similar, dp, greedy, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0907 Tree partitioning problem
brief: Rooted tree, all values start at 0; one operation adds a non-decreasing (root to v) sequence along a root-to-v path. Each vertex must end in [l_v, r_v]. Minimize operations.
key_idea: Bottom-up: a vertex can receive at most the sum of what its children received; if that sum < l_v, spend a new operation and set its value to r_v, else cap at r_v.
solution:
1. Process vertices in decreasing index order (p_i < i ensures children before parents).
2. s[v] = sum of final values passed up from children.
3. If s[v] < l_v: ans++, val[v]=r_v (a new path ending at v, maximal value helps ancestors).
4. Else val[v] = min(s[v], r_v). Add val[v] to s[parent].
5. Use long long sums.

name: Scammy Game Ad
nearest_infosys_question: Q0281 Array Minimization Game
brief: n<=30 pairs of gates (left lane, right lane), each '+ a' or 'x a' (a in {2,3}). Each lane starts with 1 person; newly created people can be put in either lane. Maximize final total.
key_idea: Go backwards computing the final 'worth' of one person in each lane; every newly created person goes to the lane with larger worth.
solution: 1) vL = vR = 1 after the last pair. 2) For pairs i from n down to 1: best = max(vL, vR) (worth of a new person placed after this gate). 3) Left gate '+a': add a*best to a constant total; 'x a': vL = vL + (a-1)*best. Same for right with vR. 4) Answer = vL + vR + accumulated constants. 5) long long (3^30*1000 fits).

name: Dima and Hares
nearest_infosys_question: Q0335 Maximum triplets (equal or consecutive)
brief: n hares in a row fed one by one; hare i gives a_i, b_i or c_i joy if 0, 1 or 2 of its neighbors were fed before it. Maximize total joy.
key_idea: Only the relative order of adjacent hares matters: dp over hares with state = whether hare i+1 is fed before hare i.
solution: 1) f[i][t]: best for hares 1..i where t=1 means hare i+1 is fed before hare i. 2) Previous state p = f[i-1][p]: p=1 means hare i was fed before hare i-1, so the left neighbor counts as fed-before iff p==0. 3) fedBefore = (left fed before ? 1:0) + t; joy = a/b/c by fedBefore. f[i][t] = max over p of f[i-1][p] + joy. 4) Hare 1 has no left neighbor (treat as not fed before); hare n only t=0. 5) Answer f[n][0].

name: Cost of Tree
nearest_infosys_question: Q0907 Tree partitioning problem
brief: Tree rooted at 1 with values a_i. For each r, consider the subtree of r with cost sum a_u * dist(r,u); you may detach one subtree (u != r) and reattach it under any remaining node. Output the max cost for every r.
key_idea: Moving sub(u) under v gains S_u*(dep(v)+1-dep(u)); for the term using depths outside child c's subtree, u=c is always best, so best(r) = max over children c of max(best(c), S_c*(O_c - dep(r))), O_c = max(dep r, max height of other children).
solution: 1) Root at 1: dep, subtree sum S, W = sum a_u*dep(u) over subtree, H = max absolute depth in subtree. 2) base(r) = W(r) - dep(r)*S(r). 3) For r, take top-2 H among children; for child c: O_c = max(dep(r), best H among other children). 4) best(r) = max over c of max(best(c), S_c*(O_c - dep(r))); leaf best = 0. 5) Answer(r) = base(r) + best(r). long long.

name: Choosing Balls
nearest_infosys_question: Q0319 Pizza with 3N Slices and K Tolerance Tokens
brief: n<=1e5 balls with colour c_i and value v_i; for each of q<=500 queries (a,b) pick a subsequence: a ball scores a*v if same colour as the previous chosen ball, else b*v. Max total (empty = 0).
key_idea: Per query O(n) DP: best[col] = best sequence ending in colour col; keep the top two colours to get 'best ending in a different colour' in O(1).
solution:
1. best[] = -inf; top1/top2 = (colour, value), initially the empty sequence (value 0).
2. Ball i: cur = max(best[c]+a*v, bestOtherColour + b*v), where bestOther = top1 if its colour != c else top2.
3. If cur > best[c]: update best[c] and the top-two list (watch for c already being top1/top2).
4. Answer max(0, top1 value).

Ball2 (colour 2, -2) scores 0, then ball4 (colour 2, 4) scores +4 -> 4.

name: Flag 2
nearest_infosys_question: Q0319 Pizza with 3N Slices and K Tolerance Tokens
brief: n x m flag (<=500x500) of letters. Repaint the fewest cells so that each row uses at most two colours and no two side-adjacent cells share a colour; print the flag.
key_idea: A valid row alternates two distinct colours (a,b); dp over rows with state (a,b) where consecutive rows need a != a' and b != b'.
solution:
1. Row cost for (a,b) = (#even cells != a) + (#odd cells != b) from per-parity letter counts (676 pairs).
2. dp[row][(a,b)] = cost + min dp[row-1][(c,d)] with c!=a, d!=b.

4. Keep parents and rebuild the flag.

2. dp[0]=1, dp[1]=1.

name: String Equality
nearest_infosys_question: Q0469 Remove two distinct or one element
brief: Strings a,b of length n and k. Operations on a: swap adjacent chars; or turn k equal letters c (c!='z') into c+1. Can a become b?
key_idea: Swaps make order irrelevant; process letters a..y with counts: excess of letter c must be divisible by k and is carried to c+1; deficit means No.
solution:

2. For c=0..24: if ca[c]<cb[c] -> No; d=ca[c]-cb[c]; if d%k -> No; ca[c+1]+=d.

4. Print Yes otherwise.

2. Count '(' after f.

name: We Be Flipping (Hard Version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0449 Oil Tank / Gas Station
brief: Array of n nonzero integers. An operation picks an index i with a_i > 0 and negates the prefix a_1..a_i. Using at most n operations, maximize the final sum and print the operations.
key_idea: Let m be the largest index ever operated: it is hit exactly once, must be originally positive and ends negative; everything after m is untouched and everything before m can be made positive. So answer = max(original sum, max over a_m>0 of sum|a_1..a_{m-1}| - a_m + sum a_{m+1..n}).
solution:
1. Option 0: do nothing (sum of a).
2. For each m with a_m > 0: value = prefAbs(m-1) - a_m + suffixSum(m+1). Take the best m (use long long).
3. Construct for best m: scan i = m-1 down to 1 keeping parity p of ops done; current sign of a_i is sign(a_i) flipped if p=1; if it is positive, operate at i (it becomes negative, p ^= 1). Now a_1..a_{m-1} are all negative.
4. Operate at m (a_m is untouched, still positive): prefix becomes all positive, a_m negative.
5. Total ops <= m <= n. If doing nothing is best print 0.

name: Prime Destruction
tags: brute force, dp, math, number theory
nearest_infosys_question: Q0275 DP + GCD OA problem
brief: Multiset of n values (each <= n). One operation: pick x>1 and prime p | x, replace x with p copies of x/p. Find the minimum operations so all elements are <= k.
key_idea: Elements are independent: cost(x) = 0 if x <= k, else min over prime p | x of 1 + p*cost(x/p). Compute bottom-up for x = 1..n with a smallest-prime-factor sieve.
solution:
1. Sieve spf up to 2e5 once.
2. Per test: for x = 1..n: if x <= k cost=0; else iterate distinct primes p of x (via spf) and take min(1 + p*cost[x/p]).
3. Answer = sum of cost[a_i] (long long; can reach ~4e10).
4. x/p < x so cost[x/p] is already computed.
complexity: O(n log n) per test, O(n) space

name: Palindrome Basis
tags: brute force, dp, math, number theory
nearest_infosys_question: Q0179 Count subsets with sum X
brief: Count the multisets of positive palindromic integers that sum to n (n <= 4e4, t <= 1e4 queries), modulo 1e9+7.
key_idea: Unbounded-knapsack counting over the ~500 palindromes below 4e4 (coins loop outer so order does not matter); precompute once for all queries.
solution:
1. Collect all palindromes p <= 40000.
2. dp[0] = 1.
3. For each p (outer loop), for s = p..40000: dp[s] = (dp[s] + dp[s-p]) % MOD.
4. Answer each query with dp[n].
complexity: O(P * N) ≈ 2e7 precompute, O(1) per query, O(N) space

name: Air Conditioner
tags: dp, greedy, implementation, sortings, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0478 Battery charge to make array strictly increasing
brief: An AC starts at temperature m at time 0 and can change temperature by -1, 0 or +1 per minute. n customers (sorted by time t_i) each want the temperature in [l_i, h_i] at time t_i. Can all be satisfied?
key_idea: Track the interval [lo, hi] of reachable temperatures: after dt minutes it widens by dt on each side, then intersect with the customer's range.
solution:
1. lo = hi = m, prev = 0.
2. For each customer: dt = t - prev; lo -= dt; hi += dt.
3. lo = max(lo, l), hi = min(hi, h). If lo > hi -> NO.
4. prev = t. If all pass -> YES. Use long long.

name: Line Empire
tags: binary search, brute force, dp, greedy, implementation, math
nearest_infosys_question: Q0876 Max Balanced L/R Substrings after One Adjacent Swap
brief: Capital at 0, kingdoms at x_1<...<x_n. Moving the capital to a conquered kingdom costs a per unit; conquering costs b per unit distance from the capital (no unconquered kingdom in between). Minimize total cost.
key_idea: Optimal strategy: conquer kingdoms in order, moving the capital along up to some final kingdom i, then conquer the rest from x_i. Cost(i) = (a+b)*x_i + b*(sum_{j>i} x_j - (n-i)*x_i); try all i (x_0 = 0).
solution:
1. suffix = sum of all x.
2. For i = 0..n (x_0 = 0): when i >= 1 subtract x_i from suffix.
3. cost = (a+b)*x_i + b*(suffix - (n-i)*x_i).
4. Answer = min cost. Use long long (values up to ~2e5 * 1e8 * 1e5 needs care: ~2e18 fits).

name: Nikita and string
nearest_infosys_question: Q0176 Min cost to reach step N with forced 1-step after big jump
brief: String of a/b (length<=5000); delete characters to get the longest string of the form a*b*a*. Output that length.
key_idea: Three states: in first a-block, in b-block, in last a-block; each char either counts in the current state or a later state.
solution:
1. d0,d1,d2 = best length so far ending in state 0 (a*), 1 (a*b*), 2 (a*b*a*).
2. For char c: d2 = max(d0,d1,d2) + (c=='a'); d1 = max(d0,d1) + (c=='b'); d0 = d0 + (c=='a') (update d2, then d1, then d0 so old values are used).
3. Answer max(d0,d1,d2).
4. Edge: all one letter works automatically.

name: Make Nonzero Sum (hard version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0486 Flip or Swap (alternating binary string)
brief: Array of -1/0/1 (n<=2e5). Split into contiguous segments; each segment contributes its alternating sum a_l - a_{l+1} + ...; make the total 0. Print any partition or -1.
key_idea: Number of nonzeros must be even; pair consecutive nonzeros and make each pair cancel, using a preceding zero to flip the sign of the second if needed.
solution:
1. Collect indices of nonzero elements; if count is odd print -1.
2. Pair them (i,j) in order; everything not in a pair's special segments is a singleton segment (zeros add 0).
3. If a_i != a_j: [i,i] and [j,j] as singletons -> a_i + a_j = 0.
4. If a_i == a_j and j==i+1: segment [i,j] -> a_i - a_j = 0.
5. If a_i == a_j and j>i+1: [i,i], singletons, then [j-1,j] (a_{j-1}=0) -> a_i + (0 - a_j) = 0.

name: Add One
nearest_infosys_question: Q0245 Balanced Bracket Sequence Count with wildcards
brief: Each operation replaces every digit d of n by the decimal form of d+1 (9 -> 10). After m operations (m <= 2e5, t <= 2e5 queries), output the length of the number mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Digits evolve independently. L[x] = length obtained from digit 0 after x operations: L[x] = 1 for x < 10, else L[x-9] + L[x-10] (0 becomes 10 after 10 steps: a '1' (= '0' one step ahead) and a '0'). Digit d after m ops has length L[m+d].
solution:
1. Precompute L[0..2e5+10]: L[x] = 1 for x < 10; L[x] = (L[x-9] + L[x-10]) mod p.
2. For each query read n as a string and m.
3. Answer = sum over digits d of L[m + d] mod p.
complexity: O(M + total digits) time, O(M) space

name: Good Key, Bad Key
tags: bitmasks, brute force, dp, greedy, math
nearest_infosys_question: Q0281 Array Minimization Game
brief: Open n chests in order. A good key costs k; a bad key is free but halves (floor) the coins in this and every later chest. Maximize final coins.
key_idea: It's optimal to use good keys first and then only bad keys (swapping a bad key before a good key never hurts). After ~31 halvings everything is 0, so for each split i compute the tail in O(31).
solution:
1. Prefix sums P of a.
2. For i = 0..n (good keys on the first i chests): val = P[i] - i*k.
3. Tail: for j = i..min(n-1, i+31): val += a[j] >> (j - i + 1).
4. Answer = max val (long long; can be negative contributions from k, but i=0 gives >= 0).

name: Jellyfish and Mex
nearest_infosys_question: Q0200 Word Break
brief: Repeat n times: delete one element of the array, then add the MEX of the remaining array to m. Minimize final m.
key_idea: Lower the MEX in jumps: dp[j]=min over i>j of dp[i]+(cnt[j]-1)*i+j, starting from dp[mex]=0.
solution:
1. Let M = current MEX (<= n); only values < M matter, cnt[v] their counts.
2. Optimal play: pick a value j<M, delete all its copies; while deleting the first cnt[j]-1 copies MEX stays i, last deletion makes MEX j.
3. dp[M]=0; for j from M-1 down to 0: dp[j]=min over i in (j, M] of dp[i]+(cnt[j]-1)*i+j.
4. Once MEX is 0 every later add is 0; answer dp[0]. Use long long.

name: Sums on Segments
tags: binary search, brute force, data structures, dp, greedy, math
nearest_infosys_question: Q0497 Road lamps with dead posts and one generator truck
brief: Array where all elements are +-1 except at most one arbitrary x. Output all distinct subarray sums (empty subarray gives 0) in ascending order.
key_idea: With +-1 steps, achievable sums form a contiguous range; split into segments avoiding x (range containing 0) and segments containing x (another range), output their union.
solution:
1. Let k be the index of x (if none, only case A).
2. Case A (segments not containing k): Kadane max and min subarray sum resetting at k; range [mn,mx] (both include 0 via empty).
3. Case B (segments containing k): with prefix sums P, max = max P[r] (r>=k) - min P[l-1] (l<=k); min = min P[r] - max P[l-1]. Range [lo,hi] is contiguous.
4. Output union of the two integer ranges sorted without duplicates (merge if they overlap).

name: Kevin and Puzzle
nearest_infosys_question: Q0245 Balanced Bracket Sequence Count with wildcards
brief: n people in a line; person i claims a_i liars to their left. Honest people tell the truth, liars may say anything, and no two liars are adjacent. Count possible honest/liar assignments mod 998244353.
key_idea: dp[i]=#configs of first i with person i honest: from i-1 honest (a_i==a_{i-1}) or i-1 liar and i-2 honest (a_i==a_{i-2}+1).
solution:
1. Add virtual honest person 0 with a_0=0, dp[0]=1.
2. If person i is honest, the liar count left of i is exact; if i-1 is liar then i-2 is honest and liars-left-of-i = a_{i-2}+1.
3. dp[i] = (a_i==a_{i-1} ? dp[i-1] : 0) + (i>=2 && a_i==a_{i-2}+1 ? dp[i-2] : 0).
4. Answer = dp[n] + dp[n-1] (last person honest, or liar with n-1 honest), mod p.

name: Functions again
nearest_infosys_question: Q0497 Road lamps with dead posts and one generator truck
brief: For array a, f(l,r)=sum_{i=l}^{r-1} |a_i-a_{i+1}|*(-1)^(i-l) (formula from the statement image; matches both samples). Find max f over l<r.
key_idea: Build d_i=|a_i-a_{i+1}| with alternating signs; run Kadane twice (starting at even and at odd positions).
solution:
1. d_i=|a_i-a_{i+1}| for i=1..n-1.
2. Sequence b_i = d_i*(-1)^i and c_i = -b_i; a segment starting at even l uses one sign pattern, odd l the other.
3. Kadane on both: max subarray of b starting at even index and of c starting at odd index. Simpler: dp over states (best ending at i with + sign / - sign): pos[i]=max(d_i, neg[i-1]+d_i), neg[i]=pos[i-1]-d_i.
4. Answer = max pos[i] (segment must start with + sign). Use long long.

pos1=3,neg1=-inf; pos2=max(2,-inf)=2,neg2=3-2=1; pos3=max(1,1+1)=2,neg3=2-1=1; pos4=max(2,1+2)=3.

name: Long Path
nearest_infosys_question: Q0497 Road lamps with dead posts and one generator truck
brief: Rooms 1..n+1; in room i an odd cross count sends you to p_i (<= i), an even count to i+1; each entry paints a cross. Count portal moves from room 1 to room n+1, mod 1e9+7 (n<=1000).
key_idea: dp[i] = moves from first entering room i until first reaching i+1 = 2 + sum_{j=p_i}^{i-1} dp[j], since going back to p_i resets all rooms p_i..i-1 to the 'first entry' state.
solution:
1. First entry to i (odd) -> jump to p_i (1 move); you must then re-walk rooms p_i..i-1, each taking dp[j] moves to advance (their counts are now even-parity-equivalent to first visit).
2. Back in i (even) -> go to i+1 (1 move). So dp[i] = 2 + sum_{j=p_i}^{i-1} dp[j].
3. Keep prefix sums pre[i] mod M; dp[i] = (2 + pre[i-1] - pre[p_i-1] + M) % M.
4. Answer = pre[n].

name: Alyona and Spreadsheet
tags: binary search, data structures, dp, greedy, implementation, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0497 Road lamps with dead posts and one generator truck
brief: n x m table (n*m<=1e5) and k queries [l,r]: answer Yes if some column is non-decreasing on rows l..r.
key_idea: up[i][j] = first row of the non-decreasing run in column j ending at row i; best[i] = min_j up[i][j]; query Yes iff best[r] <= l.
solution:
1. For each column j: up[1][j]=1; up[i][j] = (a[i][j] >= a[i-1][j]) ? up[i-1][j] : i.
2. best[i] = min over columns of up[i][j] (keep only a rolling previous row to save memory).
3. Query (l,r): print Yes if best[r] <= l else No.
4. Store the table as flat vector since n*m <= 1e5 but either dimension can be large.
complexity: O(n*m + k) time, O(n + m) extra space

Query (2,5): every column breaks somewhere in rows 2..5; best[5]=4 > 2 -> No.
Query (4,5): best[5]=4 <= 4 -> Yes.

name: Anton and Making Potions
tags: binary search, dp, greedy, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0113 Heroes vs Villains (remove from front)
brief: Make n potions at x seconds each with mana budget s; optionally use one type-1 spell (cost b_i, time becomes a_i) and one type-2 spell (cost d_i, instantly c_i potions; c and d non-decreasing). Minimize total time.
key_idea: Try every type-1 choice (including none); with the remaining mana, binary search the largest affordable type-2 spell, which gives the most potions because c is non-decreasing.
solution:
1. Add the option 'no type-1 spell': a = x, b = 0.
2. For each type-1 option with b_i <= s: rem = s - b_i.

name: Zero-One (Hard Version)

brief: Given a permutation p of 1..n, build any tree on vertices 1..n such that for every edge (u,v) with u<v, u appears before v in p, or report No.
key_idea: Attach every non-prefix-minimum element to the current prefix minimum; then link consecutive prefix-min groups with edge (prefix min before the boundary, suffix max after it), which must satisfy min < max.
solution:
1. Scan p keeping curMin. If p[i] < curMin, it starts a new group (record boundary i); else add edge (curMin, p[i]).
2. Compute suffix max sm[i] = max(p[i..n-1]).
3. For each boundary b>0 with prefix min m = min(p[0..b-1]): if m > sm[b] answer No (no edge can cross this cut); else add edge (m, sm[b]).
4. Each group gets exactly one edge to a later group -> n-1 edges, connected, acyclic.
5. Necessity: any cut needs some earlier u < later v, i.e. prefix min < suffix max.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0518 Minimum balls to reset box strengths
brief: Trampolines with strengths S_i; landing on i sends you to i+S_i and decreases S_i by 1 (min 1). Each pass starts anywhere and ends when you leave. Minimize passes to make all strengths 1.
key_idea: Go left to right: visits already arriving at i (cnt[i]) are free; start max(0,S_i-1-cnt[i]) new passes; the jumps from i land on i+2..i+S_i once each, surplus visits spill to i+1.

1. cnt[i] = number of times earlier passes land on i.
2. need = max(0, S_i-1-cnt[i]); ans += need; total visits v = cnt[i]+need.

4. The remaining v-(S_i-1) visits (strength 1) go to i+1: cnt[i+1] += v-(S_i-1).
5. Direct loop is O(n^2) (n<=5000) or use a difference array.

brief: n rectangles a_i x b_i; coloring one cell is one operation; each fully colored row or column of a rectangle gives 1 point. Minimum operations to get at least k points (k<=100), or -1.
key_idea: Within one rectangle, fully coloring r rows and q columns costs r*a + q*b - r*q cells for r+q points; take the min per point count, then a min-cost knapsack over rectangles.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0297 Investment opportunities (non-overlapping range revenue)
brief: n x m table (<=1500). Pick prefix lengths c_i>=1 per row with c1>c2<c3>c4<...; maximise the sum of chosen cells.
key_idea: dp[i][c] = best with row i using prefix c; the alternating constraint is a prefix/suffix max over the previous row.
solution:
1. pre = row prefix sums. Row 1: dp[c]=pre[c].
2. Row i even (1-indexed): need c < previous -> dp'[c] = pre[c] + max_{c'>c} dp[c'] (suffix max).
3. Row i odd: need c > previous -> prefix max over c'<c.
4. Unreachable = -inf; answer max dp of last row. Use long long.

3. Each position with digit d receives exactly d ones, so sum is n.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0876 Max Balanced L/R Substrings after One Adjacent Swap
brief: Given permutation p, decide if a tree on 1..n exists where for every edge (u<v), u appears before v in p.
key_idea: Allowed edges are pairs (u<v, u before v); the graph is disconnected iff some split has prefix minimum > suffix maximum.
solution:
1. Compute suffix maximum sufmax[i] of p[i..n-1].
2. Sweep prefix minimum pm over p[0..i].
3. If for some i<n-1, pm > sufmax[i+1]: no edge crosses the cut -> No.
4. Otherwise the allowed-edge graph is connected -> Yes (a spanning tree exists).

brief: Columns of cubes a_i; gravity pushes every cube right at its height. You may first decrease one a_i by 1. Maximize the number of cubes whose column changes.
key_idea: A cube at height h stays iff all columns to its right reach height h, so stationary cubes = sum of suffix minima; moved = sum(a) - sum(sufmin). Decreasing a_i (a suffix minimum) lowers every sufmin(j)==a_i for j<=i.
solution:
1. sufmin[j]=min(a_j..a_n); base = sum a - sum sufmin.
2. Decreasing a_i by 1 costs 1 cube total but reduces sufmin(j) by 1 for each j<=i with sufmin(j)==a_i.
3. That count is nonzero only if a_i==sufmin(i); then it equals i - first(j with sufmin(j)==a_i) + 1 (contiguous block since sufmin is non-decreasing).
4. gain = max(0, max count - 1). Answer base + gain (long long).

name: Mortal Kombat Tower
nearest_infosys_question: Q0176 Min cost to reach step N with forced 1-step after big jump
brief: n bosses, each easy(0) or hard(1). Friend and you alternate turns (friend first), each turn killing 1 or 2 next bosses. Each hard boss killed by the friend costs a skip point. Minimize skip points.
key_idea: dp[i][who] = min skips to kill bosses i..n-1 when it is who's turn; each turn take 1 or 2 bosses.
solution:
1. dp[n][*] = 0 (also allow overshoot: taking 2 needs i+2 <= n).
2. Friend's turn: dp[i][0] = min(a_i + dp[i+1][1], a_i + a_{i+1} + dp[i+2][1]).
3. Your turn: dp[i][1] = min(dp[i+1][0], dp[i+2][0]).
4. Answer dp[0][0]. Fill i from n-1 down.

name: Maximize the Root
tags: binary search, dfs and similar, dp, greedy, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0907 Tree partitioning problem
brief: Rooted tree (root 1) with values a_i >= 0. Operation on a vertex v with children: a_v += 1 and every other vertex in v's subtree -= 1; values must stay non-negative. Maximize a_1.
key_idea: Compute f(v) = the largest value m such that every vertex in v's subtree can be kept >= m when the parent pulls; leaf: a_v; internal: m = min child f; if a_v >= m then f = m else f = (a_v + m) / 2. Root answer = a_1 + min child f.
solution:
1. Build children lists from parents; get BFS order from root and process in reverse.
2. Leaf: f = a_v.
3. Internal non-root: m = min f(child); f = a_v >= m ? m : (a_v + m) / 2 (raise a_v by operating on v, which lowers the subtree equally).
4. Root: answer = a_1 + min f(child).
5. Use long long. (Binary search on answer also works.)

key_idea: All pieces must share the prefix's own ratio; the answer for prefix i is the number of earlier prefixes (including itself) with the same reduced ratio (d/g, k/g).
solution:

2. g = gcd(d, k); key = (d/g, k/g).
3. cnt[key]++ and output cnt[key].
4. Each earlier prefix with the same ratio is a valid cut point, and they are exactly the cut points.
