key_idea: Take the k smallest; the largest m go on day 1, the next m on day 2, ... Hence x_k = x_{k-m} + (sum of the k smallest).
solution:
1. Sort a ascending; S_k = prefix sum.
2. x_k = S_k + (k > m ? x_{k-m} : 0).
3. Reason: moving from k-m to k pushes every previously eaten sweet one day later (adds S_{k-m}) and adds the m new ones on day 1; total = S_k + x_{k-m}.

complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

name: Flower Boy
tags: binary search, dp, greedy, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0495 Min sum of AP-index selection after one swap
brief: Flowers a_1..a_n; collect m flowers left to right where the i-th collected has beauty >= b_i. You may insert at most one flower of any beauty k anywhere. Output the minimum k (0 if no insertion needed, -1 if impossible).
key_idea: Greedy prefix match L[j] = earliest end index after matching b_0..b_{j-1}, greedy suffix match R[j] = latest start index for matching b_j..b_{m-1}. Inserting a flower for b_j works iff L[j] <= R[j+1]; answer = min such b_j.
solution:
1. L[0]=0; greedily scan a matching b in order: L[j+1] = index after the match of b_j (INF if not matched).
2. If L[m] <= n (all matched) print 0.
3. R[m] = n; scan from the right matching b backwards: R[j] = index of the match for b_j (or -INF).
4. For each j: if L[j] <= R[j+1] candidate b_j.
5. Print min candidate or -1.
complexity: O(n + m) per test, O(n + m) space

name: Maximum Subarray Sum
tags: binary search, constructive algorithms, dp, implementation, math
nearest_infosys_question: Q0481 Temperature Cooling
brief: Array of length n where s marks known (1) / unknown (0) entries; fill unknowns (|a_i|<=1e18) so the maximum subarray sum is exactly k (k<=1e12), or say No.
key_idea: Make every unknown a huge negative wall except one unknown p, then set a[p] = k - (best sum ending at p-1) - (best sum starting at p+1).
solution:
1. If no unknowns: run Kadane; answer Yes iff max == k.
2. Otherwise set all unknowns to -1e13 and run Kadane; if max > k answer No (known parts already exceed k).
3. Pick the first unknown p. L = max(0, best suffix sum ending at p-1), R = max(0, best prefix sum starting at p+1) (walls at -1e13 stop them naturally).
4. Set a[p] = k - L - R; the best subarray through p is exactly k, others are <= k.
5. Print Yes and the array.

name: Skyscrapers (easy version)

brief: n<=1000 plots with limits m_i; choose heights 1<=a_i<=m_i forming a unimodal (non-decreasing then non-increasing) sequence with maximum total. Print the heights.

brief: Insert the fewest spaces into a lowercase word (<=3000) so no piece has 3+ consecutive consonants that are not all the same letter. Print the result.

name: Sequence and Swaps
nearest_infosys_question: Q0478 Battery charge to make array strictly increasing
brief: Sequence a and number x (all <= 500). Operation: choose i with a_i > x and swap a_i with x. Find the minimum operations to make a non-decreasing, or -1.
key_idea: Scan left to right: stop as soon as the array is sorted; otherwise any a_i > x must be swapped now (later swaps only increase x, so skipping it would leave a too-large early element).
solution:

2. If a[i] > x: swap(a[i], x), ops++.

name: Kachina's Favorite Binary String
nearest_infosys_question: Q0876 Max Balanced L/R Substrings after One Adjacent Swap
brief: Interactive: recover a hidden binary string of length n using at most n queries '? l r' returning the number of '01' subsequences in s[l..r], or print IMPOSSIBLE if it cannot be determined.
key_idea: Query f(1,i) for all i; the first i with f>0 fixes the prefix (ones then exactly f zeros then a 1), and afterwards s[i]=1 iff f(1,i) increased.
solution:
1. Ask f[i] = f(1,i) for i = 2..n (n-1 queries); f[1]=0.
2. If all f are 0 the string is 1..10..0 shaped and indistinguishable -> '! IMPOSSIBLE'.
3. Let k be the first index with f[k] > 0, v = f[k]: s[k]='1', s[k-v..k-1]='0', s[1..k-v-1]='1' (those leading ones create no '01' with each other).

5. Flush after every print.

name: Running with Obstacles
nearest_infosys_question: Q0064 Insert Interval
brief: Athlete goes from 0 to m; before each jump he must run at least s obstacle-free meters, a jump is at most d and must land on a free point strictly past obstacles (never beyond m). Output alternating RUN X / JUMP Y moves or IMPOSSIBLE.
key_idea: Sort obstacles; take off right before an obstacle, and keep swallowing following obstacles into the same jump while the gap between them leaves fewer than s free meters for a run (a[j+1]-a[j]-2 < s); land right after the last swallowed obstacle.
solution:
1. Sort a; pos = 0.
2. At obstacle a[i]: run length = a[i]-1-pos must be >= s, else IMPOSSIBLE. Emit RUN.
3. Extend j from i while j+1<n and a[j+1]-a[j]-2 < s (cannot run s between them).
4. Jump from a[i]-1 to a[j]+1: length must be <= d, else IMPOSSIBLE. Emit JUMP; pos = a[j]+1; i = j+1.
5. After all obstacles, if pos < m emit RUN m-pos. Landing as early as possible is optimal (maximizes the next run).
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

brief: Given a string s (|s|<=1e6), find the longest substring that is a prefix, a suffix, and also occurs strictly inside s (not as the prefix or suffix occurrence); otherwise print 'Just a legend'.
key_idea: Use the KMP prefix function: candidate L = pi[n-1]; it works if some pi[i] >= L for i < n-1, otherwise fall back to pi[L-1].
solution:
1. Compute prefix function pi.
2. L = pi[n-1]; if L == 0 -> 'Just a legend'.
3. If max(pi[0..n-2]) >= L, the prefix of length L occurs ending at some middle position -> answer s[0..L-1].
4. Else L2 = pi[L-1]; if L2 > 0 answer s[0..L2-1] (it occurs at the end of the length-L prefix, which is a middle position), else 'Just a legend'.

name: Consecutive Subsequence
nearest_infosys_question: Q0258 LIS with index-varying difference K
brief: Array of n<=2e5 values; find the longest subsequence whose values are x, x+1, ..., x+k-1 (consecutive increasing integers) and print k and its indices.
key_idea: dp[v] = longest such subsequence ending with value v so far = dp[v-1] + 1, stored in a hash map; reconstruct by scanning for x, x+1, ... greedily.
solution:
1. For each a_i in order: dp[a_i] = dp[a_i - 1] + 1 (missing key = 0).
2. Track the value v* with maximal dp, length k.
3. Start value x = v* - k + 1; scan the array left to right, taking index i whenever a_i == x, then x++ until k indices are taken.
4. Greedy earliest picks are always valid because the dp proved the chain exists.
complexity: O(n log n) with map (O(n) expected with unordered_map), O(n) space

name: Sleeping Schedule
nearest_infosys_question: Q0319 Pizza with 3N Slices and K Tolerance Tokens
brief: Day has h hours; Vova sleeps n times, the i-th sleep starting a_i or a_i - 1 hours after waking (each sleep lasts exactly h). A start is good if its time mod h is in [l, r]. Maximize good starts.
key_idea: dp[i][t] = max good starts after i sleeps when the current time mod h is t; each step branches to (t + a_i) % h or (t + a_i - 1) % h.
solution:
1. dp[0][0] = 0, all others = -INF.
2. For each sleep i and each reachable t: for each nt in {(t + a_i) % h, (t + a_i - 1) % h}: dp[i+1][nt] = max(dp[i+1][nt], dp[i][t] + (l <= nt <= r)).
3. Waking time mod h equals sleep start mod h (a sleep lasts h), so t is both.
4. Answer = max_t dp[n][t]. Use two rolling rows.

brief: n monsters in a row with health a_i. Choose a start and power x; the spell hits monsters expanding outward in an adversarial order, the k-th hit dealing x-(k-1). Minimize x that kills all monsters for the best start.
key_idea: For start i, monster j<i can be hit last at step n-j+1 and j>i at step j, so x >= a_j + (n-j) on the left and a_j + (j-1) on the right.

2. dp[n]=1 (any letter fails); dp[i] = 1 + min over c of (nxt[i][c]==n ? 0 : dp[nxt[i][c]+1]).

brief: f(n) = min total pairwise comparisons in a tournament splitting n girls into equal groups of x each round (group of x costs x(x-1)/2). Compute sum_{i=l}^{r} t^(i-l) * f(i) mod 1e9+7, r <= 5e6.

brief: Stack of n mobs with healths h_i (mob 1 at bottom). Each attack deals 1 damage to any mob; when a mob dies, mobs above fall and the new bottom takes fall damage equal to the number of mobs it was standing on (cascading). Minimum attacks to kill all.

name: Adjusting Drones
tags: binary search, brute force, data structures, dp, dsu, greedy, implementation, sortings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0366 Kruskal's minimum spanning tree
brief: Drone energies a_i; while some value appears more than k times, every drone whose value appeared at an earlier index gets +1. Count the number of such operations.
key_idea: Per value, one unit stays and the extra c-1 units move right together at speed 1, dropping one unit at each empty position. Groups never merge; groups starting further right fill empty cells first. Value v finishes at time p - v where p is the (c_v - k)-th cell its group fills.
solution:
1. cnt[v] for each value; positions up to ~3n are enough (allocate 4n+5).
2. DSU 'next empty position' nxt(x); occupied = originally nonempty values.
3. Process values v from largest to smallest; its group has g = cnt[v]-1 free units; repeatedly take p = nxt(v+1), mark filled (union with p+1), g times, recording the (cnt[v]-k)-th filled p if cnt[v] > k.
4. T_v = p - v; answer = max T_v (0 if all counts <= k).
5. Correctness: per-group pile size is non-increasing, and the pile at time t is <= k exactly from the (cnt-k)-th fill onward.

name: Programming Competition
tags: dfs and similar, dp, graph matchings, greedy, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0912 Min vertex removals so every tree component has < K vertices
brief: In a rooted tree, pair up vertices into teams of two where neither vertex is an ancestor of the other. Each vertex can be in at most one team. Maximize the number of teams.
key_idea: Below v there are tot vertices, and M of them are in the largest child subtree. If M <= tot-M, everything below v can be paired, giving tot/2. Otherwise pair the other tot-M vertices with the big subtree and recurse into the big child for the rest.
solution:
1. Get a BFS order. Process it in reverse to compute subtree sizes, since p_i can be larger than i.
2. tot = sz[v]-1. M = size of the biggest child c.
3. If M <= tot-M: dp[v]=tot/2.
4. Else dp[v] = (tot-M) + min(dp[c], (M-(tot-M))/2). The answer is dp[1].
dry_run:

name: Cake Trial
nearest_infosys_question: Q0335 Maximum triplets (equal or consecutive)
brief: A string over T/F/N: replace each N with T or F to maximise min over contiguous segments [l,r] (or empty) of the mistakes from guessing exactly [l,r] as F. n<=500, sum n^3 <= 500^3.
key_idea: min mistakes = #F - max(0, max subarray sum) with F=+1 and T=-1. Fix the cap M on the max subarray and run Kadane-state DP maximising #F.
solution:
1. Guessing segment S costs #F outside S + #T inside S = totalF - (#F - #T in S). So the best guess gives totalF - maxSub, where maxSub >= 0.
2. For each M in 0..n, run DP over positions with state c = current Kadane suffix value (0..M) and value = max #F so far.
3. Choosing F: c->c+1 (only if <= M), #F+1. Choosing T: c->max(0,c-1).
4. The candidate is max_c dp[c] - M. The answer is the max over M (the true maxSub is among the M tried, and other M only underestimate).

key_idea: Each array's chosen segment is in state before/inside/after. Run a 3x3 joint state DP, trying both swap options at each index.

1. dp[p][q] = best sum so far, with p,q in {0 before, 1 inside, 2 after} for arrays A and B. Start dp[0][0]=0.
2. At index i, for swap in {0,1}: x and y are the values going to A and B. Move to p2>=p and q2>=q, adding x if p2==1 and y if q2==1.
3. The answer is the max over all states (an empty segment is allowed, so >= 0).

nearest_infosys_question: Q0176 Min cost to reach step N with forced 1-step after big jump
brief: Building with n<=15 floors, each a corridor of m rooms between a left and right staircase (grid n x (m+2)); start at the ground floor's left stairs, must turn off all lights floor by floor (moving one cell or one floor costs 1). Minimize total time; no need to return.
key_idea: dpL/dpR = min time to finish floors below and stand at the left/right staircase; on each floor either go to the farthest light and come back, or cross the whole corridor.

brief: Cities 0..n on a line with directed roads (L/R); after every move all roads flip. For each starting city, output the maximum number of distinct cities visited.

solution:

2. left[i] = 0 if s[i-1]!='L'; else 1 + (i>=2 && s[i-2]=='R' ? 1 + left[i-2] : 0).
3. right[i] = 0 if s[i]!='R'; else 1 + (i+1<n && s[i+1]=='L' ? 1 + right[i+2] : 0).
4. You can go one way then come back and go the other, so answer = 1 + left[i] + right[i].

nearest_infosys_question: Q0138 Maximum Xor-Sum in range [0,K]

key_idea: k odd: k copies of n. k even: k-2 copies of n (cancel) plus a pair (a,b), a^b=n, a,b<=n, maximising a+b = n + 2*(a&b).

2. New i: nd[0] = max(a_i, dp[m-1] + a_i) - k (start new or extend into new block).

name: Quest
nearest_infosys_question: Q0294 Kevin and Paul array game
brief: Place tasks (time t_i, interest q_i) as leaves of a binary question tree where depth + t_i <= T on every path. Maximise the total interest. n<=1000, T<=100.
key_idea: A task can sit at depth at most T - t_i. Sweep depths bottom-up: at each level sort the values and merge adjacent pairs (largest with second largest...) into parent nodes. At the root take the best single value.
solution:
1. Put each task in bucket d = T - t_i (its deepest allowed level).
2. For d = T down to 1: add bucket d to the current list and sort descending. Pair them up: (v0+v1), (v2+v3), ...; an odd last one goes up alone. These become nodes at level d-1.
3. At level 0 add bucket 0. Only one node fits at the root, so the answer is the max of the list.
4. Pairing the largest values together is optimal: two leaves share a parent.
complexity: O(T * n log n) time, O(n) space

name: To Become Max

nearest_infosys_question: Q0499 Rugged Terrain (strictly descending slope)
brief: Array a (n <= 1000). Operation: choose i < n with a_i <= a_{i+1} and increase a_i by 1. With at most k operations maximize max(a).
key_idea: Fix the index i that becomes the maximum X. It needs a_{i+1} >= X-1, a_{i+2} >= X-2, ... until some original a_{i+j} >= X-j already; cost = sum of (X-j - a_{i+j}) over the raised ones. Feasibility is monotone in X: binary search per i.

1. For each i: binary search X in [a_i, a_i + k].
2. check(i, X): cost = 0; for j = 0..: if i+j == n -> infeasible; need = X - j; if a[i+j] >= need -> feasible if cost <= k; else cost += need - a[i+j].
3. Track the best feasible X over all i (also the original max).
4. Use long long for costs.

name: Omkar and Bed Wars

key_idea: Valid iff no run of 3+ equal letters (circularly); a maximal run of length L needs L/3 changes.

2. BFS each component assigning color[v]=color[u]^w; a conflict -> -1.
3. Count cnt0, cnt1 in the component; we can flip the whole component, so add max(cnt0,cnt1).
4. Isolated vertices count as imposters (max(1,0)=1).

Sample 1: 1-2 imposter (diff), 2-3 crewmate (same).
Colors: 1=0, 2=1, 3=1 -> sides {1} and {2,3}.
Max 2 imposters (matches).

name: Problem with Random Tests
nearest_infosys_question: Q0472 Maximum number after one segment digit mapping
brief: Binary string s (random in real tests); choose two substrings, read them as binary numbers, and maximize their bitwise OR; print it in binary.
key_idea: One substring is s from its first '1' to the end; the other is the same string shifted right by k, where k ranges only up to the position of the first '0' (expected tiny on random data).
solution:
1. Strip leading zeros: t = s from the first '1'; if no '1' print 0.
2. z = index of the first '0' in t; if none, print t.
3. For each shift k=1..z: candidate[i] = t[i] OR (i>=k ? t[i-k] : 0); keep the lexicographically largest (same length).
4. Shift k fills the first zero with a 1 from the run of leading ones; random data keeps z small so O(n*z).
complexity: O(n * z) time (z ~ small on random input), O(n) space

name: TediousLee
nearest_infosys_question: Q0329 Ordered coin change count with large target
brief: Rooted Dead Bush of level n is built recursively; choose vertex-disjoint claws (center + 3 child leaves) to color yellow. Max yellow vertices for level n (<= 2e6), mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: A level-n RDB is a root whose children are one level-(n-1) and two level-(n-2) RDBs; take their answers, and the root's claw can be added exactly when n % 3 == 0.
solution: 1) dp[1]=dp[2]=0. 2) dp[n] = dp[n-1] + 2*dp[n-2] + (n%3==0 ? 4 : 0) mod p. 3) Precompute up to 2e6, answer queries.
complexity: O(max n) precomputation, O(1) per query

name: Beautiful Array
tags: brute force, data structures, divide and conquer, dp, greedy
nearest_infosys_question: Q0335 Maximum triplets (equal or consecutive)
brief: Array a and integer x (|x|<=100). Optionally multiply one contiguous subarray by x; maximize the maximum subarray sum (empty allowed).
key_idea: Kadane with 3 phases: before the multiplied segment, inside it, after it.
solution: 1) d0,d1,d2 = best sum of a subarray ending at i in phase 0/1/2 (fresh start allowed). 2) n0 = max(d0,0) + a; n1 = max(d0,d1,0) + a*x; n2 = max(d1,d2,0) + a. 3) ans = max(ans, n0, n1, n2), starting ans = 0. 4) long long (|a*x| <= 1e11).
dry_run: Sample x=-2, a=-3 8 -2 1 -6: take 8 normally then multiply [-2,1,-6] -> 8+4-2+12 = 22.

name: Smithing Skill
tags: brute force, data structures, dp, greedy, math, sortings, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0281 Array Minimization Game
brief: n weapon classes (forge costs a_i ingots, melting returns b_i < a_i), m metal stocks c_j. Each forge and each melt gives 1 experience. Maximize experience.
key_idea: Always forge+melt the weapon with the smallest net loss a_i - b_i among those affordable; precompute best[x] and dp[x] for x <= 1e6, and jump large stocks down in one step.
solution: 1) A = max a (<= 1e6). best[x] = min (a_i - b_i) over a_i <= x (prefix min over a). 2) dp[x] = (best[x] < INF) ? 2 + dp[x - best[x]] : 0 for x = 1..A. 3) For each c_j: if c_j > A: k = ceil((c_j - A)/best[A]); exp += 2k; c_j -= k*best[A]. Then exp += dp[c_j]. 4) Sum over metals (long long).
dry_run: Sample: total 12 experience over metals 10, 4, 7 (e.g. class 1 with loss 1 used repeatedly on metal 10).

name: Marble Council
nearest_infosys_question: Q0278 Machine subset with stability < position
brief: Partition multiset a into non-empty parts, take one mode from each part into multiset s. Count distinct s modulo 998244353 (sum n <= 5000).
key_idea: s uses set S of values with multiplicities 1..c_v each; feasible iff every unchosen value u has c_u <= sum of c_v over S. Count by knapsack over sums, sorted by count.
solution:
1. Let c_v = frequency of value v; a choice of S contributes prod_{v in S} c_v (m_v from 1..c_v parts with mode v).
2. Unchosen u can be spread over the parts, each holding at most its mode count; total capacity = sum_{v in S} c_v. So need max unchosen c_u <= sum_S c.
3. Sort counts ascending. Case all chosen: prod of all c. Case u is the largest unchosen (all later values chosen, suffix sum T, suffix product Q): add Q * sum_{s >= c_u - T} dp[s], where dp = weighted subset-sum knapsack over earlier values (weight c_v when taken).
4. Then add u to dp: dp'[s+c_u] += dp[s]*c_u. Sums are bounded by n.
complexity: O(n^2) time worst case, O(n) space
dry_run:
Sample 1 2 2: counts sorted [1(c=1), 2(c=2)].
All chosen: 1*2=2.
u=value1 (c=1): T=2>=1 -> Q=2 * dp total(1) = 2.
u=value2 (c=2): T=0, need s>=2 from dp{0:1,1:1} -> 0.
Total 4 (matches).

name: Speedbreaker
tags: binary search, data structures, dp, greedy, implementation, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0518 Minimum balls to reset box strengths
brief: There are n cities in a row with deadlines a_i. Start by conquering one city at time 1, then each step conquer a city adjacent to the conquered block. Count the start cities from which every city i is conquered by time a_i.
key_idea: A good start s must have |i-s|+1 <= a_i for every i, so s lies in the intersection of the intervals [i-a_i+1, i+a_i-1]. Then either every s in that intersection wins or none does. The check: for each t, the cities with deadline <= t must span at most t positions.
solution:
1. L = max(i-a_i+1), R = min(i+a_i-1). If L>R, the answer is 0.
2. For each t from 1 to n, take lo_t, hi_t = the min and max index with a_i <= t (use running min/max over sorted deadlines).
3. If hi_t-lo_t+1 > t for some t, the answer is 0.
4. Otherwise the answer is R-L+1.
dry_run:
Sample 1, a=6 3 3 3 5 5:
The intervals are i=1:[-4,6], i=2:[0,4], i=3:[1,5], i=4:[2,6], i=5:[1,9], i=6:[2,10], so L=2 and R=4.
Check t=3: cities 2..4 span 3 <= 3, fine. t=5: cities 2..6 span 5 <= 5, fine.
Answer 4-2+1=3 (matches).

name: Decoding Genome
nearest_infosys_question: Q0329 Ordered coin change count with large target
brief: Count the strings of length n (up to 1e15) over m<=52 letters that avoid k forbidden ordered adjacent pairs, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: The transition dp_{len+1}[c] = sum of dp_len[d] over allowed pairs (d,c) is linear. So raise the m x m allowed matrix to the power n-1 and sum all its entries.
solution:
1. A[i][j]=1 unless the pair (i,j) is forbidden. 'a'-'z' map to 0..25 and 'A'-'Z' map to 26..51.
2. R = A^(n-1) by fast exponentiation.
3. The answer is the sum of all entries of R (n=1 gives m).
4. Reduce mod p after every multiply-add.
dry_run:
Sample n=3, m=3, with ab and ba forbidden. A has 7 ones.
A^2: the row sums of A are a:2, b:2, c:3. The total of A^2 = sum over j of (column sum of j) * (row sum of j) = 2*2 + 2*2 + 3*3 = 17.
Output 17 (matches).

name: Odd-Even Subsequence
tags: binary search, dp, dsu, greedy, implementation
nearest_infosys_question: Q0115 Make all elements non-positive (subtract A from one, B from rest)
brief: Choose a subsequence of size k from a (n<=2e5); cost = min(max at odd positions, max at even positions). Minimise cost.
key_idea: Answer <= X iff we can build a length-k subsequence where all odd-position (or all even-position) elements are <= X; greedy check.
solution:
1. Binary search X over values.
2. check(X, parity): scan a; if the next position to fill has the restricted parity, take a[i] only if a[i]<=X; otherwise take a[i] freely.
3. Feasible if built length >= k for parity odd or even.
4. Smallest feasible X is the answer.
complexity: O(n log V) time, O(n) space
dry_run:
a=5 3 50 2 4 5, k=4, X=3, odd restricted: 5 skip, 3 take(pos1), 50 take(pos2), 2 take(pos3), 4 take(pos4) -> 4 >= k.
X=2 fails both ways -> answer 3.

name: Keep the Average High
nearest_infosys_question: Q0281 Array Minimization Game
brief: Select max elements of a (n<=5e4) so that every contiguous run of >=2 selected elements has average >= x.
key_idea: Subtract x; then it suffices that all selected windows of length 2 and 3 have sum >= 0 (longer ones split into those). Greedily select left to right.
solution:
1. b_i = a_i - x.
2. Scan i: select i unless (i-1 selected and b_i+b_{i-1}<0) or (i-1,i-2 selected and b_i+b_{i-1}+b_{i-2}<0).
3. Skipping the current element (rather than an earlier one) is optimal by exchange argument.
4. Count selected.

name: Accommodation
nearest_infosys_question: Q0281 Array Minimization Game
brief: n floors x m windows (m%4==0, nm<=5e5). Each floor is split into m/4 two-window apartments (adjacent) and m/2 single-window ones; an apartment is occupied if any window is lit. Min and max total occupied.
key_idea: Occupied = ones - (#two-room apartments covering '11'); min: greedily grab disjoint '11' pairs (cap m/4); max: greedily grab disjoint non-'11' pairs, the shortfall must be '11'.
solution:
1. Per floor ones = count of '1'.
2. p11 = greedy count of disjoint adjacent '11' pairs; min += ones - min(m/4, p11).
3. pn = greedy count of disjoint pairs that are not '11'; max += ones - max(0, m/4 - pn).
4. Leftover two-room apartments can always be placed elsewhere.
dry_run:
Floor 1011 (m=4, one 2-room): ones=3.
min: '11' at 2-3 -> 2. max: pair '10' -> 3.
Summing all floors gives 7 10.

name: Moving Chips
nearest_infosys_question: Q0335 Maximum triplets (equal or consecutive)
brief: 2 x n board with chips '*'. A move shifts a chip to an adjacent cell, capturing a chip there. Minimum moves to leave exactly one chip.
key_idea: Sweep columns left to right keeping all chips merged into one chip; dp[row] = cost to have that single chip at (row, current column).
solution:
1. Trim to columns l..r containing chips.
2. Init dp0 = (row2 at l has chip), dp1 = (row1 at l has chip) (one vertical move to merge column l).
3. For column j: n0 = min(dp0 + 1 + [row2 chip at j], dp1 + 2); n1 = min(dp1 + 1 + [row1 chip at j], dp0 + 2).
4. (+1 move right; +1 extra to absorb the other row's chip; switching rows costs 2 total.)
5. Answer min(dp0, dp1) at column r.
dry_run:
Sample 4: rows '**.*', '**..'.
col0: dp=[1,1]; col1 (both chips): [min(3,3),3]=[3,3].
col2 empty: [4,4]; col3 (row1 chip): dp0=min(5,6)=5, dp1=min(6,6)=6.
Answer 5 (matches).

name: Number Transformation
nearest_infosys_question: Q0275 DP + GCD OA problem
brief: Turn a into b (b<=a<=1e18) using: subtract 1, or subtract (v mod x) for any 2<=x<=k (k<=15). Minimum steps.
key_idea: L = lcm(2..k) <= 360360; no move ever jumps past a multiple of L, so solve inside one block with a DP and multiply the cost of crossing a whole block.
solution:
1. g(hi,lo): DP over residues from hi down to lo: from v go to v-1 or v - v%x (if >= lo).
2. Same block (a/L == b/L): answer g(a%L, b%L).
3. Else: g(a%L, 0) + (qa-qb-1) * (1 + g(L-1, 0)) + 1 + g(L-1, b%L) (the +1 is the step from a multiple of L to L-1 below).

name: Yet another 2D Walking
nearest_infosys_question: Q0296 Hotel customers minimum unhappiness (Chef Monocarp)
brief: Visit n points in increasing order of level max(x,y), finishing each level before the next, starting from (0,0). Minimise the total Manhattan distance walked. n<=2e5.
key_idea: Each level's points lie on an L-shaped border. Sort them along it; you must enter at one end and leave at the other, so the DP only needs 2 states per level.
solution:
1. Group points by level L=max(x,y). Sort each group by (x ascending, y descending), which walks along the L shape.
2. Let a=first and b=last point of the group, and w=dist(a,b) (the cost of covering the whole level).
3. State d0/d1 = best cost ending at the previous level's a or b (start: both are (0,0) with cost 0).
4. To end at a you must enter at b: n0 = min(d0+dist(e0,b), d1+dist(e1,b)) + w. Ending at b is symmetric.
5. The answer is min(d0,d1) after the last level. Use long long.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

name: Longest Array Deconstruction
tags: data structures, divide and conquer, dp, sortings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0230 Maximum gates taken (2D DP like LIS)
brief: Remove any elements from array a (n<=2e5) to maximise the number of positions with a_i = i after shifting.
key_idea: Element i can land on position a_i iff a_i <= i (remove i-a_i elements before it). Chosen elements need strictly increasing a and non-decreasing d=i-a_i: sort by d, then take the LIS on a.
solution:
1. Keep only the indices with a_i <= i, and set d_i = i - a_i (the number of removals needed before it).
2. Two kept elements i<j are compatible iff a_i < a_j and d_i <= d_j (removals only accumulate).
3. Sort by (d asc, a asc) and find the strictly increasing LIS of a with lower_bound.
4. The LIS length is the answer.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
dry_run:
Sample 2: [4,2,3,1]. Valid (d,a): (0,2), (0,3), (3,1).
Sorted, a = 2,3,1: the LIS is 2,3.
Answer 2.

name: Birds
nearest_infosys_question: Q0307 Powers of 2 and 5 subset product 10^z
brief: n <= 1000 trees, nest i has c_i birds (sum c <= 1e4) costing cost_i mana each; every bird raises capacity by B; moving to the next tree restores X mana up to capacity. Start with W mana/capacity. Maximize birds summoned.
key_idea: Swap value and state: dp[j] = maximum mana left after summoning j birds total (capacity is then W + B*j).
solution:
1. dp[0] = W, others -1 (impossible).
2. At tree i: nd[j+t] = max(dp[j] - t*cost_i) for t = 0..c_i while mana stays >= 0.
3. Move: nd[j] = min(nd[j] + X, W + B*j).
4. Answer = largest j with dp[j] >= 0. Total work <= (sum c)^2.
complexity: O((sum c)^2) time worst case, O(sum c) space
dry_run:
Sample 1: W=12, B=0, X=4, c=3,4, cost=4,2.
Tree1: j=0..3 -> mana 12,8,4,0; move -> 12,12,8,4.
Tree2: from j=2 (8 mana) take 4 birds -> j=6, mana 0.
Answer 6 (matches).

name: Qpwoeirut And The City
nearest_infosys_question: Q0481 Temperature Cooling
brief: Buildings h_1..h_n; building i (not first/last) is cool if strictly taller than both neighbours. Add floors (only increase) to maximize the number of cool buildings using minimum total floors; output that minimum.
key_idea: Max cool count is (n-1)/2 with no two adjacent; for odd n positions are fixed (1,3,5..), for even n pick a split: odd indices before, even indices after, via prefix/suffix sums.
solution:
1. 0-indexed cost(i)=max(0, max(h[i-1],h[i+1])+1-h[i]) for 1<=i<=n-2.
2. Odd n: answer = cost(1)+cost(3)+...+cost(n-2).
3. Even n: k=(n-2)/2; for j=0..k use first j odd indices 1,3,..,2j-1 and remaining even indices 2j+2,...,n-2.
4. Compute with running prefix of odd costs and suffix of even costs; take min. Use long long.

name: Approximating a Constant Range
nearest_infosys_question: Q0540 Count equal pairs within distance k
brief: Sequence with |a_{i+1}-a_i|<=1; find the longest contiguous range whose max-min <= 1.
key_idea: Sliding window with value counts; since neighbours differ by <=1, the window is valid iff it contains at most 2 distinct values.
solution:
1. cnt[value] array, distinct=0, l=0.
2. For r: add a[r] (distinct++ if cnt becomes 1).
3. While distinct>2: remove a[l++].
4. best=max(best,r-l+1). (General alternative: multiset max-min check.)

name: Vasya and String
tags: binary search, dp, strings, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0945 Smallest subarray with K good pairs
brief: String of 'a'/'b' of length n (<= 1e5); you may change at most k characters. Maximize the length of the longest block of equal letters.
key_idea: For each target letter c, find the longest window containing at most k letters different from c (sliding window).
solution:
1. For c in {'a','b'}: l = 0, bad = 0.
2. For r = 0..n-1: if s[r] != c, bad++.
3. While bad > k: if s[l] != c, bad--; l++.
4. best = max(best, r-l+1).
5. Answer best over both letters.

Sample n=8,k=1, aabaabaa, c='a': window grows to [0..4] 'aabaa' (1 b) len 5.
At r=5 ('b') bad=2 -> shrink l to 3: 'aab' len 3; r=7: 'aabaa' len 5.
c='b' gives at most 2 -> answer 5.

name: Add Zeros
tags: brute force, data structures, dfs and similar, dp, graphs, greedy
nearest_infosys_question: Q0381 Graph + DP OA problem
brief: Array a (n <= 3e5, a_i <= 1e12). Operation: choose 1 < i <= |a| with a_i = |a| + 1 - i, then append i-1 zeros. Maximize the final length.
key_idea: Index i (original, since zeros never qualify) is usable exactly when the current length is u_i = a_i + i - 1, and moves the length to u_i + i - 1. Build a graph on lengths and find the largest length reachable from n.
solution:
1. For each i in 2..n: u = a_i + i - 1, v = u + i - 1; add edge u -> v (map<long long, vector>).
2. BFS/DFS from length n with a visited set.
3. Answer = max visited length.
4. Appended zeros never satisfy a_i = |a|+1-i >= 1... (they are 0), so only original indices matter.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

Sample a=2 4 6 2 5 (n=5): edges i2: 5->6, i3: 8->10, i4: 5->8, i5: 9->13.
From 5: reach 6, 8; from 8 reach 10.

name: Multiplicity
tags: data structures, dp, implementation, math, number theory
nearest_infosys_question: Q0300 Count arrays with gcd conditions on neighbours
brief: Count non-empty subsequences b of a (by index set) where b_i is divisible by i for every position i, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: dp[j] = number of good subsequences of length j; a_i can extend at position d for each divisor d of a_i (d<=n), updated in decreasing d.
solution:
1. dp[0]=1.
2. For each a_i, list its divisors d<=n (trial division up to sqrt).
3. Process divisors in decreasing order: dp[d] += dp[d-1] (decreasing like 0/1 knapsack so a_i is used once).
4. Answer = sum dp[1..n] mod p.

a=2: divisors {2,1}: dp2+=dp1 -> 1; dp1+=dp0 -> 2.

name: Gambling
nearest_infosys_question: Q0200 Word Break
brief: Known die outcomes x_1..x_n. Pick a value a and a range [l,r]; money doubles when x_i==a and halves otherwise, starting at 1. Output a, l, r maximizing the final money.
key_idea: Maximize (#matches - #misses); for each value run Kadane over its occurrence positions, where a gap of g non-matching rounds costs g.
solution:
1. Group indices by value (map value -> positions).
2. For value v with positions p_0<p_1<...: cur score ending at p_j = max(1 (restart at p_j), cur + 1 - (p_j - p_{j-1} - 1)).
3. Track the start index when restarting; update best (score, v, l, r).
4. Segment endpoints are always at occurrences of a, so this covers all optimal answers.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
dry_run:
Sample 1: 4 4 3 4 4, value 4 positions 1,2,4,5.
cur: p1 ->1; p2 -> 2; p4 -> 2+1-1=2; p5 -> 3 (start 1).
Value 3 gives 1. Best: 4 1 5 (matches).

name: Lazy Narek
nearest_infosys_question: Q0319 Pizza with 3N Slices and K Tolerance Tokens
brief: n strings of length m; choose a subsequence of strings and concatenate. Narek scans for n,a,r,e,k in order, +5 per complete sequence; ChatGPT gets +1 per n/a/r/e/k letter not used in a completed sequence. Maximize difference.
key_idea: Count every narek letter as -1 upfront; each completed sequence adds +10. DP over strings with state = next letter index (0..4).
solution: 1) dp[j] = best value with next expected letter 'narek'[j]; dp[0]=0, others -INF. 2) For each string and each start state j: simulate scanning: each narek letter gives -1; if it equals the expected letter advance, and after 'k' add +10 and reset to 0. Get end state j2 and delta. 3) ndp[j2] = max(ndp[j2], dp[j]+delta); ndp also keeps dp (skip string). 4) Answer = max_j dp[j] (unfinished letters already counted -1).
dry_run: Sample 'narek': from j=0: -5 letters, completes once +10 -> delta 5, state 0. Answer 5. Sample 'nare': -4, state 4 -> dp[4]=-4; best is 0.

name: Colored Balls
nearest_infosys_question: Q0278 Machine subset with stability < position
brief: n colors with a_i balls (sum <= 5000). Groups hold at most 2 balls of different colors. Value of a color subset = min groups. Sum values over all 2^n subsets mod 998244353.
key_idea: Value of a subset = max(max a, ceil(sum/2)); sort ascending, fix the max element, and count subsets of smaller ones by sum with a knapsack.
solution: 1) Sort a ascending. 2) dp[s] = number of subsets of processed elements with sum s; dp[0]=1. 3) For element a_i (as the maximum): add sum over s of dp[s] * max(a_i, ceil((s+a_i)/2)). 4) Then insert a_i: for s descending dp[s+a_i]+=dp[s]. 5) Empty set contributes 0.

name: Shooting Gallery
nearest_infosys_question: Q0289 Common arrival order over K days
brief: n targets with (x, y, appearance time t, hit probability p). The sight moves at speed 1 and starts anywhere. Maximize expected number of hits.
key_idea: Sort by time; dp[i] = p_i + max dp[j] over earlier targets reachable in time (distance <= t_i - t_j); like LIS on a DAG.
solution: 1) Sort targets by t. 2) dp[i] = p_i + max(0, max over j<i with (t_i - t_j)^2 >= (x_i-x_j)^2 + (y_i-y_j)^2 of dp[j]). 3) Use long long for squared comparisons. 4) Answer = max dp; print with 10 decimals.

name: Two Paths
tags: dfs and similar, dp, graphs, shortest paths, trees, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0394 Longest trip after moving one road (tree diameter)
brief: In a tree with n<=200 nodes, choose two paths that share no vertex so that the product of their lengths (counted in edges) is as large as possible.
key_idea: Two vertex-disjoint paths can always be separated by removing some edge. So try deleting each edge and multiply the diameters of the two components.
solution:
1. For each edge (u,v), treat it as deleted.
2. Diameter of u's component: DFS from u to the farthest node x, then DFS from x and take the max depth.
3. Do the same for v. ans=max(ans, d1*d2).
4. A single-node component has diameter 0, so the product is 0.
dry_run:
Sample: path 1-2-3-4.
Delete edge 2-3: diameters are 1 (1-2) and 1 (3-4), product 1.
Delete edge 1-2: diameters 0 and 2, product 0.
Maximum is 1 (matches).

name: Tree Shuffling
tags: dfs and similar, dp, greedy, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0912 Min vertex removals so every tree component has < K vertices
brief: Rooted tree; node u has cost a_u, bit b_u, target c_u. Operation: pick u and k nodes of its subtree, shuffle their bits, cost k*a_u. Min cost to reach targets, or -1.
key_idea: Replace a_u by min over its ancestors (cheapest manager); fix mismatches as low as possible where a_u is smaller, pairing 0->1 with 1->0 at each node.
solution:
1. Top-down: a[v] = min(a[v], a[parent]).
2. Bottom-up: x[u] = #need 0->1, y[u] = #need 1->0 in subtree (unpaired so far).
3. At u: t = min(x,y); cost += 2*t*a[u]; subtract t from both; pass leftovers to parent.
4. If root still has leftovers -> -1.
5. Use iterative BFS order (n=2e5) and long long.

Node3 needs 0->1, node2 needs 1->0: paired at node2 (a=2000): 4000.
Node1 (0->1) and node5 (1->0): paired at root (a=10000): 20000. Total 24000.

name: Choosing flowers
tags: binary search, brute force, data structures, dfs and similar, dp, greedy, sortings, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0113 Heroes vs Villains (remove from front)
brief: Buy exactly n flowers (n<=1e9) from m types: first flower of type i gives a_i, each additional gives b_i. Maximise total happiness.
key_idea: At most one type gets extra flowers; if type i is the one, take all a_j > b_i as first flowers, then fill the rest with b_i.
solution:
1. Sort a descending, prefix sums.
2. Candidate: only first flowers: pre[n] if n<=m.
3. For each i: p = #a_j > b_i (binary search); if p>=n skip.
4. val = pre[p]; if a_i <= b_i add a_i (buy type i's first) and one fewer slot; fill remaining slots with b_i.
5. Answer = max.

name: Buds Re-hanging
tags: constructive algorithms, dfs and similar, dp, greedy, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0912 Min vertex removals so every tree component has < K vertices
brief: Rooted tree. A bud is a non-root vertex whose children are all leaves (at least one). Re-hang buds (with their children) anywhere else. Minimise the number of leaves.
key_idea: Bottom-up: a vertex with at least one 'leaf' child is a bud (it gets cut off), otherwise it acts as a leaf. With k buds, hanging each bud on another bud's leaf saves one leaf each.
solution:
1. Process vertices bottom-up; leaf[v] = true if v has no child that is a leaf (all children were buds or none).
2. Otherwise v is a bud: k++.
3. Non-root vertices = k buds + L leaves, L = n-1-k.
4. If the root has a leaf child: answer L - k = n-1-2k; else L - k + 1 = n-2k.
dry_run:

Root child 3 is a leaf -> answer 7-1-4 = 2.

name: Seller Bob
nearest_infosys_question: Q0741 Prefix-minimum unique count after point decrements
brief: n<=5000 days of events 'win x' (get a 2^x stick) or 'sell x' (a customer pays 2^x if Bob holds that stick); Bob holds at most one stick. Max earnings (a huge number).
key_idea: 2^x exceeds the sum of all smaller powers, so greedily take sales by decreasing x, each using the latest matching win before it (shortest holding interval), if it doesn't overlap chosen intervals. Print with big-number arithmetic.
solution:
1. For each sell x find the latest earlier 'win x' -> interval [win, sell].
2. For x from 2000 down: take the interval if no day in it is already used; mark it.
3. Result = sum of 2^x for taken x: set bits, convert binary to decimal by repeated doubling in base 1e9.
4. (DP alternative: dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[win-1] + 2^x) with big integers.)
complexity: O(n * maxX) time with big-number conversion

Take 2^10 + 2^5 = 1024 + 32 = 1056.

name: Anton and Tree
nearest_infosys_question: Q0394 Longest trip after moving one road (tree diameter)
brief: paint(v) flips the whole same-colored component containing v. Find the minimum number of paints that makes the whole black/white tree one color.
key_idea: Contract each same-color component into one node. Each paint at the centre merges its neighbours, so the answer is ceil(d/2), where d is the diameter of the contracted tree. Compute it with 0-1 BFS, where an edge costs 1 if its endpoints have different colors.
solution:
1. 0-1 BFS from node 1 to find the farthest node x.
2. 0-1 BFS from x. d = the max distance.
3. Print (d+1)/2.
4. A single-color tree has d=0, so the answer is 0.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0075 Maximum index difference j-i with a[j] > a[i]
brief: Count indices i (1<=i<=n-k) such that the length-(k+1) subarray a_i..a_{i+k} satisfies 2^0*a_i < 2^1*a_{i+1} < ... < 2^k*a_{i+k}.
key_idea: Condition reduces to a_j < 2*a_{j+1} for each adjacent pair; count windows of k consecutive good adjacent pairs.
solution:
1. good[j]=1 if a[j] < 2*a[j+1] (j=0..n-2) (dividing the chain by 2^j).
2. A start i works iff good[i..i+k-1] are all 1.
3. Slide a window of length k over good counting ones (or prefix sums).
4. Count windows whose sum equals k. Use long long for 2*a.

name: Chat
nearest_infosys_question: Q0203 Minimum cost for tickets
brief: n messages; message i may link to earlier message a_i (0 = none). Opening x shows messages x-k..x+k; starting at t you read visible messages and follow links repeatedly. For every t print the number of distinct messages read.
key_idea: Links point backwards, so dp[i] = dp[a_i] + |window(i)| - |window(i) ∩ window(a_i)|; the overlap is [L_i, R_{a_i}] since everything the chain from a_i reads lies at or left of R_{a_i}.
solution:
1. L_i = max(1,i-k), R_i = min(n,i+k).
2. If a_i = 0: dp[i] = R_i - L_i + 1.
3. Else j=a_i: dp[i] = dp[j] + (R_i-L_i+1) - max(0, R_j - L_i + 1).
4. Process i increasing (j < i). Print dp.

name: Block Sequence
nearest_infosys_question: Q0215 Paint House with Budget Constraint
brief: A sequence is beautiful if it splits into blocks where each block starts with a number equal to the count of elements after it in that block. Find the minimum deletions to make a given sequence (n <= 2e5) beautiful.
key_idea: dp[i] = min deletions for suffix starting at i: either delete a_i, or start a block at i that covers exactly the next a_i elements.
solution:
1. dp[n] = 0.
2. For i = n-1 down to 0: dp[i] = dp[i+1] + 1 (delete a_i).
3. If i + a_i + 1 <= n: dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i + a_i + 1]).
4. Answer dp[0].

name: Tenzing and Balls
nearest_infosys_question: Q0215 Paint House with Budget Constraint
brief: n balls in a row with colors. Operation: choose i<j with equal colors and remove balls i..j. Maximize the total number of removed balls.
key_idea: dp[i] = max removed among the first i balls; ball i is kept (dp[i-1]) or ends a removed segment starting at an earlier j of the same color: dp[j-1] + (i-j+1). Keep best[c] = max(dp[j-1] - j + 1) per color.
solution:
1. dp[0] = 0, best[c] = -INF.
2. For i = 1..n with color c: dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], i + best[c]).
3. Then best[c] = max(best[c], dp[i-1] - i + 1) (ball i as a future left end).
4. Answer dp[n].

name: The Fair Nut and String
nearest_infosys_question: Q0208 Number of handshakes (DP)
brief: Given a string (length <= 1e5), count strictly increasing sequences of positions of 'a' such that between every two consecutive chosen positions there is at least one 'b'. Mod 1e9+7, non-empty sequences only.
key_idea: Split the string by 'b' into groups; from each group choose at most one 'a' (c_j + 1 ways). Answer = prod (c_j + 1) - 1.
solution:
1. Walk the string keeping cnt = number of 'a' in the current group.
2. On 'b': ans *= (cnt+1), cnt = 0.
3. Other letters are ignored (they don't separate).
4. After the loop ans *= (cnt+1); print ans - 1 mod p.

(1+1)*(0+1)*(2+1) = 6.
6 - 1 = 5 (expected 5).

name: The Humanoid
nearest_infosys_question: Q0488 Machine Cooling and Task Scheduling
brief: Humanoid with power h, two green serums (x2) and one blue serum (x3). It can absorb an astronaut with power strictly less than its own, gaining floor(a_i/2). Maximize astronauts absorbed.
key_idea: Sort astronauts; always absorb while possible, and use a serum only when stuck. Only the order of serums matters: try the 3 orders GGB, GBG, BGG and take the best.
solution:
1. Sort a ascending.
2. For each order of serums (2,2,3), (2,3,2), (3,2,2): h' = h, i = 0, k = 0.
3. While i < n: if a[i] < h': h' += a[i]/2, i++; else if k < 3: h' *= order[k++]; else break.
4. Answer = max i over orders. Use long long.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(1) extra space

stuck at 8 -> B (15): absorb 8 (19), absorb 9 (23).
All 4 absorbed -> answer 4.

name: Ayoub and Lost Array
nearest_infosys_question: Q0208 Number of handshakes (DP)
brief: Count arrays of length n (<=2e5) with all elements in [l,r] (<=1e9) whose sum is divisible by 3, modulo 1e9+7.
key_idea: Only residues mod 3 matter: count how many values in [l,r] give each residue, then DP over the running sum mod 3.
solution:
1. c[m] = number of x in [l,r] with x%3==m; g(N,m) = N>=m ? (N-m)/3+1 : 0 counts in [0,N]; c[m]=g(r,m)-g(l-1,m).
2. dp[0]=1 (empty array), dp[1]=dp[2]=0.
3. Repeat n times: nd[(j+m)%3] += dp[j]*c[m].
4. Answer dp[0] mod 1e9+7.

After 1 element: dp=[1,1,1].

name: Kyoya and Colored Balls
nearest_infosys_question: Q0208 Number of handshakes (DP)
brief: k colours with c_i identical balls each (total <=1000). Count draw orders where the last ball of colour i comes before the last ball of colour i+1 for all i, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Add colours one by one: the last ball of colour i must be at the end of the current sequence, the other c_i-1 balls go anywhere among the earlier positions: multiply by C(prefix-1, c_i-1).
solution:
1. Build Pascal's triangle C up to 1000 mod p.
2. total=0, ans=1.
3. For each colour i: total += c_i; ans *= C(total-1, c_i-1).
4. Print ans.

name: Colorful Bricks
nearest_infosys_question: Q0208 Number of handshakes (DP)
brief: Paint n bricks in a row with m colours (n,m<=2000) so exactly k bricks differ in colour from their left neighbour. Count colourings mod 998244353.
key_idea: Choose which k of the n-1 boundaries are changes, colour the first brick in m ways and each change in m-1 ways: m * (m-1)^k * C(n-1,k).
solution:
1. Choose positions of the k changes among bricks 2..n: C(n-1,k).
2. First brick: m colours; each change brick: m-1 colours; non-change bricks copy the left colour.
3. Answer = m * (m-1)^k * C(n-1,k) mod p (Pascal triangle or factorials).
4. (DP alternative: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i-1][j-1]*(m-1).)
complexity: O(n^2) with Pascal (or O(n) with factorials), O(n^2) space

name: Pie Rules
nearest_infosys_question: Q0215 Paint House with Budget Constraint
brief: N<=50 pie slices handed out in order; the holder of a decider token (Bob first) gives the next slice to someone and passes the token to the other person. Both maximise their own total. Output Alice's and Bob's totals.
key_idea: dp[i] = most the current token holder can get from slices i..N-1: either take slice i (token goes to the other) or give it away and keep the token.
solution:
1. S[i] = suffix sum of slices i..N-1; dp[N]=0.
2. dp[i] = max(a[i] + (S[i+1] - dp[i+1]), dp[i+1]).
3. Bob holds the token first: Bob = dp[0], Alice = S[0] - dp[0].
4. Print Alice then Bob.

name: Linova and Kingdom
tags: dfs and similar, dp, greedy, sortings, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0488 Machine Cooling and Task Scheduling
brief: Tree rooted at city 1 (n <= 2e5). Choose exactly k industry cities; each industry city's envoy gains happiness equal to the number of tourism cities on its path to the root. Maximize the total.
key_idea: Optimal choices are closed downward (children before parents), so choosing v contributes depth(v) - (subtree_size(v) - 1). Take the k largest such values.
solution:
1. BFS/DFS from 1 to get depth (root depth 0) and an order; accumulate subtree sizes in reverse order.
2. val(v) = depth(v) - (size(v) - 1).
3. Sort values descending, sum the top k (long long).
4. Picking v adds its depth but each of its size-1 descendants (already industry) loses 1.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

name: Sending a Sequence Over the Network
nearest_infosys_question: Q0248 Wasted Space (bag size changes)
brief: A sequence a was cut into segments and each segment's length was written immediately to its left or right, giving b. Given b, decide if this is possible.
key_idea: dp[i] = prefix of length i can be fully explained. Element at position i (1-indexed) with value v either is a left marker covering i+1..i+v (dp[i+v] |= dp[i-1]) or a right marker covering i-v..i-1 (dp[i] |= dp[i-v-1]).
solution:
1. dp[0] = true.
2. For i = 1..n, v = b_i:
   a) if i - v - 1 >= 0 and dp[i-v-1]: dp[i] = true (right marker).
   b) if dp[i-1] and i + v <= n: dp[i+v] = true (left marker).
3. Process i increasing (both updates only depend on smaller indices being final).
4. YES iff dp[n].

i=2 v=1: right: dp[0] -> dp[2] = true (segment [3] with length 1 to its right).
YES (expected YES). Sample [1] -> NO.

name: Obtain The String
nearest_infosys_question: Q0281 Array Minimization Game
brief: Build t starting from empty z; one operation appends any subsequence of s. Find the minimum number of operations, or -1 if some letter of t is missing from s.
key_idea: Greedy: match t through s as far as possible, then start a new pass. Precompute nxt[i][c] = first position >= i holding c to make each step O(1).
solution:
1. nxt[n][c] = -1; for i = n-1..0: nxt[i] = nxt[i+1], nxt[i][s[i]] = i.
2. ops = 1, pos = 0. For each char c of t: if nxt[0][c] == -1 -> answer -1.
3. If pos == n or nxt[pos][c] == -1: ops++, pos = 0.
4. pos = nxt[pos][c] + 1.
5. Print ops.

name: Chain Reaction
nearest_infosys_question: Q0272 Highway amplifier coverage
brief: Beacons at distinct positions a_i with power b_i; activated right to left, each destroys beacons to its left within distance b_i. You add one beacon to the far right (activated first) with any power. Minimize destroyed beacons.
key_idea: dp[i] = destroyed among first i beacons if beacon i is activated; added beacon destroys a suffix.
solution:
1. Sort by position.
2. For beacon i (1-indexed): j = number of beacons with position < a_i - b_i (lower_bound).
3. dp[i] = dp[j] + (i-1-j) (beacons j+1..i-1 die, beacon j then activates).
4. Added beacon destroys beacons i+1..n: answer = min over i of dp[i]+(n-i).
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

name: Segments Covering
nearest_infosys_question: Q0656 Buckets of coloured balls probability
brief: n segments on m cells; segment i exists independently with probability p_i/q_i. Find the probability (mod 998244353) that every cell is covered by exactly one existing segment.
key_idea: Factor out prod(1-p_i); then dp over cells: dp[r]+=dp[l-1]*p_i/(1-p_i) for segments that tile the strip.
solution:
1. Probability of a chosen set T = prod_{i in T} p_i * prod_{i not in T}(1-p_i) = P * prod_{i in T} p_i/(1-p_i), where P=prod (1-p_i).
2. Valid T is exactly a tiling of [1,m] by consecutive segments.
3. Group segments by right end; dp[0]=1; for r=1..m: dp[r]=sum over segments (l,r) of dp[l-1]*w_i, w_i=p_i*inv(q_i-p_i) mod p.
4. Answer = P*dp[m] mod p (p_i<q_i so 1-p_i is nonzero).
complexity: O((n+m) + n log MOD) time, O(n+m) space

name: Decorate Apple Tree
tags: constructive algorithms, dfs and similar, dp, graphs, greedy, sortings, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0488 Machine Cooling and Task Scheduling
brief: Rooted tree (root 1, parents p_i < i); bulbs go on leaves, and a node is happy if all bulbs in its subtree have distinct colors. For each k=1..n output the minimum colors so at least k nodes are happy.
key_idea: Node v needs exactly leaves(v) colors to be happy (and that many colors suffice for all nodes with fewer leaves), so the answer for k is the k-th smallest leaf count.
solution:
1. cnt[v] = number of leaves in v's subtree.
2. Since p_i < i, process v = n down to 1: if cnt[v]==0 then cnt[v]=1 (leaf); add cnt[v] to cnt[p_v].
3. Sort cnt ascending.
4. Print cnt[0..n-1] (the i-th value is the answer for k=i).
5. Edge: n=1 -> root is a leaf, output 1.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

name: Travel Card
nearest_infosys_question: Q0272 Highway amplifier coverage
brief: Tickets: one trip 20, 90-minute 50, 1440-minute 120. Trips at increasing times t_i; after each trip the system charges (optimal cost for all trips so far) minus (total charged before). Print each charge.
key_idea: dp[i] = min cost covering first i trips = min(dp[i-1]+20, dp[j]+50, dp[k]+120) where j/k = number of trips before t_i-89 / t_i-1439; print dp[i]-dp[i-1].
solution:
1. dp[0] = 0.
2. For trip i (time t): j = lower_bound(t, t-89) index (first trip covered by a 90-min ticket ending at t), k = lower_bound(t, t-1439).
3. dp[i] = min(dp[i-1] + 20, dp[j] + 50, dp[k] + 120) (dp indexed by count of trips).
4. Output dp[i] - dp[i-1].
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

name: Short Task
tags: brute force, dp, math, number theory
nearest_infosys_question: Q0654 Largest subset of 1..n-1 with product 1 mod n
brief: d(n) = sum of divisors of n. For each c (<=1e7) output the smallest n with d(n)=c, or -1.
key_idea: Precompute sigma(n) for all n<=1e7 with a divisor sieve, then ans[sigma(n)] = smallest such n.
solution:
1. sigma[n] for n<=1e7: for each i, add i to all multiples (harmonic sum ~1.6e8 ops) or use a linear sieve.
2. Since sigma(n) >= n+1 > n for n>1, only n<=c matter, so N=1e7 suffices.
3. ans[] init -1; for n from N down to 1: if sigma[n]<=N, ans[sigma[n]]=n (descending keeps the smallest).
4. Answer each query in O(1). Memory ~80MB of ints (limit 512MB).
complexity: O(N log N) precompute, O(1) per query

name: Good Schedule
nearest_infosys_question: Q0272 Highway amplifier coverage
brief: Alice/Bob see episodes a_i/b_i on day i. In a day range [L,R] each starts having seen nothing and watches the day's episode only if it is the next one they need. Range is valid if every day both watch the same episode or neither watches. Count valid ranges (n<=5e5).
key_idea: While valid, both counters stay equal (c); only 'event' days where a_i or b_i equals c+1 matter, so precompute for each matched day the furthest valid end via jumps.
solution:
1. Validity is prefix-closed, so answer = sum over L of (maxR(L)-L+1).
2. pos[w] = sorted days i where a_i==w or b_i==w. After a matched day j (a_j==b_j=v, counter becomes v), next event k = first day in pos[v+1] greater than j.
3. f[j] (furthest valid R after advancing at j): no k -> n; a_k==b_k -> f[k]; else k-1. Compute j from n down to 1.
4. For L: k = first day >= L in pos[1]; none -> maxR=n; a_k==b_k==1 -> f[k]; else k-1.
5. Sum (maxR-L+1) in long long.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

f[2]: v=2, no day with value 3 after 2 -> 3. f[1]: v=1, next value-2 day is 2 (matched) -> f[2]=3.
L=1: first value-1 day is 1 (matched) -> R=3: 3 ranges. L=2: first value-1 day>=2 is 3 (a=1,b=2 mismatch) -> R=2: 1. L=3: R=2: 0.
Total 4.

name: Office Keys
tags: binary search, brute force, dp, greedy, sortings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0296 Hotel customers minimum unhappiness (Chef Monocarp)
brief: n people and k>=n keys on a line, office at p. Each person takes a distinct key then walks to the office. Minimize the time when the last person arrives.
key_idea: After sorting both, an optimal assignment uses a contiguous block of n keys matched in order; try every block.
solution: 1) Sort people a and keys b. 2) For each start j (0..k-n): time = max over i of |a_i - b_{j+i}| + |b_{j+i} - p|. 3) Answer = min over j. 4) (DP alternative: dp[i][j] = min max-time for first i people using first j keys.) 5) long long.

name: Andrey and Escape from Capygrad
tags: binary search, data structures, dp, dsu, greedy, sortings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0272 Highway amplifier coverage
brief: n portals (l,r,a,b) with l<=a<=b<=r: from any point in [l,r] you can teleport into [a,b]. For each of q start points, the max reachable coordinate.
key_idea: Only [l_i, b_i] matters (from there jump to b_i; from (b_i, r_i] it never helps); merge these intervals and answer by binary search.
solution: 1) Make intervals [l_i, b_i]; sort by l. 2) Merge overlapping/touching intervals (next.l <= cur.R) into [L,R]. 3) For query x: find last merged interval with L <= x; if x <= R answer R else x. 4) Print answers.
complexity: O((n+q) log n) time, O(n) space

name: Fixing a Binary String
tags: bitmasks, brute force, constructive algorithms, dp, greedy, hashing, strings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0879 Palindrome Pairs Variant
brief: Binary string s, k divides n. Choose p: result = s[p+1..n] + reverse(s[1..p]). Find p making the result k-proper (first k equal, s_i != s_{i+k}), or -1.
key_idea: Only two k-proper strings exist (blocks of k alternating, starting with 0 or 1); check each p with a Z-function (suffix match) and a common prefix with the reversed target.
solution: 1) For c in {0,1}: T = blocks of k starting with c; rT = reverse(T). 2) L = longest common prefix of s and rT (reverse(s[0..p)) == T[n-p..] iff s[0..p) == rT[0..p)). 3) Z-function on T + '#' + s: s[p..] == T[0..n-p) iff z[n+1+p] >= n-p. 4) Any p in 1..n with p <= L and suffix match is an answer (p=n: suffix empty). 5) Else -1.

name: Slime Escape
tags: data structures, dp, greedy, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0495 Min sum of AP-index selection after one swap
brief: Slimes at positions 1..n with health a_i; you control slime k (a_k>=0). Moving onto a slime absorbs its health; health must never go negative. Can you reach position 0 or n+1?
key_idea: Expand greedily on each side, but only 'commit' a stretch when its total is >= 0 (health doesn't drop); alternate sides until an escape is reached or both sides are stuck.
solution: 1) h = a_k; left scan pointer lp=k-1 with uncommitted sum ls=0; right rp=k+1, rs=0. 2) Left step: while lp>=1 and h+ls+a[lp]>=0: ls+=a[lp], lp--; whenever ls>=0, commit h+=ls, ls=0. If lp reaches 0 -> YES. 3) Same for the right side (reaching n+1 -> YES). 4) Repeat while some commit happened; if a full round has no commit -> NO. 5) Scan pointers never move back (larger h keeps earlier prefixes valid), so it's amortized O(n).

name: Korney Korneevich and XOR (easy version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0304 Longest Special Subsequence (bitwise LIS)
brief: Array a (n<=1e5, a_i<=500). List all x such that some strictly increasing subsequence (possibly empty) has XOR equal to x.
key_idea: dp[x] = smallest possible last element of an increasing subsequence with XOR x; a smaller last element is always better for extension.

key_idea: Removing position 1 repeatedly always works; the array is unambiguous iff each a_i (i>=2) shares a prime with every index 2..i, i.e. a_i is divisible by the product of all primes <= i.

key_idea: dp[i][left] = max rating after day i with 'left' kg of day-i food remaining (<= 400). On each day feed the k cheapest present friends, using yesterday's food first.

5. Greedy per day fails: saving today's food may feed more friends tomorrow, which is why the DP is needed.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0546 Binary array trim to balance
brief: A string is alternating if its length is even, all odd positions hold one letter and all even positions hold one letter. Using at most one deletion and any number of replacements, minimize operations to make s alternating.
key_idea: Even n: no deletion; cost = (n/2 - max freq on even positions) + (n/2 - max freq on odd positions). Odd n: must delete one char; try every i using prefix counts per parity and suffix counts per parity (suffix parities swap after deletion).

1. If n even: cnt[p][c] over parity p; answer n - max_c cnt[0][c] - max_c cnt[1][c].
2. If n odd: suf[p][c] = counts over the whole string initially; pre[p][c] = 0.
3. For i = 0..n-1: remove s[i] from suf; new even counts = pre[0] + suf[1], new odd = pre[1] + suf[0]; cost = 1 + (n-1) - maxEven - maxOdd; then add s[i] to pre[i%2].
4. Answer min cost (n=1 gives 1).

3. f(X) = pop(X) * (n - pop(X)); pop(w) = number of positions where s and z differ.

brief: Count arrays of n integers in [0,2^k) where AND of all elements >= XOR of all elements, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Compare bit by bit from the top: per bit count ways AND==XOR (tie) vs AND>XOR (win, then lower bits free).
solution:
1. Per bit, #assignments with an even number of ones = 2^(n-1).
2. n odd: all-ones gives AND=1,XOR=1 (tie); ties per bit = 2^(n-1)+1, AND>XOR impossible -> answer (2^(n-1)+1)^k.
3. n even: tie = 2^(n-1)-1 (even, not all ones), win = 1 (all ones gives AND=1, XOR=0).
4. Answer = tie^k + sum over winning bit i (from top) of tie^(k-1-i) * (2^n)^i, where i = number of lower bits free.
5. Use fast power mod; k=0 -> 1.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0518 Minimum balls to reset box strengths
brief: Binary strings s,t; per query (l,r) on substrings a=s[l..r], b=t[l..r]: op1 a_i=a_{i+2}=0 -> b_{i+1}=1; op2 b_i=b_{i+2}=1 -> a_{i+1}=1. Max ones in a.

brief: Count the strictly increasing arrays 1..m of length n that satisfy an lcm/fraction condition between neighbours, where some entries are fixed and the rest are free (0). Rule (derived from samples): a_1 = 1 and (a_{i+1} - a_i) divides a_i for each neighbour pair.
key_idea: The condition reduces to a_1=1 and (a_{i+1}-a_i) dividing a_i, which follows from 1/lcm(x,y) ≤ 1/x-1/y. So each step goes from v to v+d for a divisor d of v.

1. Precompute the divisors of every v ≤ m.
2. dp over positions: dp[v] = ways where the current element equals v. Start with dp[1]=1 at position 1 if that is allowed.
3. Transition: for each v and each divisor d of v with v+d ≤ m, ndp[v+d] += dp[v].

5. The answer is the sum of dp after n positions, mod p.

name: New Year and the Permutation Concatenation
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: Concatenate all permutations of 1..n in lexicographic order; count length-n windows whose sum is n(n+1)/2, mod 998244353.
key_idea: Answer = n*n! - sum_{j=1}^{n-1} n!/j!: a boundary-straddling window fails exactly when the left permutation's tail of length j is decreasing (n!/j! such permutations).
solution:
1. The n! windows aligned with a permutation are all good.
2. A window with the last n-k elements of P and the first k of the next permutation Q is good iff Q keeps P's first k elements, i.e. P's tail of length j=n-k is NOT decreasing.
3. Permutations with a decreasing tail of length j: n!/j!; so good windows for that split = n! - n!/j! (the last permutation, always decreasing, has no successor and cancels out).
4. Total = n! + sum_{j=1}^{n-1} (n! - n!/j!) = n*n! - sum_{j=1}^{n-1} n!/j!, computing n!/j! = (j+1)...n iteratively, mod p.

brief: A frog starts at depth n. From depth x it can jump up to any depth in [x-a_x, x]. After landing at depth y it slips down to y+b_y. Find the minimum number of jumps to reach depth 0 and print the depths it lands on.
key_idea: Run BFS over the positions after slipping. Each landing depth y needs to be expanded only once, so keep the unvisited landing depths in a set and erase them as you go. This makes the BFS O(n log n).

2. Pop x. If x-a_x<=0, depth 0 is reachable: answer dist+1, then rebuild the path.
3. Otherwise go through the set from lower_bound(x-a_x) while y<=x. Erase y, set nx=y+b_y, and if nx is unvisited record dist, the parent x and the landing depth y, then push nx.
4. If the queue empties, print -1.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

brief: There are n shelves. From each shelf you may take items only from its left or right end. Take exactly m items in total and maximize their total value.
key_idea: For each shelf, best[j] = max over taking l items from the left and j-l from the right, computed with prefix sums. Then run a group knapsack over the shelves.

3. Start with dp[0]=0 and everything else -inf.

brief: n photos sit in a circle, starting at photo 1. A swipe costs a, a first view costs 1 (+b if the photo needs rotating), and you can't skip unseen photos. Maximize the photos seen within time T.
key_idea: The seen photos form 1..r going right plus l photos going left from n. You pay for the shorter side twice. For each r, binary search the largest l, since the cost is monotone in l.

key_idea: Each bit present in the total OR appears in exactly half of the 2^n subsets' XORs, so coziness = (OR of all x) * 2^(n-1).
solution:
1. OR together all given x -> T (equals OR of the whole array since segments cover everything).
2. For a bit set in at least one element, exactly 2^(n-1) subsets have odd count of it.
3. Answer = T * 2^(n-1) mod 1e9+7 (fast power).

name: Tree Cutting
tags: binary search, dp, greedy, implementation, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0907 Tree partitioning problem
brief: Tree with n vertices. Remove exactly k edges so every component has at least x vertices; find the maximum x.
key_idea: For a fixed x, greedily cut a subtree as soon as its accumulated size reaches x (bottom-up); feasible iff at least k+1 pieces of size >= x are formed (extra cuts can be merged back). Binary search x.
solution:
1. Root at 1, compute a BFS order and parents.
2. check(x): rem[v] = 1; process vertices in reverse order: add rem[v] to parent unless rem[v] >= x for a non-root v (then cnt++ and pass 0).
3. At the root: if rem[root] >= x then cnt++.
4. Feasible iff cnt >= k+1.
5. Binary search the largest x in [1, n/(k+1)].
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

x=3: node2 gets 3 -> cnt 1, root rem 1 < 3 -> cnt 1 < 2 fail.
Answer 2.

name: Job Interview
tags: binary search, dp, greedy, implementation, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0876 Max Balanced L/R Substrings after One Adjacent Swap
brief: n+m+1 candidates arrive in order; each goes to programmer (if a_i > b_i) or tester role, or the other role if that one is full (n programmers, m testers). For each candidate, output the team skill if that candidate does not come.
key_idea: Simulate the first n+m candidates (that's the answer when the last one is absent). Removing candidate i frees its role r: the first later candidate j who preferred r but was pushed to the other role now takes r, and the last candidate fills the freed other slot; if no such j, the last candidate takes r.
solution:
1. Simulate candidates 1..n+m greedily: role[i], base = total skill. val(i, r) = a_i or b_i.
2. Precompute nxt[r][i] = first j > i (j <= n+m) with preferred role r but assigned the other role.
3. For i <= n+m with role r: if j = nxt[r][i] exists: ans = base - val(i,r) + val(j,r) - val(j,!r) + val(last,!r); else ans = base - val(i,r) + val(last,r).
4. For the last candidate: ans = base.
5. Use long long.
complexity: O(n + m) per test, O(n + m) space
dry_run:
Sample n=1,m=0: a = 2 1, b = 1 2. First candidate: programmer (2), base = 2.
Remove 1: no later j; last candidate takes programmer: 2 - 2 + 1 = 1.
Remove 2 (last): 2. Output '1 2' (expected).

name: Remove the Bracket
nearest_infosys_question: Q0507 Song volume coefficient changes
brief: Split each middle a_i into x_i+y_i=a_i with (x_i-s)(y_i-s)>=0; minimize F=a_1*x_2+y_2*x_3+...+y_{n-1}*a_n.
key_idea: F is linear in each x_i, so only the two extreme valid splits matter; 2-state DP over which extreme is used.
solution:
1. Valid x_i form an interval; extremes: if a_i<=s: lo=0; else lo=min(s,a_i-s); hi=a_i-lo. Options (x,y)=(lo,hi) or (hi,lo).
2. dp[i][0/1] = min F prefix with option 0/1 at i; prevY for i=1 is a_1.
3. dp[i][o] = min over p of dp[i-1][p] + y_{i-1,p} * x_{i,o}.
4. Answer = min over o of dp[n-1][o] + y_{n-1,o}*a_n. Use long long.

name: Alternative Thinking
nearest_infosys_question: Q0507 Song volume coefficient changes
brief: Given a binary string of length n (n<=1e5), flip exactly one contiguous substring (0<->1) to maximize the length of the longest alternating subsequence; print that maximum.
key_idea: Longest alternating subsequence = number of maximal equal blocks g; one flip can add at most 2 blocks, so answer = min(n, g+2).
solution:
1. Count g = 1 + number of positions i with s[i] != s[i-1] (each block contributes one char to the subsequence).
2. Flipping a substring changes only the two boundaries of the substring, so g grows by at most 2.
3. If some block has length>=2 (or two blocks of length 2 exist) the +2 (or +1) is achievable; overall formula min(n, g+2) covers all cases.
4. Edge: already fully alternating (g=n) -> answer n.

name: Friendly Gifts
nearest_infosys_question: Q0094 Rotated prefix MEX cost
brief: Array a (n<=6000, a_i<=n). Pick two non-overlapping subsegments of equal length L so each is a permutation of consecutive integers and together they form one consecutive range (2L distinct values). Maximize L (0 if impossible).
key_idea: A good segment of length L with min v is exactly the set {v..v+L-1}; we need good segments with mins v and v+L that are disjoint. Brute force over L with a sliding window.
solution:
1. For each L=1..n/2 slide a window of length L, keeping counts (number of duplicated values) and min/max via monotonic deques.
2. Window is good iff no duplicates and max-min==L-1; for its min v record firstEnd[v]=min end index and lastStart[v]=max start index.
3. For each v with v+L<=n: if both mins exist and firstEnd[v]<lastStart[v+L] or firstEnd[v+L]<lastStart[v], L is achievable.
4. Answer = largest achievable L (not monotone, so test all L).

name: Medical Parity
nearest_infosys_question: Q0264 Two City Scheduling with Adjacency Penalty
brief: Binary strings x' and y' of length n; y must be the prefix-parity string of x (y_i = parity of ones in x_1..x_i). Min total bit flips in x' and y' to make that true.
key_idea: Scan left to right tracking the prefix parity; choose each x_i (0/1), paying for flipping x_i and for y_i mismatching the new parity.
solution:
1. dp[p] = min flips so far with current prefix parity p; dp[0]=0, dp[1]=INF.
2. For each i and choice b in {0,1}: q=p^b, cost = (b!=x'_i) + (q!=y'_i); nd[q]=min(nd[q], dp[p]+cost).
3. Answer min(dp[0],dp[1]).
4. Total length up to 1e6: use fast IO.

name: Buses
nearest_infosys_question: Q0297 Investment opportunities (non-overlapping range revenue)
brief: Stops 0..n (n<=1e9), m<=1e5 buses; bus i goes s_i->t_i, can be boarded at any stop in [s_i, t_i-1] and left only at t_i. Count ways to get from 0 to n mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: ways(bus i) = [s_i==0] + sum of ways of buses whose end t_j lies in [s_i, t_i-1]; sort buses by t and use prefix sums + binary search.
solution:
1. Sort buses by t. Process in order; maintain prefix sums of ways over the sorted list.
2. For bus i: the buses with t_j in [s_i, t_i-1] form a contiguous index range among those already processed (find with lower_bound on t).
3. w_i = (s_i==0) + sum over that range (mod).
4. Answer = sum of w_i over buses with t_i==n; 0 if none.
complexity: O(m log m) time, O(m) space

key_idea: Alice always eats the smallest valid value; Bob's only useful plan is to fully delete some distinct-value groups before Alice reaches them, paying their counts with turns earned from Alice's moves.

Delete group i: allowed if dp[i][a] + c_i <= a (Bob has had a turns), dp[i+1][a] = dp[i][a]+c_i. 4) Answer = min a with dp[k][a] finite.

brief: Three clusters of a, b, c islands. Add bridges between any islands so that two islands of the same color are either disconnected or at distance >= 3. Count configurations mod 998244353.
key_idea: No same-color edges and no island connected to two islands of the same other color; so bridges between each pair of clusters form a matching, independently: f(x,y) = sum_k C(x,k) C(y,k) k!.
solution: 1) Precompute factorials / binomials up to 5000 (or Pascal triangle). 2) f(x,y) = sum_{k=0}^{min(x,y)} C(x,k)*C(y,k)*k! mod p. 3) Answer = f(a,b) * f(b,c) * f(a,c) mod p. 4) Alternative DP: f(x,y) = f(x-1,y) + y*f(x-1,y-1).

brief: n days x m hours timetable of lessons; skip at most k lessons total. Each day costs (last attended - first attended + 1) hours (0 if none). Minimize total hours.
key_idea: Per day, skipping j lessons optimally means attending a contiguous run of the lesson list; then a knapsack over days on the number of skips.
solution: 1) For day d with lesson positions P (cnt c): best[j] = 0 if j>=c else min over i of P[i+c-j-1] - P[i] + 1. 2) dp[s] = min total hours using s skips over processed days; init dp[0]=0. 3) For each day: nd[s+j] = min(dp[s] + best[j]) for j<=c, s+j<=k. 4) Answer = min over s<=k of dp[s].
complexity: O(n*m^2 + n*k*m) time, O(k + m) space

key_idea: States are lattice paths (i,j) with i,j <= N moves; the number of distinct states is sum over cells of C(i+j, i) = C(2N+2, N+1) - 1.
solution: 1) Count = sum_{i=0}^{N} sum_{j=0}^{N} C(i+j, i) = C(2N+2, N+1) - 1 (hockey-stick identity twice). 2) Precompute factorials up to 2N+2 and modular inverses. 3) Print (C(2N+2,N+1) - 1) mod p.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0117 Three cuts to 4 parts minimize max-min sum
brief: You start at 0 on a line with boxes and special positions; you can push boxes (not pull). Maximise the number of boxes ending on special positions.
key_idea: Positive and negative sides are independent (mirror negatives). On one side, pushing to the right forms a contiguous block of the first t boxes ending at some special position b_j.

name: XORificator 3000
tags: bitmasks, dp, number theory, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0324 Ordinary Numbers (binary string XOR pairs)
brief: Each query gives l, r, i, k (r up to 1e18, i up to 30). Output the XOR of all x in [l,r] with x mod 2^i != k.
key_idea: Take XOR(l..r) and XOR it again with the excluded numbers k + j*2^i. The j's form a range, so their XOR is (XOR of the j range) << i, and the low bits are k only if the count is odd.
solution:
1. f(n)=XOR 0..n: n%4==0->n, 1->1, 2->n+1, 3->0; XOR(l..r)=f(r)^f(l-1).
2. m=2^i. Excluded x=k+j*m with j in [lo,hi], lo=ceil((l-k)/m) (0 if l<=k), hi=floor((r-k)/m) (no terms if r<k).
3. ex = (f(hi)^f(lo-1))<<i, and if (hi-lo+1) is odd, ex|=k.
4. answer = XOR(l..r) ^ ex. i=0 gives 0 automatically.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0659 Pick two distinct numbers whose GCD is not prime
brief: Given 2n numbers, count the integers m whose multiset {p1,e1,...,pk,ek} of primes and exponents equals the given multiset. Answer mod 998244353.
key_idea: Choose n distinct prime values to act as the bases. The remaining n numbers are exponents, and they can be arranged in n!/prod(cnt_rest!) ways. Run a knapsack DP over the distinct primes to sum prod 1/(remaining count)!.
solution:
1. Sieve up to 1e6 and count each value c_v.
2. Non-prime values are always exponents. Multiply the base factor by inv(c_v!) for each.
3. dp[j] over the distinct prime values: for each prime v, new[j] = dp[j]*inv(c_v!) + dp[j-1]*inv((c_v-1)!), meaning v is not chosen or chosen as a base.
4. Answer = n! * base * dp[n]. It is 0 if there are fewer than n distinct primes.

name: Symmetric and Transitive
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: Count binary relations on an n-element set (n<=4000) that are symmetric and transitive but NOT reflexive, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Such a relation = an equivalence relation on a subset S plus >=1 'isolated' elements; count = sum_{k>=1} C(n,k)*Bell(n-k) = Bell(n+1)-Bell(n).
solution:
1. Element x with any pair (x,y) must have (x,x) by symmetry+transitivity, so elements split into 'used' (an equivalence relation) and 'unused'.
2. Non-reflexive means at least one unused element.
3. Count = sum_{k=1..n} C(n,k)*B(n-k) = B(n+1)-B(n) (Bell numbers).
4. Compute Bell numbers with the Bell triangle in O(n^2) using a rolling row.

brief: Connected graph, n<=100. Put a police station in one city; a road is safe if an endpoint has it. Maximise the average number of safe roads over all shortest paths from 1 to n.
key_idea: Count shortest paths from 1 and from n with BFS; paths through an edge (a,b) = c1[a]*cn[b].
solution:
1. BFS from 1 and from n: distances d1,dn and path counts c1,cn (use double, counts can be huge).
2. Edge a->b lies on a shortest path iff d1[a]+1+dn[b]==D.
3. For station v (not 1 or n): sum over incident shortest-path edges of c1[a]*cn[b]; each path through v uses 2 such edges, so this counts safe roads.
4. Average = sum / c1[n]. Station at 1 or n gives exactly 1. Take max.

name: Short Permutation Problem
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: For every m in [3,n+1] and k, count permutations of 1..n (n<=4000) with exactly k adjacent pairs having sum >= m (mod 998244353), then output a hash sum a_{m,k} x^{mn+k} mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: For fixed m, insert numbers in an order where each new number is either >=m-paired with ALL inserted numbers or with NONE; then an insertion DP over #good adjacencies works.
solution:
1. Build order by repeatedly removing: if min+max >= m remove max (good with all), else remove min (bad with all); insert in reverse removal order.
2. f[j] = #arrangements of t inserted numbers with j good adjacencies (t+1 slots: 2 ends, j good gaps, t-1-j bad gaps).
3. Good-with-all insert: j->j+1 in (j+2) ways (ends + good gaps), j->j+2 in (t-1-j) ways.
4. Bad-with-all insert: j->j-1 in j ways, j->j in (t+1-j) ways.
5. This is O(n^2) per m = O(n^3) total (fine for small n, verified vs brute force n<=5); the full n=4000 needs the editorial's closed form/FFT speedup, not reproduced here.
complexity: O(n^3) as described (too slow for n=4000 without the extra optimisation)
