name: The Endspeaker (Easy Version)
tags: binary search, dp, graphs, greedy, implementation, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0945 Smallest subarray with K good pairs
brief: Array a (n) and strictly decreasing b (m), k starts at 1. Free op: k++ (k<m). Paid op: remove a prefix of a with sum <= b_k at cost m-k. Min cost to empty a, or -1. n*m<=3e5.
key_idea: f[i][k] = min cost to clear suffix from i with current k; for fixed k always jump to the furthest reachable index (two pointers).
solution:
1. f[n][k]=0 for all k; process k from m down to 1, keeping only arrays for k and k+1.
2. For fixed k, r(i) = largest r with sum a[i..r-1] <= b_k; r is non-increasing as i decreases -> two pointers.
3. f[i][k] = min(f[i][k+1] (if k<m), (m-k) + f[r(i)][k] if r(i)>i).
4. Jumping furthest is optimal because f[.][k] is non-increasing in i (shorter suffix never costs more).
5. Answer f[0][1]; INF -> -1.

name: Yet Another Minimization Problem
nearest_infosys_question: Q0214 Fence panels with one custom panel
brief: (Statement page could not be fetched; from the known problem) Arrays a,b of length n<=100, values<=100. You may swap a_i with b_i for any i. Minimize sum over i<j of (a_i+a_j)^2 + (b_i+b_j)^2.
key_idea: sum_{i<j}(a_i+a_j)^2 = (n-2)*sum a_i^2 + (sum a)^2; the first part is swap-invariant, so minimize (Sa)^2 + (S-Sa)^2 via subset sum.
solution: 1) S = total of all a and b; Q = sum of a_i^2 + b_i^2. 2) Subset-sum DP over i: reachable sums of chosen element of each pair (choose a_i or b_i). 3) For each reachable Sa: cost = (n-2)*Q + Sa^2 + (S-Sa)^2. 4) Answer = minimum. 5) n=1 gives 0.

For m=2..n: x=pp[m], y=pq[m]; if x or y in [L,R] -> 0; else lo=1, hi=n; for each of x,y: if < L lo=max(lo,v+1), if > R hi=min(hi,v-1); add (L-lo+1)*(hi-R+1); then L=min(L,x,y), R=max(R,x,y). 4) Add 1 for the full array (MEX n+1). 5) long long.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0386 Graph + state DP (Hard)
brief: DAG with n<=5000 nodes, m<=5000 weighted edges. Find a path 1 -> n of total time <= T that visits the maximum number of nodes; print it.
key_idea: dp[k][v] = minimum time to reach v having visited exactly k nodes; layer by k so no topological sort is needed.

key_idea: Answer(p) = min over meeting vertex v of d(1,v) + d(p,v); a layered Dijkstra: layer 0 walks forward edges from 1, a free switch to layer 1, then layer 1 walks reversed edges toward p.

key_idea: Floyd per car, take the per-pair minimum over cars as 'one segment', then min-plus multiply to allow more segments; more than n changes never help.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0138 Maximum Xor-Sum in range [0,K]
brief: Operation: XOR a segment [l,r] with any x at cost ceil(len/2). Find the minimum total cost to make the whole array zero (n<=1e5).
key_idea: Using only length-1/2 operations, cost n works; each disjoint segment with XOR 0 saves 1. Answer = n - max number of disjoint zero-XOR segments (greedy cut).
solution:
1. Any op of length L costs like ceil(L/2) ops of length <=2, so consider pairs/singles: a chain of length-2 ops across a block saves 1 when the block XOR is 0.
2. Greedy: keep a set of prefix XORs since the last cut (start with {0} and running xor p=0).
3. For each a_i: p ^= a_i; if p in set -> cnt++, reset set = {0}, p = 0; else insert p.
4. Answer n - cnt.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

nearest_infosys_question: Q0308 Max alternating-sign sum over non-decreasing subsequence
brief: Choose a subset of indices maximizing sum a_i such that every chosen pair satisfies |i-j| > max(a_i,a_j).
key_idea: Checking consecutive chosen indices is enough. dp[j] = a_j + max dp[i] over i <= j-a_j-1 with i+a_i < j. Activate dp[i] in a prefix-max BIT at time i+a_i+1, then query the prefix up to j-a_j-1.

4. The answer is max dp (or 0). Use long long.

key_idea: d_i = h - a_i is the number of segments covering i, with d_0 = d_{n+1} = 0. Between i-1 and i, at most one segment ends and at most one starts. A delta of +1 means start one (1 way). 0 means nothing, or end one of the d_{i-1} open segments and start a new one (d_{i-1}+1 ways). -1 means end one (d_{i-1} ways).
solution:
1. If any d_i < 0, the answer is 0.
2. For i=1..n+1: delta = d_i - d_{i-1}.
3. Multiply ans by: 1 (delta=+1), d_{i-1}+1 (delta=0), or d_{i-1} (delta=-1). If |delta|>1, the answer is 0.

name: Paint the Tree
nearest_infosys_question: Q0917 Count tree colorings with B nodes at distance >= K
brief: Weighted tree in which each vertex gets k colors and each color is used by at most 2 vertices. An edge is saturated if its endpoints share a color. Maximize the total weight of saturated edges, which is the same as choosing edges with every vertex degree ≤ k.
key_idea: This is a maximum-weight subgraph with every degree ≤ k. dp[v][0] allows v at most k-1 chosen child edges, so the parent edge is still free. dp[v][1] allows at most k. Taking child c gains w + dp[c][0] - dp[c][1]. Sort the gains and take the best positive ones.
solution:
1. Root the tree and process vertices in reverse DFS order, iteratively.
2. base = sum of dp[c][1] over the children. gain_c = w(v,c) + dp[c][0] - dp[c][1].
3. Sort the gains in descending order and keep the positive ones.
4. dp[v][1] = base + sum of the top k. dp[v][0] = base + sum of the top k-1.
5. The answer is dp[root][1].

name: Gerald and Giant Chess
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: Count right/down paths on an h x w board (up to 1e5) avoiding n<=2000 black cells, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Sort the black cells and add the target as the last 'cell'. dp[i] = paths reaching cell i with no black cell before it = C(total) - sum dp[j]*paths(j->i).
solution:
1. Precompute factorials up to h+w.
2. Sort the black cells by (r,c) and append (h,w).
3. dp[i] = C(r_i+c_i-2, r_i-1) - sum over j<i with r_j<=r_i and c_j<=c_i of dp[j]*C(r_i-r_j+c_i-c_j, r_i-r_j).

name: Phoenix and Computers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: n<=400 computers in a row. A computer turns on automatically when both neighbours are on. Count the sequences of manual activations that turn everything on, mod a prime M.
key_idea: The final picture is blocks of manually-activated computers separated by single auto computers. A block of length L has 2^(L-1) internal orders, and blocks interleave via binomials.
solution:
1. dp[i][k]: the first i positions are decided (position i is an auto separator or the virtual start), with k manual activations so far.
2. Add a block of L manual computers followed by one auto: dp[i+L+1][k+L] += dp[i][k] * C(k+L, L) * 2^(L-1).
3. The last block ends at n, so the transition lands on n+1 (a virtual separator).
4. Answer = sum over k of dp[n+1][k].

name: Earn or Unlock

brief: A deck of n cards (top card unlocked). Use an unlocked card either to unlock the next v locked cards or to earn v points. Maximise the points. n<=1e5.
key_idea: If exactly k cards end up unlocked, all their values are used, and the cards used to unlock sum to k-1, so the points = prefix(k) - (k-1). Find the reachable k with a bitset subset-sum that respects order.
solution:
1. Bitset dp over the unlocked count, dp[1]=1. Size 2n (it can overshoot n).
2. For card i=1..n: dp |= dp << a_i (card i can unlock).
3. Then if dp[i]: ans = max(ans, P[i] - (i-1)), and clear dp[i] (that state stops at i and can't use later cards).
4. For k in (n,2n] with dp[k]: ans = max(ans, P[n] - (k-1)).

name: Sum of Paths
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: Sum the values over all paths of exactly k moves on n cells (any start, moving left/right). q point updates; print the sum after each. n,k<=5000, q<=2e5.
key_idea: The total is sum a_i * cnt_i, where cnt_i = the number of (path, time) pairs visiting i = sum_t f[t][i]*f[k-t][i] (paths are reversible). Each update is O(1).
solution:
1. f[0][i]=1. f[t][i] = f[t-1][i-1] + f[t-1][i+1] (the number of t-step walks ending at i = starting at i).
2. cnt_i = sum over t=0..k of f[t][i] * f[k-t][i].
3. S = sum a_i*cnt_i mod p.
4. Update: S -= a_i*cnt_i, set a_i = x, S += x*cnt_i, then print.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0507 Song volume coefficient changes
brief: You may reverse any segment whose min+max is odd. Can the array be sorted non-decreasingly?
key_idea: If it is already sorted, or global min+max is odd, the answer is YES. Otherwise min and max share a parity P. Elements of the other parity can move freely. A P-parity element above every opposite-parity value ('high') can never pass a P-parity element below every opposite-parity value ('low').
solution:
1. If sorted, or (mn+mx) is odd, print YES.
2. P = parity of mn. Wmax and Wmin = the max and min of the elements with parity != P. If there are none, print NO, since no move is possible.
3. Scan left to right. Mark when you see a P-parity x > Wmax. If you then see a P-parity x < Wmin, print NO.
4. Otherwise print YES.
(Derived by me and checked against BFS brute force on all 50,069 arrays with n<=6 and values<=n.)

name: Insertion Sort

brief: Permutation of 0..n-1 (n<=5000). Swap exactly two elements so that insertion sort does the fewest swaps (= inversions). Print that minimum and how many pairs (i,j) achieve it.
key_idea: Swapping i<j with a[i]>a[j] changes inversions by -(2x+1), where x = #k in (i,j) with a[j]<a[k]<a[i]; get x in O(1) from a 2D prefix count.
solution:
1. I = total inversions (O(n^2) fine).
2. c[j][v] = number of positions k<j with a[k]<v (short table, 5001x5002).
3. For each i<j with a[i]>a[j]: x = (c[j][a[i]]-c[i+1][a[i]]) - (c[j][a[j]+1]-c[i+1][a[j]+1]).
4. new = I-2x-1; track min and its count.
5. Pairs with a[i]<a[j] only increase inversions (a better swap is guaranteed).

name: Colorings and Dominoes
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: n x m board (nm <= 3e5) with white cells; each white cell colored red or blue. Value of a coloring = max dominoes where horizontal dominoes cover two red cells and vertical ones two blue cells. Sum values over all 2^w colorings mod 998244353.
key_idea: Rows and columns are independent: a red horizontal run contributes floor(len/2), counted greedily as 'pair ends at cell j when the red streak ending at j has even length'.
solution:
1. Horizontal dominoes only use red, vertical only blue, so total = sum over horizontal runs + vertical runs.
2. In a run, greedy left-to-right pairing: a domino ends at cell j iff cells ...j are red with an even-length streak ending at j.

4. Each such ending at position j of a run contributes f[j]*2^(w-j) (other cells free). Precompute G[L] = sum_{j=2..L} f[j]*2^(w-j).

name: Cactus

nearest_infosys_question: Q0906 Layer-Split Path
brief: In a vertex cactus (each vertex in at most one simple cycle), answer k queries: the number of distinct simple paths from x to y, mod 1e9+7. n,m,k<=1e5.
key_idea: Shrink each cycle to one node to get a tree; every cycle on the x-y tree path doubles the number of paths, so the answer is 2^(number of cycle nodes on the path).

1. DFS. On a back edge u->v (v an ancestor), walk the parents from u up to v and label all of them with a new cycle component.
2. Every other vertex gets its own component. Edges between different components (bridges) form a tree.
3. BFS the tree from the root: cnt[c] = cnt[parent] + isCycle[c]. Build binary lifting for LCA.
4. For a query, a=comp[x], b=comp[y], l=LCA: k=cnt[a]+cnt[b]-2cnt[l]+isCycle[l]. Print 2^k.
complexity: O((n+q) log n) time, O(n log n) space

name: Coin Troubles
nearest_infosys_question: Q0307 Powers of 2 and 5 subset product 10^z
brief: Count coin-count vectors (n<=300 types, values a_i) summing to t (<=1e5), subject to q constraints 'count[b] > count[c]' (all b distinct, all c distinct). Mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: The constraints form disjoint chains. Substitute differences: each node's effective value becomes the prefix sum of values along the chain from its head, and each non-last chain node forces a minimum that is subtracted from t. Then run an unbounded knapsack count.
solution:
1. Build next[b]=c. Heads are the nodes that never appear as a c. If some node is not reachable from a head, there is a cycle: answer 0.
2. Walk each chain from its head: cur += a[v], set a'[v] = cur, and if v is not last, t -= cur (forced +1 in the strict chain). If t<0 at any point, answer 0.
3. Count the unbounded-knapsack ways to make t with the values a': dp[s] += dp[s-a'].
4. Output dp[t].

name: Prefix GCD
tags: brute force, dp, greedy, math, number theory
nearest_infosys_question: Q0441 Min operations to make GCD of array multiple of K (similar)
brief: Rearrange the array to minimise the sum of prefix gcds. Sum n and sum max a are <= 1e5.
key_idea: Start with the minimum element, then greedily append the element that gives the smallest new gcd. The gcd at least halves each step, so after O(log) steps it reaches the global gcd G, and the remaining terms are all G.
solution:
1. G = gcd of everything. g = min(a), sum = g.
2. While g != G: g = min over x of gcd(g,x); add g to sum; used++.
3. sum += (n - used) * G.
4. Each round is O(n log), and there are at most ~17 rounds.
complexity: O(n log^2 A) time, O(1) extra

name: Looking at Towers (easy version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0328 Vaccine dose scheduling count
brief: Count the subsequences of a (n<=5000) whose set of heights visible from the left and set visible from the right equal those of a. Mod 998244353.
key_idea: Left part: f[i] = ways to pick the left-record chain ending at index i (a_i = the next record value), where optional elements between consecutive records must be <= the previous record. Symmetric g from the right. Join at the first and last chosen maximum, with 2^(gap) free middle elements.
solution:
1. L = the record values from the left. f[i]=1 if a_i == L[0].
2. From j (value L[t]) to i>j with a_i = L[t+1]: f[i] += f[j] * 2^(#k in (j,i) with a_k <= a_j).
3. Compute g the same way on the reversed array (right records).
4. Answer = sum over i<=j with a_i = a_j = max of f[i]*g[j]*(i==j ? 1 : 2^(j-i-1)) (everything between is <= max).

g at 8 = 1 (via the 3).
Answer 5*1 = 5.

brief: On a huge strip, n traffic lights at p_i turn red at times l*k+d_i; each second you turn around if standing on a red light, then move one cell. For each start (facing right at time 0), decide if you eventually leave the strip.

name: Ralph and Mushrooms
nearest_infosys_question: Q0381 Graph + DP OA problem
brief: On a directed graph (1e6 nodes and edges), the i-th pass over an edge collects its mushrooms and then lowers the count by i. Starting from s, maximize the mushrooms collected.
key_idea: Inside an SCC every edge can be passed until it is empty, which gives full(w) = (t+1)w - t(t+1)(t+2)/6 with t the max t such that t(t+1)/2 <= w. Between SCCs each edge is used once. So condense, then take the longest path in the DAG from comp(s).
solution:
1. Run an iterative Tarjan from s (only the reachable part matters).
2. inner[c] += full(w) for edges inside c. Edges between components go into a DAG list.
3. Tarjan's component ids are in reverse topological order, so process c=0..C-1: best[c] = inner[c] + max(best[b] + w).
4. Print best[comp[s]].

name: Speedrun

nearest_infosys_question: Q0379 Min-K Longest Path in DAG
brief: Quest j can only be done at hours ≡ h_j (mod k), and the DAG dependencies a<b require a's time <= b's time. Minimize (last completion time - first completion time).
key_idea: Earliest times: t_v = max(h_v, t_u + ((h_v-h_u) mod k)). Then try every 'first quest': go through the sources in increasing h, and after evaluating each one, delay that source by one day and propagate the increase. Each node is pushed back at most once, so the total work is O(n+m).
solution:
1. t = h. Since a<b, a pass in index order is topological: t_v = max(t_v, t_u + (h_v-h_u) mod k).
2. mx = max t. Sort the sources (in-degree 0) by h.
3. For each source s: ans = min(ans, mx - h_s). Then set t_s = h_s + k and BFS-propagate the increases, updating mx.
4. Print ans.

name: Binary Strings and Blocks
nearest_infosys_question: Q0254 Binary strings without K consecutive 1s, first!=last
brief: A binary string is beautiful if removing exactly one block (maximal run) leaves an odd number of blocks. Count strings of length n where every given substring [l_i, r_i] is beautiful, mod 998244353.
key_idea: With k blocks you can reach k-1 (remove an end) or k-2 (remove a middle block), so beautiful <=> k >= 2 <=> the substring is not constant; count strings where no constraint interval lies inside one run.
solution:
1. ml[r] = max l over intervals ending at r.
2. f[j] = ways where a new run starts at j (f[1]=2 for the first character's choice).
3. Run [k, j-1] is valid iff every interval with r <= j-1 has l < k, i.e. k > M_j = max ml[r] for r <= j-1 (monotone).
4. f[j] = sum f[k] for k in [M_j+1, j-1] via prefix sums; answer = same sum with j = n+1.

name: Ilya and Roads
nearest_infosys_question: Q0301 Checkpoint problem (segments + DP)
brief: n<=300 holes and m<=1e5 company segments [l,r] each with cost c (overlap gives no discount). Find the min cost to fix at least k holes, or -1.
key_idea: Precompute w[l][r] = the min cost of a segment covering [l,r]. dp[i][j] = min cost over the first i holes with exactly j fixed, where the last block of fixed holes is [l..i].
solution:
1. w[l][r] = min c of segments exactly [l,r], then propagate w[l][r] = min(w[l][r], w[l-1][r], w[l][r+1]) so it covers [l,r].
2. dp[i][j] = min(dp[i-1][j] (hole i unfixed), min over l of dp[l-1][j-(i-l+1)] + w[l][i]).
3. Iterate l from i downwards and stop when the block length exceeds j.
4. Answer = min over j>=k of dp[n][j], or -1.

name: Moon Craters
nearest_infosys_question: Q0278 Machine subset with stability < position
brief: n<=2000 craters (intervals [c-r,c+r] on a line). Pick the largest subset where every pair is nested or disjoint (touching allowed), and print the indices.
key_idea: A laminar family: f[i] = 1 + the best disjoint packing of the intervals inside i. Packing inside a range is a 1-D DP over compressed coordinates, processing intervals by increasing length.
solution:
1. Compress the endpoints and list the intervals by their right endpoint.
2. Process intervals by length. For interval i: h[x] = max(h[x-1], h[L_j] + f[j]) over intervals j ending at x with L_j >= L_i. Then f[i] = 1 + h[R_i].
3. The final answer is the same packing over the whole coordinate range.
4. Reconstruct by backtracking the h array, recursing into each chosen interval.
complexity: O(n * (n + coords)) = O(n^2) time, O(n) extra per call

name: Cleaning
nearest_infosys_question: Q0518 Minimum balls to reset box strengths
brief: Piles a_i in a row; an operation removes one stone from each of two adjacent non-empty piles. With at most one swap of adjacent piles beforehand, can all stones be removed? Sum n <= 2e5.
key_idea: Without a swap, clearing from the left forces p_i = a_i - p_{i-1} >= 0 with p_n = 0. Precompute prefix leftovers and suffix leftovers; each swap (i,i+1) only changes a local O(1) check.
solution:
1. p[i] = a_i - p[i-1] (BAD if negative or the previous is BAD). Similarly s[i] = a_i - s[i+1] from the right.
2. No swap works if p[n-1]==0.
3. For a swap at (i,i+1): L=p[i-1], R=s[i+2]. The new order is a_{i+1}, a_i: x = a_{i+1}-L >= 0, y = a_i - x >= 0, and we need y == R.
4. YES if any swap works.

name: Winter is here

key_idea: For each d: the subsets of multiples of d have total size k*2^(k-1). Subtract the exact-gcd values of the multiples of d (processing d descending) to get the exact gcd = d contribution.
solution:
1. k_d = the number of elements divisible by d (harmonic loop).
2. f(d) = k_d * 2^(k_d - 1): the sum of sizes over non-empty subsets of the multiples.
3. g(d) = f(d) - sum of g(m) over multiples m=2d,3d,... (computed from large d to small).

name: Yunli's Subarray Queries (hard version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0797 Next greater on right not seen on left, with updates (XOR of query answers)
brief: f(b) = min point changes so b has k consecutive values each one more than the previous. For queries (l,r) with r >= l+k-1 output sum_{j=l+k-1..r} f(a[l..j]).
key_idea: With b_i = a_i - i, the cost of window s is c_s = k - (max frequency of b in [s, s+k)); the query is a sum of prefix minima of c over [l, r-k+1], answered offline by sweeping l leftwards with range-assign / range-sum.

4. Answer = range sum over [l, R].
complexity: O((n + q) log n) time, O(n) space

name: Cyclic Permutations
nearest_infosys_question: Q0152 Permutations with Condition Around Maximum
brief: For a permutation, connect each index to the nearest larger element on its left and on its right. Count permutations of length n (n <= 1e6) whose graph has a cycle, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Acyclic permutations are exactly the unimodal ones (increase then decrease), and there are 2^(n-1) of them (each value except n goes left or right of the peak). Answer = n! - 2^(n-1).
solution:
1. fact = n! mod p.
2. pw = 2^(n-1) mod p.
3. Answer = (fact - pw + p) % p.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0309 Fuzzy Grid
brief: 2 x n grid with values in [1,2n]. Count pairs (l,r), 1<=l<=r<=2n, such that a right/down path from (1,1) to (2,n) exists using only cells with values in [l,r].
key_idea: Each path turns down at some column k; it uses top prefix 1..k and bottom suffix k..n, so it works iff l <= mn_k and r >= mx_k. For each l take the smallest mx_k among k with mn_k >= l.

4. For each l with R(l) finite add 2n - R(l) + 1 (R(l) >= l automatically).
5. Sum as long long.

name: Beavermuncher-0xFF
tags: dfs and similar, dp, dsu, greedy, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0917 Count tree colorings with B nodes at distance >= K
brief: A tree with k_i beavers per vertex. A machine starting at s eats one beaver each time it enters a vertex (it can't enter an empty one) and must return to s. Maximise the beavers eaten. n<=1e5.
key_idea: Bottom-up: each child trip costs one beaver at v on return. Visit the children in descending order of value while v has beavers, then use the remaining beavers for back-and-forth bounces with the children's leftovers (+2 each).
solution:
1. Root at s. For v != s, available = k_v - 1 (one eaten on entry) and the base gain is 1. For s, available = k_s.
2. Sort the children by dp desc. For each while available > 0: total += dp[c] + 1 (the return eats one at v), available--.
3. Bounces: b = min(available, sum of children leftovers), total += 2b, available -= b.
4. dp[v] = total, left[v] = available. The answer is dp[s]. Use long long and iterative order (n=1e5).
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

nearest_infosys_question: Q0296 Hotel customers minimum unhappiness (Chef Monocarp)
brief: Repeatedly colour a middle element j between i<j<k with a_i=a_k (all three uncoloured). Maximise the number of coloured elements. n<=2e5.
key_idea: Use segments [first, last] of each value. In each connected union of segments covering length len with a minimum chain of cnt segments, you can paint len - cnt - 1 elements. Find cnt with a greedy max-reach jump (like interval cover).
solution:
1. last[v] = the last index of value v.
2. Scan i: start a component at L=i with cur=last[a_i] (skip singletons).
3. Greedy: scan j up to cur, tracking best = max last[a_j]. If best > cur, use one more segment (cnt++) and set cur = best. Repeat.
4. ans += (cur-L+1) - (cnt+1). Continue from cur+1. (Brute-force verified.)

[5,7] has length 3 and chain 1, giving 3-2 = 1.

name: Ezzat and Grid
nearest_infosys_question: Q0320 Stock Trader's Alternating Streak (one mulligan)
brief: n rows given as column segments of 1s (columns up to 1e9). Delete the fewest rows so that every two consecutive remaining rows share a column with 1 in both. Print the deleted rows.
key_idea: A longest chain DP: dp[i] = 1 + max dp[j] over earlier rows j sharing a column. A segment tree over compressed columns supports range 'chmax' assignment and range max of the pair (dp, row).
solution:
1. Compress all segment endpoints.
2. For row i: best = max over its segments of the tree query (dp, row). dp[i] = best.dp+1, prev[i] = best.row.
3. Then range-chmax all of row i's segments with (dp[i], i).
4. Rebuild the chain from the overall best row. Delete every row not on it (count n - length).
complexity: O((n+m) log m) time, O(m) space

name: Tourism
tags: dfs and similar, dp, dsu, graphs, greedy, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0909 Tree Beautiful Set
brief: Connected graph with city scores. Starting at s, walk without immediately reusing the last road. Maximise the sum of distinct cities visited. n,m<=2e5.
key_idea: Repeatedly peel degree-1 vertices (except s). Everything left can be fully visited with a return. Peeled parts are hanging trees, of which you can enter only one at the end, so add the best root-to-leaf chain.
solution:
1. Queue all leaves != s. Pop v: mark it removed, chain[v] = w[v] + best[v].
2. For each non-removed neighbour u: best[u] = max(best[u], chain[v]). Decrement deg[u]; push u if it becomes a leaf and u != s.
3. Answer = sum of w over non-removed vertices + max over non-removed u of best[u].
4. If the graph is a tree, only s remains: answer = w[s] + best chain.

The sum of all weights is 2+2+8+6+9 = 27.

name: Priority Queue
tags: combinatorics, dp, implementation, math, ternary search
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: A sequence of '+x' / '-' (remove the minimum) operations, n<=500. Sum, over all 2^n subsequences, of the sum of the multiset left at the end. Mod 998244353.
key_idea: Contribution technique: for each insert x, count the subsequences where x survives. dp[j] = ways with j elements 'smaller than x' present, breaking ties by index.
solution:
1. Fix insert i (it must be taken). Scan the other operations.
2. '+y' smaller (y<x, or equal with an earlier index): take moves j to j+1, skip keeps it. Larger: both choices keep j (x2).
3. '-': skip keeps j. Take with j>0 gives j-1. Take with j=0: allowed before i (it removes nothing relevant), forbidden after i (it would remove x).
4. Add x * sum(dp) to the answer.
dry_run:

x=1 survives in subsequences: those containing +1 without the final '-' (2*2 = 4), so 4*1 = 4.
x=2 survives in 6 subsequences: 6*2 = 12. Total 16.

name: Mocha and Stars
tags: combinatorics, dp, fft, math, number theory
nearest_infosys_question: Q0915 Splitting Cities into Realms (subsets with prime component count)
brief: Count integer tuples a_i in [l_i,r_i] (n<=50) with sum <= m (<=1e5) and gcd = 1, mod 998244353.
key_idea: Möbius over the gcd: answer = sum_d mu(d) * #(tuples of multiples of d with sum <= m). The count for d is a bounded knapsack on b_i = a_i/d with sum <= m/d, using prefix sums.
solution:
1. Sieve mu up to m.
2. For each d with mu(d) != 0: S = m/d, b_i in [ceil(l_i/d), floor(r_i/d)] (skip if empty).
3. dp over items: nd[s] = sum of dp[s-hi..s-lo] via prefix sums.
4. Add mu(d) * sum(dp) to the answer.
complexity: O(n * m log m) time, O(m) space

name: Card Game
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: Deck of n suits x m ranks (m even) split evenly between two players. Suit 1 beats other suits; same suit higher rank beats lower. Count splits where player 1 can match each of player 2's cards with a beating card, mod 998244353.
key_idea: Each non-trump suit is a bracket sequence where player 2 may end with surplus e (to be beaten by trumps); trump suit is a bracket sequence where player 1 ends with surplus E = total of those surpluses.
solution:
1. w[e] = number of length-m +/-1 paths that never go negative and end at e (ballot numbers via O(m^2) DP).
2. In suit s != 1 scan ranks from low to high: player 2's card opens, player 1's card closes (must match an earlier lower card, so never negative); final balance e = player 2's unmatched cards, count w[e].
3. dp over suits 2..n: dp[a+e] += dp[a]*w[e] (total surplus <= m).
4. Answer = sum_E dp[E] * w[E] (trump suit, scanned the same way with roles swapped, leaves player 1 exactly E spare trumps).
dry_run:
n=1, m=4: only suit 1, need surplus 0: w[0] = Catalan(2) = 2.
Answer 2 (matches).
n=2, m=2: w = [1, -, 1] -> dp = w; sum dp[E]*w[E] = 1*1 + 1*1 = 2 (matches).

name: Shohag Loves Inversions
nearest_infosys_question: Q0309 Fuzzy Grid
brief: Start with [0,1]; repeatedly insert k = current inversion count anywhere. Count distinct arrays of length n (n <= 1e6) mod 998244353.
key_idea: Once k exceeds every element, inserting k anywhere but the end creates a new k' > all elements; so d[i] = i * sum_{j>i} d[j] + 1, and the early phase (k <= 1) contributes n-1 arrays plus ((m-2)(m-1)/2 - 1) ways to enter the big phase at length m.
solution:
1. Big phase: d[i] = i * (suffix sum of d over j > i) + 1 (the +1 = keep inserting at the end until length n).
2. Small phase: arrays of form 0,..,0,1,..: n-1 of them stay small to the end.
3. Entering the big phase at length m (first insertion of a 1 before some 1... ) can be done in (m-2)(m-1)/2 - 1 ways.
4. Answer = (n-1) + sum_{m=3..n} ((m-2)(m-1)/2 - 1) * d[m], computed backwards with a running suffix sum.
complexity: O(n) time per test, O(1) extra space

name: Valid Bitonic Permutations
tags: combinatorics, dp, implementation, math, number theory
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: Count bitonic permutations of 1..n (strictly up to a peak at 2..n-1, then down) with B_i = x and B_j = y, mod 1e9+7 (n <= 100).
key_idea: Build the permutation by placing values 1..n-1 in increasing order, each at the leftmost or rightmost free slot; value n fills the last slot, which must not be an end.
solution:
1. dp[l] = ways with l values placed on the left (v-1-l on the right).
2. Value v goes to slot l+1 (left) or n-(v-1-l) (right).
3. A placement is allowed iff (pos==i) == (v==x) and (pos==j) == (v==y).
4. Finally n goes to slot l+1, which must lie in [2, n-1] and satisfy the same check; sum dp[l].

name: Small Permutation Problem (Easy Version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: Given a_1..a_n, count permutations p where for each i the prefix p_1..p_i contains exactly a_i values <= i, mod 998244353.
key_idea: View p as rooks on an n x n board; a_i = rooks in the top-left i x i square, and going from i-1 to i adds row i and column i; free rows = free columns = (i-1) - a_{i-1}.
solution:
1. If a_n != n -> 0.
2. For each i: d = a_i - a_{i-1}, fr = (i-1) - a_{i-1}; if d not in {0,1,2} or fr < 0 -> 0.
3. d = 0: factor 1 (no rook in the new L-strip).
4. d = 1: rook in new row (fr columns), new column (fr rows) or corner (i,i): 2*fr + 1.
5. d = 2: one in row i and one in column i: fr^2. Multiply all factors.

name: Railguns
tags: brute force, dfs and similar, dp, graphs
nearest_infosys_question: Q0378 Longest increasing path in matrix
brief: Move from (0,0) to (n,m) (n*m <= 1e4): each second go down, right or stay. r <= 100 railgun shots each hit a whole row or column at the end of a given second. Earliest safe arrival time or -1.
key_idea: Time-layered reachability: you never need more than n+m+r seconds (each shot costs at most one wait), so propagate the reachable set second by second and clear shot lines.
solution:
1. cur = {(0,0)} at t=0.
2. For t = 1 .. n+m+r: nx = cur (stay) plus down/right moves from cur.
3. Clear every cell on rows/columns shot at second t.
4. If (n,m) is in nx, answer t; otherwise continue. Never reached -> -1.

name: Arthur and Brackets
nearest_infosys_question: Q0877 Lexicographically maximum string after removing duplicates (hashed)
brief: For each of n <= 600 opening brackets (left to right) the distance to its matching closing bracket must lie in [l_i, r_i]. Output any correct bracket sequence of length 2n satisfying this, or IMPOSSIBLE.
key_idea: Closing the innermost open bracket as early as allowed never hurts: at each position close the stack top if its distance >= l, else open the next bracket; fail if a top overshoots r or nothing remains to open.
solution:
1. Stack of (open position, index).
2. At position pos: if top exists and pos - open >= l[top]: if also > r[top] -> IMPOSSIBLE, else write ')' and pop.
3. Otherwise open the next bracket (if none left -> IMPOSSIBLE) after checking the top has not already exceeded r.
4. At the end the stack must be empty.

name: Alyona and the Tree
tags: dfs and similar, dp, graphs, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0910 Tree delete edge maximize degree score
brief: Rooted tree (root 1) with vertex values a_u and edge weights (possibly negative). Vertex v is sad if some u in its subtree has dist(v,u)>a_u. Remove leaves repeatedly until no vertex is sad; minimize removed leaves.
key_idea: u must be deleted (with its subtree) iff max over ancestors v of dist(v,u) > a_u; that max is a Kadane-style best = max(0, best_parent + w).
solution:
1. DFS from root carrying best = max path sum ending at current vertex from some ancestor: best_u = max(0, best_parent) + w(parent,u) (track max(0,..) for starting fresh).
2. If best_u > a_u, u is sad-causing: cut its whole subtree (don't descend).
3. Count kept vertices; answer = n - kept.
4. Use iterative DFS and long long.

name: Choosing Capital for Treeland
tags: dfs and similar, dp, graphs, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0910 Tree delete edge maximize degree score
brief: A tree of n cities with directed roads; choosing a capital requires reversing roads so all cities are reachable from it. Output the minimum number of reversals and all optimal capitals.
key_idea: Rerooting: compute reversals for root 1, then moving root across edge u->v changes the count by +1 if the edge points u->v, else -1.
solution:
1. Store each undirected edge with weight 0 if it points away (u->v as given) and 1 if it points toward u.
2. BFS/DFS from 1: cost[1] = sum of weights of edges in direction parent->child (1 means needs reversing).
3. For child v of u via weight w: cost[v] = cost[u] + (w==0 ? 1 : -1).
4. Output min cost and all vertices achieving it in increasing order.

Root 1: edge 1-4 ok (0), 4-2 needs reversal (1), 4-3 (1) -> cost 2.
To 4 (edge 1->4, w=0): cost 3; to 2 and 3 (edge toward 4 from them, w=1 from 4's view): 3-1=2.
Min 2 at 1 2 3 (matches).

name: Two Hundred Twenty One (easy version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0309 Fuzzy Grid
brief: String of n charges +1/-1; for each query [l,r], min number of rods to remove so the alternating sum s_l - s_{l+1} + ... of remaining rods is 0.
key_idea: Answer is only 0, 1 or 2: 0 if alternating sum is 0, 1 if segment length is odd, else 2.
solution:
1. p[i] = p[i-1] + sign_i * (i odd ? 1 : -1) (prefix of alternating sum).
2. For query: S = p[r]-p[l-1] (sign flip doesn't matter for zero test).
3. If S==0 -> 0. Else if (r-l+1) odd -> 1 (removing one suitable rod always works: the running sum changes by +-1 steps). Else -> 2 (remove last rod to get odd length, then 1 more).

name: You Are Given a Decimal String...
nearest_infosys_question: Q0372 Graph shortest paths (Floyd-Warshall)
brief: An x-y counter starts at 0, prints its last digit, then adds x or y. Given printed string s (starts with '0', |s|<=2e6) with some digits erased, for every 0<=x,y<=9 output the min number of digits to insert (or -1), as a 10x10 table.
key_idea: Only consecutive digit pairs matter: count cnt[a][b]; for each (x,y) BFS over 10 digit states gives min steps between digits.
solution:
1. cnt[a][b] = number of adjacent pairs (s_i, s_{i+1}) - at most 100 kinds.
2. For each (x,y): dist[a][b] = min number of additions (>=1) to go from digit a to digit b, moving a->(a+x)%10 or (a+y)%10 (BFS/Floyd on 10 nodes).
3. Answer = sum cnt[a][b]*(dist[a][b]-1); if some cnt>0 has dist=INF -> -1.
4. Note a->a needs >=1 step (cycle), so compute dist as shortest path with at least one edge.

name: Queries for Number of Palindromes
nearest_infosys_question: Q0881 Magical Vine (alternating P/Q prefix pattern)
brief: String s (|s|<=5000) and up to 1e6 queries [l,r]: count palindromic substrings (by position) of s[l..r].
key_idea: pal[l][r] by interval DP, then 2D inclusion-exclusion cnt[l][r]=cnt[l+1][r]+cnt[l][r-1]-cnt[l+1][r-1]+pal[l][r].
solution: 1) pal[l][r] = s[l]==s[r] && (r-l<2 || pal[l+1][r-1]). 2) Process l from n-1 down to 0, r from l up to n-1. 3) cnt[l][r] as above (cnt with l>r is 0). 4) Answer each query in O(1). 5) Memory: int cnt 5000x5000 = 100MB OK; pal can be two rolling rows; use fast IO.
dry_run: Sample s=caaaba, query 1..4 'caaa': palindromes c,a,a,a,aa,aa,aaa = 7. cnt via recurrence matches 7.

name: Omsk Metro (simple version)
tags: data structures, dfs and similar, dp, graphs, greedy, math, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0267 Hero Duel Intensity
brief: Tree grows by '+ v x' (new vertex with weight x in {-1,1}); queries '? 1 v k': is there a contiguous (possibly empty) subsegment of the path 1..v with sum k?
key_idea: With +-1 weights, achievable subsegment sums form a contiguous range [minSub, maxSub] (0 included); maintain Kadane values along the root path for each vertex.
solution: 1) For each vertex store: maxEnd (best sum ending here, >=0 allowing empty), maxAll, minEnd (<=0), minAll. 2) Root (weight 1): maxEnd=1,maxAll=1,minEnd=0,minAll=0. 3) New vertex w child of p with weight x: maxEnd[w]=max(0,maxEnd[p]+x), maxAll[w]=max(maxAll[p],maxEnd[w]); minEnd[w]=min(0,minEnd[p]+x), minAll[w]=min(minAll[p],minEnd[w]). 4) Query: YES iff minAll[v] <= k <= maxAll[v].

name: Mr. Kitayuta, the Treasure Hunter
tags: dfs and similar, dp, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0301 Checkpoint problem (segments + DP)
brief: Islands 0..30000 with gems. Start at 0, first jump d, each next jump is l-1, l or l+1 of the previous (positive). Maximize gems collected on landed islands.
key_idea: Jump length can deviate from d by at most ~245 (1+2+...+245 > 30000), so dp[position][length - d + 250] fits in memory.
solution: 1) gem[p] counts. 2) dp[p][o] = max gems arriving at p with last jump length d + o - 250; -1 = unreachable. dp[d][250] = gem[0] + gem[d]. 3) For p ascending, each reachable (p,o): for dl in -1..1: L = len + dl; if L >= 1 and p+L <= 30000: dp[p+L][o+dl] = max(.., dp[p][o] + gem[p+L]). 4) Answer = max over all dp.

name: A BIT of an Inequality
nearest_infosys_question: Q0324 Ordinary Numbers (binary string XOR pairs)
brief: Count tuples x<=y<=z with f(x,y) xor f(y,z) > f(x,z), where f(l,r) is XOR of a_l..a_r (n<=1e5).
key_idea: f(x,y)^f(y,z) = f(x,z)^a_y, and P^a_y > P iff the highest bit h of a_y is 0 in P = f(x,z); count segments containing y with bit h of their XOR equal to 0.
solution:
1. Prefix xor p_0..p_n; f(x,z) = p_z ^ p_{x-1}.
2. For each bit b keep prefix counts of how many p_i (i=0..j) have bit b = 0/1.
3. For y with top bit h: left indices i in [0,y-1], right indices j in [y,n]; segments with bit h zero = L0*R0 + L1*R1.
4. Sum over y (long long).

name: Good Trip
nearest_infosys_question: Q0338 Great Ball Chains
brief: There are k excursions. Each picks one of the n(n-1)/2 pairs uniformly at random. A friend pair contributes its current value f, and that value then increases by 1. Find the expected total, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Use linearity of expectation. With P=n(n-1)/2, at excursion j (0-based) a given friend pair is chosen with probability 1/P and has expected value f + j/P. Summing gives a closed form.
solution:
1. S = sum of f_i mod p. P = n(n-1)/2. inv = P^{-1} mod p.
2. Answer = k*S*inv + m*inv^2*(k(k-1)/2).
3. Reduce every term mod p, and compute k(k-1)/2 as an integer before taking mod.
4. m=0 gives 0.
dry_run:
Sample n=3, m=1, k=2, f=1: P=3.
k*S/P = 2/3. m*(1/9)*1 = 1/9. Sum = 7/9, which is 777777784 (matches).
Sample n=2, k=10, f=1: P=1, so 10+45=55 (matches).

name: Bank Hacking
tags: constructive algorithms, data structures, dp, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0911 Sum of Distances in Tree
brief: Hacking a bank raises the strength of online banks within distance 2 (through online banks) by 1. Each later hack must be adjacent to an offline bank. Find the minimum computer strength that hacks the whole tree.
key_idea: The answer is mx, mx+1 or mx+2. If you start at u, u's neighbours gain 1 and everything else gains at most 2. Try every u and check whether all the maximum-valued nodes (and the mx-1 nodes) lie in u's closed neighbourhood.
solution:
1. Count cM = nodes with value mx and cM1 = nodes with value mx-1.
2. For each u, count m = how many max nodes are in {u} plus its neighbours.
3. If m==cM: the answer is mx when u is the unique max and every mx-1 node is a neighbour of u; otherwise mx+1.
4. If no u works, the answer is mx+2.

So the answer is 5 (matches). Samples 2 and 3 (93 and 8) also verified.

name: Permutation Sum
nearest_infosys_question: Q0324 Ordinary Numbers (binary string XOR pairs)
brief: Count ordered pairs of permutations (a,b) of length n<=16 such that c_i=((a_i-1+b_i-1) mod n)+1 is also a permutation, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Fix b = identity by relabeling (multiply by n!); count a with (a_i+i) mod n distinct via bitmask backtracking offline, then hardcode the 16 values.
solution:
1. For any fixed b the count of valid a is the same, so answer = n! * T(n), T(n) = #a with a_i+i (mod n) all distinct.
2. T(n)=0 for even n (sum argument).
3. Compute T for odd n offline by DFS over positions with two bitmasks (used values, used sums); n=15 runs in seconds locally.
4. Hardcode table: 1,3,15,133,2025,37851,1030367,36362925 for n=1,3,...,15.
complexity: O(1) at runtime (table); offline backtracking exponential

n even -> 0.

name: Subsequences (easy version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0509 Playing with MEX
brief: String s (n,k<=100). Pick k distinct subsequences; cost of each is n-|t|. Minimum total cost or -1.
key_idea: Take subsequences from longest to shortest; BFS from s deleting one char at a time visits them in non-increasing length.
solution:
1. BFS from s with a set of seen strings.
2. Pop a string: take it (cost n-|t|), stop after k.
3. Push every unseen string obtained by deleting one character.
4. If the queue empties before k strings -> -1.
(Hard version needs a counting DP of distinct subsequences per length.)

name: Maple and Tree Beauty (Hard Version)
tags: bitmasks, brute force, dfs and similar, dp, fft, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0270 Split array into two subsequences with equal sum and equal count
brief: Rooted tree, label vertices 0/1 with exactly k zeros. Beauty = LCS length of all root-to-leaf label strings. Maximize beauty (n ≤ 2e5).
key_idea: Answer is d (min leaf depth) if levels 1..d can each be made uniform: subset-sum of level sizes must fit k zeros and n−k ones; otherwise d−1.
solution:
1. BFS depths; d = minimum depth of a leaf; cnt[x] = vertices at depth x ≤ d; T = Σcnt.
2. Need subset sum s of cnt[1..d] with T-(n-k) ≤ s ≤ k (deeper vertices absorb the rest).
3. Subset sum with bitset; group equal counts and use binary splitting (Σcnt ≤ n -> O(√n) distinct).
4. Answer d if achievable else d-1.

name: Round Subset
nearest_infosys_question: Q0915 Splitting Cities into Realms (subsets with prime component count)
brief: Choose exactly k of n<=200 numbers (<=1e18) to maximise the trailing zeros of their product.
key_idea: Trailing zeros = min(#2, #5); knapsack dp[j][fives] = max twos using j numbers.
solution:
1. Count t (factors of 2) and f (factors of 5) per number (f <= 25).
2. dp[j][s] = max total twos with j chosen numbers and s total fives (-1 = impossible).
3. Iterate items, j downward: dp[j][s] = max(dp[j][s], dp[j-1][s-f] + t).
4. Answer = max over s of min(s, dp[k][s]).
complexity: O(n * k * 25n) ~ 2e8 simple ops, O(k * 25n) space

name: Treasure Hunting
nearest_infosys_question: Q0281 Array Minimization Game
brief: n x m grid, start at (1,1); k treasures. You may move left/right, and up only in one of q safe columns; never down. Minimum moves to collect all treasures.
key_idea: Per treasure row you finish at its leftmost L or rightmost R; between rows go up through the nearest safe column left or right of where you stand.
solution:
1. For each row keep L[r], R[r] of treasures; skip rows with none (row 1 without treasures: L=R=1).
2. Row 1: dL = (R-1)+(R-L) (end at L), dR = R-1 (end at R).
3. Next treasure row r from end position p: for c in {nearest safe >= p, nearest safe <= p} (lower_bound): base = d + |p-c| + (r-last).
4. End at L: base + |c-R| + (R-L); end at R: base + |c-L| + (R-L).
5. Answer min(dL, dR) after the last treasure row. Use long long.
complexity: O((k + n) log q) time, O(n + q) space

name: Generational Triplets
nearest_infosys_question: Q0662 Count pairs A^B<=X with D | A+B
brief: Count triples 1<=a<b<c<=n in arithmetic progression with a xor b xor c = 0, mod 1e9+7, for n up to 1e18 (t up to 1e4).
key_idea: c=2b-a and c=a^b together give b = 2*(a & ~b). So b is determined bit by bit from a (b_{i+1} = a_i AND NOT b_i). Run a digit DP from the LSB tracking a<b and c<=n.
solution:
1. Use a^b = a+b-2(a&b) = 2b-a, which gives b = 2(a-(a&b)) = 2(a&~b). So b_0=0 and b_{i+1} = a_i & !b_i, and c = a^b.
2. Digit DP over bits i=0..62 from low to high. State: (b_i, cmp(a,b) of the low bits, cmp(c,n) of the low bits, a!=0).
3. Choose a_i (0/1, with bits > 60 forced to 0) and compute c_i=a_i^b_i. A higher differing bit overrides the comparison.
4. Count the final states with b's carry 0, a<b, c<=n and a>0. Since c>b>a, all values are <= n.

solution:

2. From the boat's side pick i fifties and j hundreds (i+j>=1, 50i+100j<=k). The number of ways is C(cntA,i)*C(cntB,j).
3. BFS: on first discovery set dist=d+1. If dist==d+1, add ways[cur]*multiplicity.
4. If the target is unreached, print -1 and 0.

name: The Unbearable Lightness of Weights
nearest_infosys_question: Q0214 Fence panels with one custom panel
brief: n indistinguishable weights with known masses (n, a_i <= 100). With one query (k,m) you are shown some k weights summing to m. Find the max number of weights whose masses you can determine.
key_idea: You learn k weights for sure only if k copies of a value v is the unique multiset of size k with sum k*v. Count multisets with a bounded knapsack capped at 2. With <= 2 distinct values the answer is n.
solution:
1. If there are <= 2 distinct masses, ask for all copies of one value: everything is identified, so the answer is n.
2. dp[k][s] = number of distinct multisets (capped at 2) with k items and sum s, using a bounded knapsack per distinct value (use j copies, 0..cnt).
3. For each value v with count c and k=1..c: if dp[k][k*v]==1 the answer is >= k.
4. The answer is the max such k (at least 1).
complexity: O(n * n * S) with S = sum a <= 1e4, fast in practice

brief: b_i = a_{i mod n} for i<l (l up to 1e18). Count non-decreasing subsequences of length 1..k taking one element from each of consecutive blocks of n (n*k<=1e6). Mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Consecutive picks come from consecutive blocks, so a length-j sequence is a non-decreasing chain over j copies of a. dp[j][i] = ways ending at a_i, placed in (q-j+1) full-block windows, plus the windows ending in the partial last block.

2. dp[1][i]=1. dp[j][i] = sum of dp[j-1][i'] with a[i'] <= a[i] (sort by value, prefix sums, equal values grouped).
3. For j<=min(k,q): add (sum_i dp[j][i]) * ((q-j+1) mod p).
4. For j<=min(k,q+1): add sum over i<r of dp[j][i] (sequences ending in the partial block).
5. Note: the comparison uses the raw a values (both samples check out).
complexity: O(n*k + n log n) time, O(n) space

solution:

3. Extend to neighbours u > s not in mask: dp[mask|1<<u][u] += dp[mask][v].

name: Balanced String
nearest_infosys_question: Q0307 Powers of 2 and 5 subset product 10^z
brief: Binary string (|s|<=100). Minimise the swaps so that the number of '01' subsequences equals the number of '10' subsequences.
key_idea: #01 + #10 = c0*c1, so balanced means #01 = c0*c1/2. Choose the positions of the c1 ones by DP over (ones placed, #01 so far), counting ones placed on original-0 positions (each such 1 needs one swap).
solution:
1. Target T = c0*c1/2.
2. dp[j][x] = min mismatches after scanning a prefix, with j ones placed and x '01' pairs.
3. At position i, placing a 1 adds z = i - j zeros before it: dp[j+1][x+z] = dp[j][x] + (s_i=='0'). Placing a 0 keeps the state.
4. The answer is dp[c1][T].

name: Multiplicative Arrays
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: For each x in 1..k (k <= 1e5) count arrays of length 1..n (n <= 9e8) with elements in [1,k] and product x, mod 998244353.
key_idea: At most 16 elements are > 1; count ordered factorizations g[j][x] into j factors >= 2, then place the 1s: sum over lengths of C(len, j) = C(n+1, j+1).
solution:
1. g[1][x] = 1 for x >= 2; g[j][x*y] += g[j-1][x] for y >= 2 (harmonic loop), j <= 17.
2. Hockey stick: sum_{len=1..n} C(len, j) = C(n+1, j+1), computed with j+1 factors and a modular inverse.
3. ans[1] = n; ans[x] = sum_j g[j][x] * C(n+1, j+1).
complexity: O(k log k * 17) time, O(17k) space

key_idea: Union equal values in the same row/column with DSU, then process cells by increasing value: each component gets 1 + max of current row/column maxima of its cells.
solution:
1. For each row and column sort cells; union neighbours with equal values.
2. Sort all cells by value; process equal-value groups together.
3. For a group: component value = max over its cells of max(rowMx[r], colMx[c]) + 1.
4. Assign, then update rowMx and colMx with the new values.
5. Print results.

name: Ela and the Wiring Wizard
tags: brute force, dp, graphs, greedy, implementation, shortest paths
nearest_infosys_question: Q0370 Graph traversal with restricted moves
brief: Connected multigraph (n <= 500, m <= 2.5e5) with weighted wires. A spell on wire (u,v) detaches it from v and reattaches it as (u,t) for any neighbour t of v, costing w_i. Minimize total spell cost plus travel time from 1 to n.
key_idea: Use a single edge of weight w for everything: each spell or traversal costs w, so answer = min over edges of w * (minimum number of moves to make it join 1 and n, plus 1 traversal), with moves counted by unweighted hop distances (Floyd).
solution:
1. Floyd-Warshall on hop counts d (every edge = 1).
2. For edge (u,v,w): option A: slide ends to 1 and n: d(1,u) + d(v,n) + 1 (or swapped).
3. Option B: move one end to some y (d(u,y) or d(v,y)), make a self-loop at y (+1), then stretch to 1 and n: + d(y,1) + d(y,n), + 1 traversal.
4. Answer = min over edges of w * best count. Use long long.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0659 Pick two distinct numbers whose GCD is not prime
brief: f(w) = number of permutations of 0..n-1 where MEX i is achieved by some subarray iff w_i = 1. Given s over {0,1,?} and c, choose ? to minimize f(w) not divisible by c; print it mod 1e9+7 or -1.
key_idea: Removing the largest value keeps all smaller conditions, and MEX i is achievable iff value i lies outside the span of 0..i-1, i.e. at an end of the length-(i+1) array: f(w) = prod_{i=1}^{n-1} (w_i ? 2 : i-1), needing w_1 = w_n = 1.
solution:
1. If c = 1, or s_1 = '0' or s_n = '0' -> -1 (f = 0 is divisible by c).
2. Cheapest: '?' at i=2 -> factor 1, at i >= 3 -> factor 2.
3. Write c = 2^e * c'. Base is divisible iff v2(base) >= e and c' divides its odd part (compute mod c').
4. Since factors only get larger, the only fix is to drop the 2-adic valuation below e: switch r = v2 - e + 1 '?' at even i >= 4 (factor i-1 odd) choosing the smallest i; not enough -> -1.
5. Output the product mod 1e9+7.
complexity: O(n) time per test, O(n) space

name: A Prime Flood (Easy Version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: Array a (n <= 3000, a_i <= n). An operation picks a prime p and decrements every element divisible by p. f(b) = the largest value all elements of b can be made equal to. Sum f over all non-empty subsequences mod 998244353.
key_idea: (Found by brute force.) f depends only on (min a, max b) of the subsequence. A greedy gives it: if b has a prime not dividing a, decrement b alone; otherwise (rad(b) | a) decrement both. This is a table G[a][b] = G[a][b-1] or G[a-1][b-1]. Then count subsequences per (min, max) pair.
solution:
1. rad[] by sieve; G[b][b] = b; for a < b: G[a][b] = (a % rad[b] != 0) ? G[a][b-1] : G[a-1][b-1].
2. c[v] = counts and pre = prefix counts.
3. Single value u: (2^{c_u} - 1) * u.
4. u < v: (2^{c_u}-1)(2^{c_v}-1) * 2^{#values strictly between} * G[u][v].
5. Sum mod p.
complexity: O(MX^2) table plus O(n^2) per test (sum n <= 3000)

name: Elections in Saransk (hard version)
tags: combinatorics, dp, dp, dp, math, number theory
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: n voters, voter i picks a divisor p_i of a_i (a_i, x <= 5e5). Count arrays p with x * lcm(p) = product(p), mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Per prime q the condition becomes sum(e_i) - max(e_i) = v_q(x), and the choices factorize over primes. For each prime count exponent vectors with e_i <= v_q(a_i) by fixing the max M: [t^{M+c}] prod(1+..+t^{min(b_i,M)}) minus the same with M-1.
solution:
1. SPF sieve; factor each a_i and collect the caps b_i per prime; factor x into c_q.
2. A prime of x with no a_i divisible by it -> answer 0.
3. For each prime: s = sum over M = 0..max b of coef(M, M+c) - coef(M-1, M+c), each coef a truncated product computed with sliding-window sums.
4. Answer = the product of the s values.
complexity: O(sum over primes of (#caps) * maxb * (maxb + c)), about 1e8 worst

nearest_infosys_question: Q0317 Optimal run-length encoding after deletions
brief: String S (|S| <= 5000) is a concatenation of distinct words in alphabetical order. Split S into the maximum number of strictly increasing words and print them.
key_idea: f(i,j) = max words for S[i..] whose first word is S[i..j). With lcp[i][j], the valid next ends k (S[j..k) > S[i..j)) form a suffix range k >= k0. So f(i,j) = 1 + G[j][k0], where G is a suffix max, giving O(n^2) with short arrays.

3. For i descending: G[i][j] = max(G[i][j+1], f(i,j)), with f(i,n) = 1.
4. Answer G[0][1]; reconstruct by scanning for a matching f value.

brief: Rooted binary tree (vertex 0 -> 1, others have 0 or 2 children). Bob walks: leaf -> parent; internal empty -> write L go left; L -> write R go right; R -> erase, go parent. For every start k, output time to reach vertex 0 (mod 1e9+7).
key_idea: From v, Bob fully traverses v's subtree in 2*size(v)-1 seconds and leaves it clean; at each untouched ancestor he does the same, so tau_v = tau_parent + 2*size(v) - 1.

brief: n items with prices c_i and tags showing c_i. Pick integer x>=2, new price ceil(c_i/x). Each item whose new price has no remaining matching old tag needs a new tag costing y. Maximize sum of new prices - y*(new tags).
key_idea: For fixed x, items with new price v are those with c in [(v-1)x+1, vx]; reused tags for value v = min(count, freq[v]). Harmonic loop over x.
solution: 1) freq[v] = count of c_i = v; prefix counts P. 2) For x = 2..max(2,C) (C = max c): for v = 1..ceil(C/x): k = count of c in ((v-1)x, vx]; sum += v*k; reused += min(k, freq[v]). 3) income = sum - y*(n - reused). 4) Answer max over x. 5) long long; total work sum C/x = O(C log C).
complexity: O(C log C) per test, O(C) space

name: Infinite Set
tags: bitmasks, dp, math, matrices, number theory, strings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0137 Count subsets with XOR less than K
brief: Set S contains given distinct a_i, and is closed under y -> 2y+1 and y -> 4y. Count elements of S below 2^p, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: 2y+1 appends 1 bit, 4y appends 2 bits; after removing a_i that are generated by smaller a_j, count of descendants with exactly t extra bits is Fibonacci(t).
solution: 1) Sort a; keep a set of kept values. For each x: reduce y=x repeatedly (y odd -> (y-1)/2, y%4==0 -> y/4, else stop); if some y in kept set, x is redundant. 2) f[0]=f[1]=1, f[t]=f[t-1]+f[t-2]; prefix F[t]=sum f[0..t]. 3) For each kept x with bit length L <= p: ans += F[p-L]. 4) Mod 1e9+7.
complexity: O(n log a log n + p) time
dry_run: Sample a={6,1}, p=4: 1 has L=1 -> F[3]=1+1+2+3=7; 6 (L=3) not reducible to 1 -> F[1]=2. Total 9.

name: Math Division
nearest_infosys_question: Q0282 Buckets Probability
brief: x given as n-bit binary. Each step replaces x by floor(x/2) or ceil(x/2) with probability 1/2 each until x = 1. Expected number of steps mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Steps = (n-1) + [a carry propagates into the top bit]; track the probability of carry while processing bits from the LSB.
solution: 1) P = probability carry = 1 (start 0); inv2 = (M+1)/2. 2) For bits i = 0..n-2 from the LSB with bit b: if carry 0: b=1 -> carry 1 w.p. 1/2; b=0 -> carry 0. If carry 1: b=0 (sum 1, odd) -> carry 1 w.p. 1/2; b=1 (sum 2) -> carry 1 surely. 3) newP = (1-P)*[b==1]*inv2 + P*(b==1 ? 1 : inv2). 4) Answer = (n-1) + P mod M (if top becomes 2 one more step).

name: Jon Snow and his Favourite Number
nearest_infosys_question: Q0096 Longest Fibonacci-like subsequence (Maximum sub array satisfying condition)
brief: n strengths a_i (<=1000), number x (<=1000). k times: sort strengths, XOR every 1st, 3rd, 5th... with x. Output max and min after k operations.
key_idea: Values stay below 1024, so simulate each operation on a count array in O(1024) instead of sorting.
solution: 1) cnt[v] for v < 1024. 2) Each operation: pos = 0 (elements passed so far); for v ascending: c=cnt[v]; xored = (pos even) ? (c+1)/2 : c/2; nc[v^x] += xored; nc[v] += c - xored; pos += c. 3) cnt = nc. 4) After k ops print largest and smallest v with cnt>0.

name: Floor of MEX (Hard Version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0254 Binary strings without K consecutive 1s, first!=last
brief: a_k = MEX of {floor(y/k) : y in A} for k=1..n, for a hidden A subset of {0..n-1}. Count subsets B with the same array a, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: a_k fixes: each block [jk, jk+k-1] for j < a_k must contain an element of B, and block [a_k k, a_k k+k-1] must be empty; count subsets with forbidden points and 'interval must be hit' constraints via DP on the last chosen position.
solution: 1) For each k: forbid positions in [a_k*k, a_k*k+k-1] (clip to n-1; use a difference array). For j < a_k add a must-hit interval [jk, min(jk+k-1, n-1)]: need[r] = max left end over intervals ending at r. Total intervals O(n log n). 2) DP state = last chosen position (or none). cnt[none]=1, sum=1, low pointer = -1. 3) For p=0..n-1: if p not forbidden: cnt[p] = sum (choose p), sum *= 2 effectively (sum += cnt[p]). Then for constraint L=need[p]: kill all states < L (move low pointer, subtract). 4) Answer = sum.

name: Sum of Progression
tags: brute force, data structures, dp, implementation, math
nearest_infosys_question: Q0067 Array rotation with prefix sums
brief: For each query (s,d,k), compute sum_{i=1..k} i * a[s+(i-1)d]. n<=1e5, q<=2e5.
key_idea: Split by step size around sqrt(n). For a large d, k <= n/d is small, so loop directly. For a small d, use stride-d suffix sums and weighted suffix sums, grouping the queries by d.
solution:
1. Let B=sqrt(n). If d>B, sum directly; this takes O(n/d) steps.
2. For each small d that has queries: suf[i]=a_i+suf[i+d], and w[i]=suf[i]+w[i+d], which equals sum of a_j times its 1-based position counted from i.
3. With e=s+d*k, the answer is w[s]-w[e]-k*suf[e]. Treat indices > n as 0.
4. Use long long, since values reach about 1e8*1e5*1e5/2.
complexity: O((n+q) sqrt n) time, O(n+q) space
dry_run:
Sample a=1 2 3 4 5, query (1,2,3): terms 1*1+2*3+3*5=22.
d=2: suf[1]=1+3+5=9, w[1]=9+(3+5)+5=22. e=7 is out of range, so w[e]=suf[e]=0.
Answer 22 (matches).

name: Goblin
tags: dfs and similar, dp, dsu, greedy, math
nearest_infosys_question: Q0267 Hero Duel Intensity
brief: Build an n x n grid where row i is s with its i-th character flipped. Find the largest 4-connected component of 0-cells.
key_idea: A '0' column j splits into a top block (rows < j, size j-1) and a bottom block (rows > j, size n-j). A '1' column has just its diagonal 0. Join these pieces between neighbouring columns with a weighted DSU.
solution:
1. Nodes per column: for '0', T_j (weight j-1) and B_j (weight n-j). For '1', D_j (weight 1).
2. Neighbouring '0' columns j and j+1: union T_j with T_{j+1}, and B_j with B_{j+1}.
3. A '1' column j: union D_j with B_{j-1} if column j-1 is '0', and D_j with T_{j+1} if column j+1 is '0'.
4. The answer is the largest component weight. Use long long, since it can reach about n^2/2.

The component {B1,B2,D3,T4} has weight 3+2+1+3=9 (matches).

name: Two Chess Pieces
tags: dfs and similar, dp, greedy, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0394 Longest trip after moving one road (tree diameter)
brief: Two pieces start at root 1 of a tree. Piece 1 must visit set a and piece 2 must visit set b, the distance between them must stay <= d at all times, and both must end at the root. Minimize the total steps.
key_idea: When piece 2 goes to a node x, piece 1 must at least reach x's d-th ancestor, and the reverse holds too. Add those ancestors to each piece's required set. Then each piece costs 2 times the number of edges in the union of root paths to its required nodes.
solution:
1. Run an iterative DFS that keeps the current root path, so anc[v] = path[depth-d], or the root if v is shallower than d.
2. req1 = a plus anc(b). req2 = b plus anc(a).
3. For each piece, in reverse DFS order: if req[v] is set and v != root, mark its parent and add 2.
4. Output the total for both pieces.

req1 = {3, anc2(4)=1}: the edge 1-3 costs 2.
req2 = {4, anc2(3)=root}: edges 2-4 and 1-2 cost 4.
Total 6 (matches).

brief: n rays (n<=1e6) enter through holes in order x and exit through holes in order y. Find the largest group of rays that all pairwise intersect.
key_idea: Two rays cross iff entry order and exit order disagree; list exit positions in entry order and find the longest decreasing subsequence.
solution:
1. pos[y_i]=i (exit position of each ray).
2. b[i] = pos[x_i] for rays in entry order.
3. Answer = longest strictly decreasing subsequence of b = LIS of -b.
4. Patience sorting with lower_bound.

brief: Young diagram with n columns of non-increasing heights a_i (<=3e5). Max number of non-overlapping dominoes.
key_idea: Chessboard-colour the cells; for a Young diagram the answer equals min(#black, #white).
solution:

2. Sum black and white counts.
3. Answer = min(black, white) (each domino covers one of each, and Young diagrams achieve it).

name: Count Paths
tags: data structures, dfs and similar, dp, dsu, graphs, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0911 Sum of Distances in Tree
brief: Tree with coloured vertices (n<=2e5). Count paths (>=2 vertices) whose endpoints share a colour that no interior vertex has.
key_idea: One DFS with cnt[col] = number of same-colour vertices 'visible' from the current vertex; entering v adds cnt[c_v] to the answer.
solution:
1. Enter v: ans += cnt[c_v]; save old = cnt[c_v].
2. Before descending into each child: cnt[c_v] = 1 (only v is visible for its colour inside that subtree).
3. Leaving v: cnt[c_v] = old + 1 (v blocks its subtree's same-coloured vertices but is itself visible).
4. Iterative DFS to avoid stack overflow.

name: Watching Fireworks is Fun
nearest_infosys_question: Q0274 Maximum sum subset with index gap between a and b
brief: You stand on a street of n<=150000 sections and move at most d per unit time. m<=300 fireworks (a_i, b_i, t_i) give b_i - |a_i - x|. Maximize the total happiness.
key_idea: Maximizing sum(b) - sum|a-x| means minimizing sum|a_i - x_i|. Between fireworks you can move w=d*dt, so dp_new[x] = |a-x| + min of dp over [x-w, x+w], a sliding-window minimum done with a monotonic deque.
solution:
1. dp[x]=0 initially. sumb=0. prevT=1.
2. For each firework: w = min(n, (t-prevT)*d).
3. Sweep x=1..n with a deque window over [x-w, x+w]. nd[x] = dp[min] + |a-x|.
4. The answer is sumb - min(dp). Use long long and cap w at n to avoid overflow.

3-34 = -31, and the DP finds this optimum (matches).

name: Limited Edition Shop
nearest_infosys_question: Q0331 Gift Packing into K Boxes
brief: Alice and Bob each buy their favourite remaining item (by their own preference orders), with turns in any order. Over all reachable sets Alice can end with, maximize the total value of her items.
key_idea: Alice's set S is feasible iff no excluded y and included x have y before x in Alice's order but x before y in Bob's. Scan in Alice's order with state T = max Bob-position among excluded items. Including x needs posB(x) > T.
solution:
1. dp[T] over T in [0,n]. dp[0]=0, everything else -inf. Use a segment tree with range add, range max and point chmax. 2. For each item x in Alice's order with p=posB(x): m = max dp[0..p-1]. 3. Include x: add v_x to dp[0..p-1]. Exclude x: states T

=p must exclude x and stay unchanged. 4. The answer is max over all dp.

The max is 2 (matches). All 8 samples were verified.

name: Array Collapse
tags: data structures, divide and conquer, dp, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0297 Investment opportunities (non-overlapping range revenue)
brief: An operation deletes everything in a chosen segment except its minimum. Count the distinct arrays reachable from p (distinct values), mod 998244353.
key_idea: Two kept elements j<i can be adjacent in the result iff everything between them is > min(p_j,p_i). With L = previous smaller of i, every j in [L,i-1] works, and so does every j below L that is on the increasing monotonic stack. The ends need the prefix before the first kept element and the suffix after the last to be greater than it.
solution:
1. dp[i] = number of reachable kept-sequences ending at i. pre = prefix sums of dp. stsum = sum of dp over the stack.
2. Pop the stack while the top > p_i, subtracting from stsum.
3. If the stack is empty: dp[i] = 1 + pre[i] (i can be first). Else, with L = top: dp[i] = (pre[i]-pre[L]) + (stsum - dp[L]).
4. Push i. The answer is stsum at the end (the stack elements are exactly the valid last elements).
dry_run:
Sample 2 4 1 3:
i0 (2): the stack is empty, so dp=1. i1 (4): L=0, dp = dp[0..0] + (stack below L = 0) = 1.
i2 (1): it pops everything, so dp = 1 + (1+1) = 3. i3 (3): L=2, dp = dp[2] = 3.
The final stack is {1, 3}, so the answer is 3+3 = 6 (matches). The samples give 2, 6, 12 (verified).

name: The way home
tags: binary search, data structures, dp, graphs, greedy, shortest paths, sortings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0386 Graph + state DP (Hard)
brief: Directed flights, each with a cost s. You start at city 1 with p coins, and a performance in city i earns w_i. Find the minimum number of performances needed to reach city n, or -1.
key_idea: Perform lazily: only when the coins fall short, and then in the best-w city visited so far, crediting the performances retroactively. The state is (city, best city so far). Compare states lexicographically by (fewer performances, more leftover coins) and run Dijkstra on that order.
solution:
1. The state is (v, b), where b is the visited city with the largest w. Its value is the pair (perf, coins). Start at (1,1) with (0, p).
2. Pop the lexicographically smallest pair: fewer performances first, then more coins.
3. For an edge v→u costing s: if coins < s, add need = ceil((s-coins)/w_b) performances and need*w_b coins. Then subtract s.
4. The new best is nb = argmax(w_b, w_u). Relax state (u, nb) if the new pair is better.
5. The answer is the performance count of the first popped state with v==n, or -1.
complexity: O(n*m log(n*m)) per test, using the sums n≤800 and m≤1e4
dry_run:
w=[7,4,3,1], p=2. Edge 1→3 costs 8: perform 1×7 to get 9 coins, leaving 1.
3→2 costs 6: perform 1 more (best is still city 1), leaving 2. 2→4 costs 11: perform 2 more, leaving 5.
Total 4. Output 4 (matches).

name: Rearrange Brackets
tags: brute force, dp, greedy, sortings, strings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0488 Machine Cooling and Task Scheduling
brief: Cost of a regular bracket sequence = min total cost to erase it by removing adjacent '()' pairs, each costing the number of brackets to its right. With at most k <= 5 moves (take one bracket and reinsert it), keeping it regular, minimize the cost.
key_idea: Cost = sum over matched pairs of the number of pairs nested inside it; one move puts a '(' just before its ')', removing exactly that pair's inside count, so subtract the k largest.
solution:
1. Match brackets with a stack; for pair (o,i) inside count c = (i-o-1)/2.
2. Total cost = sum of all c (each pair is erased after everything inside it... equivalently sum of depths).
3. A move turning a pair into '()' decreases cost by its c; choices are independent.
4. Sort c descending and subtract the top k. Use long long.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

Total = 5.

name: Lucky Subsequence
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: Count index-subsequences of length exactly k where no lucky number (digits only 4 and 7) appears twice; unlucky values may repeat. Mod 1e9+7, n<=1e5.
key_idea: There are only 1022 lucky values <= 1e9. Run a knapsack over distinct lucky values (choose one occurrence or none), then multiply by C(unlucky count, k-j).
solution:
1. Count occurrences c_v of each lucky value v, and U = the number of unlucky elements.
2. dp[j] = ways to choose j distinct lucky values with one index each: dp[j] += dp[j-1]*c_v (iterate j downwards).
3. Answer = sum over j of dp[j] * C(U, k-j).
4. Precompute factorials for binomials mod p.
complexity: O(L^2 + n log) time with L <= 1022, O(n) space

dp after 4: [1,2]; after 7: [1,4,4].
Only j=2 counts: 4*C(0,0)=4. Answer 4.

name: Graph
tags: *special problem, binary search, dfs and similar, dp, math, ternary search
nearest_infosys_question: Q0393 Move 1 by reversing K-length subarrays with forbidden positions
brief: Assign real values to nodes so that every black edge's endpoints sum to 1 and every red edge's to 2, minimising the sum of |values|, or print NO. N<=1e5, M<=2e5.
key_idea: In each component every value is s_v*t + c_v (s=±1). An odd cycle pins t; otherwise minimise sum|t + s_v c_v| by taking t = the median.
solution:
1. BFS each component from root r with x_r = t (s=1, c=0). Across edge w: s_v=-s_u, c_v=w-c_u.
2. For a non-tree edge (u,v,w): if s_u+s_v=0, need c_u+c_v=w, else NO. Otherwise t=(w-c_u-c_v)/(s_u+s_v); it conflicts with a previously fixed t means NO.
3. If t is not fixed, choose t = median of (-s_v*c_v), which minimises sum |s_v t + c_v|.
4. Output x_v = s_v*t + c_v. Self-loops and multi-edges are handled by the same rule.

name: Discrete Centrifugal Jumps
nearest_infosys_question: Q0794 Longest Valid Parentheses
brief: Minimise the jumps from skyscraper 1 to n, where a jump i->j is allowed if j=i+1, or all buildings strictly between are lower than both ends, or all are higher than both. n<=3e5.
key_idea: The valid predecessors of i are exactly the elements popped from (and then the new top of) monotonic stacks. dp[i] = 1 + min dp over those.
solution:
1. dp[0]=0 and dp[i] = dp[i-1]+1.
2. Non-increasing stack: while h[top] < h[i], pop, and if the stack is non-empty, dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[top]+1) (everything between is lower). Then pop equal heights.
3. Symmetrically use a non-decreasing stack for 'between are higher'.
4. Push i onto both stacks. The answer is dp[n-1].

i=4 pops index 3, top is index 2: dp[4] = dp[2]+1 = 2.

name: Telepanting
tags: binary search, data structures, dp, sortings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0297 Investment opportunities (non-overlapping range revenue)
brief: An ant walks right from 0. Portals at x_i send it back to y_i<x_i when active (state toggles on each pass). Find the time to reach x_n+1, mod 998244353.
key_idea: dp[i] = the time from being teleported at portal i back to reaching x_i again = (x_i - y_i) + the sum of dp[j] for the portals with y_i < x_j < x_i (all of them are active then). Answer = x_n + 1 + sum of dp over the initially active portals.
solution:
1. Portals are sorted by x. For portal i, j = the first portal with x_j > y_i (binary search).
2. dp[i] = (x_i - y_i) + (pre[i] - pre[j]) mod p.
3. Each initially active portal triggers one extra loop of dp[i]. Inactive portals become active and are handled inside other dp values.
4. ans = (x_n + 1) + sum over s_i=1 of dp[i].
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

name: Vlad and the Nice Paths (hard version)
tags: binary search, combinatorics, data structures, dp, math, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0154 The Oracle of Eldoria
brief: Same as 1811G1 (count maximum-length nice paths: blocks of k same-colored tiles) but n <= 5000 with sum n^2 <= 2.5e7, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Same O(n^2) DP as G1 (last block ends at i, previous block ends at j, choose k-1 of the 'same' tiles between), but binomials from factorials instead of a table.
solution:
1. Precompute factorials and inverse factorials up to 5000.
2. len[0]=0, cnt[0]=1 (empty path).
3. For each i scan j = i-1 down to 0, same = #tiles of color c_i in (j, i); if same >= k-1: candidate len[j]+1 with cnt[j]*C(same, k-1).
4. Keep the max length and sum counts on ties; answer sums cnt over states of max length.

name: Compressed Tree
tags: dfs and similar, dp, graphs, greedy, sortings, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0917 Count tree colorings with B nodes at distance >= K
brief: Tree with values a_i (possibly negative). Repeatedly delete leaves (possibly everything), then compress degree-2 vertices. Maximize the sum of remaining vertex values.
key_idea: After compression exactly the kept vertices with degree != 2 count; dp[v] = best when v is kept and connected to its parent, depending on whether v has 0, 1 (compressed) or >= 2 kept children (then all extra positive children are free gains).
solution:
1. Sort children dp values descending: c0 >= c1 >= ...
2. dp[v] = max(a_v [leaf], c0 [degree 2, compressed], a_v + c0 + c1 + sum of positive c_i, i >= 2 [degree >= 3]).
3. v as the top vertex: max(a_v, a_v + c0, c0 + c1 [compressed], a_v + c0 + c1 + c2 + positive rest).
4. Answer = max over v of the top case, and 0 (delete all).
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
dry_run:
Test 1: star centre 2 (a=-2) with leaves 1,3,4 (1,2,1).
Centre as top with 3 children: -2 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 2; leaf 3 as top: 2 + dp[2] where dp[2] = max(-2, 1, -2+1+1) = 1 -> 3.
Answer 3 (matches). Verified vs brute force.

name: Captains Mode
nearest_infosys_question: Q0141 Ball Containers minimum cost
brief: n <= 100 heroes with strengths. A fixed sequence of m <= 20 actions, each a pick or ban by team 1 or 2. Both captains play optimally. Output team1 strength minus team2 strength.
key_idea: Only the m strongest heroes can ever matter. A pick should always take the strongest available hero; bans branch. dp[mask] over the used subset of the top m, with the action index = popcount(mask).
solution:
1. Sort strengths descending and keep the top m.
2. dp[full] = 0; process masks from large to small, with i = popcount(mask).
3. Pick by team T: j = the lowest free bit; dp = dp[mask|j] +/- s[j].
4. Ban: max (team 1) or min (team 2) over free j of dp[mask|j].
5. Answer dp[0].

name: Village Guilds
nearest_infosys_question: Q0910 Tree delete edge maximize degree score
brief: Rooted tree; a guild is the set of nodes in v's subtree at distance exactly h from v. Count distinct non-empty guilds.
key_idea: Each distinct guild is identified by its LCA: either a single node (h=0) or a node v with at least two child subtrees reaching that depth; v contributes (second-largest child max-depth) - depth(v).

1. depth[i]=depth[p_i]+1 (p_i<i so process in increasing order).
2. md[v] = max depth in subtree, computed for i=n..2: update parent's top-two child values (b1,b2) with md[i].
3. Answer = n + sum over v of max(0, b2[v] - depth[v]) where b2 is the second-largest child md.
4. Use long long.

brief: Array with values 0..63; count non-empty subsequences whose bitwise AND has exactly k set bits, mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: dp[v] = number of subsequences (so far) with AND equal to v; only 64 states.
solution:
1. dp[0..63]=0.
2. For each a_i: ndp=dp (skip a_i); for each v: ndp[v & a_i] += dp[v]; ndp[a_i] += 1 (subsequence starting here).

name: Anya Loves Trees!
tags: dfs and similar, dp, greedy, trees, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0910 Tree delete edge maximize degree score
brief: Rooted tree (root 1); leaves hold distinct values 1..k. Children start in increasing index order and you may cyclically rotate any vertex's child list. Can leaves (left to right) become 1,2,...,k?
key_idea: Every subtree's leaves must form a contiguous value range; at each node the children's ranges, read in index order, must chain consecutively after some cyclic rotation.
solution:
1. Build children lists (iterate i=2..n so lists are in index order); get a BFS order to process bottom-up.
2. Leaf: lo=hi=a_v, cnt=1. Internal: lo=min, hi=max of children, cnt=sum.
3. Require hi-lo+1 == cnt (contiguous).
4. Start from the child with smallest lo and walk cyclically: each next child's lo must equal previous child's hi+1; else NO.
5. If all nodes pass -> YES.

name: Phone Number
nearest_infosys_question: Q0205 Count number-line paths with exactly k jumps
brief: Masha's number s (<=50 digits). New number: first digit any 0..9; digit i = average of s_i and new digit i-1, rounded up or down when not integer. Count distinct new numbers, excluding s itself if it can be produced.
key_idea: dp[i][d] = number of ways (= distinct prefixes) with new digit d at position i; each choice sequence gives a different number.
solution:
1. dp[0][d]=1 for d=0..9.
2. For i>=1 and prev d: sum = s_i + d; if even -> dp[i][sum/2] += dp[i-1][d]; else add to both sum/2 and sum/2+1.
3. Total = sum dp[n-1][*] (use long long; up to 10*2^49).
4. Check if s itself is producible: for every i>=1, s_i must be floor or ceil of (s_i + s_{i-1})/2. If yes subtract 1.
complexity: O(10 n) time, O(10 n) space

brief: n<=18 dishes with value a_i; choose and order exactly m distinct dishes; k rules give bonus c if x is eaten immediately before y. Maximize total.
key_idea: dp[mask][last] = best satisfaction having eaten set mask ending with dish last.
solution: 1) dp[1<<i][i]=a[i], others -1 (unreachable). 2) For each mask, last in mask with dp valid, for j not in mask: dp[mask|1<<j][j]=max(.., dp[mask][last]+a[j]+bonus[last][j]). 3) Answer = max dp[mask][last] with popcount(mask)==m. 4) long long (values up to 1e9*18 + bonuses).
