name: Felicity's Big Secret Revealed
nearest_infosys_question: Q0391 Shortest unique paths to open door with keys
brief: Binary string of length n <= 75. Make k+1 cuts (k >= 1) so the k pieces read as binary numbers; the cut is valid if the set of numbers is exactly {1..m} for some m. Count valid cuts mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: With at most 75 bits, m <= 20, so every piece value must be in 1..20 (leading zeros allowed). dp[i][mask] counts ways where the last cut is at gap i and mask is the set of values used.
solution:
1. dp[i][0] = 1 for every i (the first cut can go anywhere).
2. From (i, mask) extend j = i..n-1 and build val; stop once val > 20; skip val == 0.
3. dp[j+1][mask | 1<<(val-1)] += dp[i][mask].
4. Answer = sum over i >= 1 and m in 1..20 of dp[i][(1<<m)-1].

name: Travelling Salesman and Special Numbers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0134 Count k in [L,R] with k & X = X
brief: Operation: replace x by popcount(x). x is special if it needs exactly k operations to reach 1. Count special numbers in [1, n], n given in binary (<= 1000 bits), mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: After one step x becomes <= 1000, so precompute steps[c]; count numbers <= n with popcount c where steps[c] == k-1 via a binary digit walk with binomials.
solution: 1) k==0 -> answer 1 (only x=1). 2) steps[1]=0, steps[c]=steps[popcount(c)]+1 for c<=1000. 3) cnt(c) = numbers in [1,n] with exactly c set bits: walk bits of n; at each '1' at position i (L = bits after it), add C(L, c - ones_so_far); at the end add 1 if popcount(n)==c. 4) Answer = sum over c>=1 with steps[c]==k-1 of cnt(c). 5) If k==1 subtract 1 (x=1 has popcount 1 but needs 0 steps).
dry_run: Sample n=110 (6), k=2: c with steps[c]=1 is c=2. Numbers <= 6 with 2 bits: 3,5,6 -> 3.

name: White Lines
tags: brute force, data structures, dp, implementation, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0297 Investment opportunities (non-overlapping range revenue)
brief: In an n x n B/W grid (n<=2000), one k x k eraser click turns a square white. Maximize the number of rows and columns that are fully white.
key_idea: Row i becomes white exactly when the click (r,c) satisfies i-k+1<=r<=i and R_i-k+1<=c<=L_i. That set is a rectangle of click positions, so add 1 over it with a 2D difference array. Do the same for columns.
solution:
1. For each row, find its leftmost and rightmost black cells L and R. If it has none, base++. Else if R-L+1<=k, add +1 to the click rectangle [i-k+1..i] x [R-k+1..L], clamped to [1,n-k+1].
2. Do the same for each column with its top and bottom black cells.
3. Take the 2D prefix sums of the difference array.
4. Answer = base + max over clicks.

At (2,2) the count is 4 and base=0, so the answer is 4 (matches).

nearest_infosys_question: Q0306 Divisible by K (base permutations)
brief: Binary n x m matrix (n<=m, nm<=1e6). Make every even-sided square contain an odd number of 1s with the fewest flips, or -1.
key_idea: n>=4 is impossible (a 4x4 is four 2x2s, odd+odd+odd+odd = even); for n<=3 only 2x2 squares matter -> DP over columns with column bitmask states.
solution:
1. n>=4 -> -1; n==1 -> 0.
2. Column masks (2^n states); cost of state s in column j = popcount(s ^ original column).
3. Transition p->s allowed iff every vertical pair of rows i,i+1 has odd count of ones across both columns.
4. dp over columns; answer min of last column.

name: Games with Rectangle

brief: Players alternately draw a rectangle strictly inside the previous one (no shared points), k moves total, starting from n x m. Count distinct final pictures mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: Horizontal and vertical sides are independent: k nested rectangles need 2k distinct interior horizontal lines and 2k vertical ones -> C(n-1,2k)*C(m-1,2k).
solution:
1. Pascal triangle up to 1000.
2. If 2k > n-1 or 2k > m-1 -> 0.
3. Answer C(n-1,2k) * C(m-1,2k) mod p.

name: Max Median
nearest_infosys_question: Q0120 Minimum K for Longest Path in Permutation DAG
brief: Array a (n<=2e5). Maximise the median (lower median) over subarrays of length >= k.
key_idea: Median >= x iff some window of length >= k has more elements >= x than < x: map to +1/-1 and test with prefix sums + running prefix minimum.
solution:
1. Binary search x in [1,n].
2. b_i = +1 if a_i >= x else -1; prefix sums P.
3. For r >= k: mn = min(mn, P[r-k]); if P[r] - mn > 0 -> feasible.
4. Largest feasible x is the answer.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

nearest_infosys_question: Q0317 Optimal run-length encoding after deletions
brief: Fill the '*' in c (|c|<=1000) with letters to maximise (occurrences of s) - (occurrences of t), with |s|,|t| <= 50.
key_idea: DP over positions with the KMP automaton states of both s and t; +1 when s's automaton completes, -1 when t's completes.
solution:
1. Build the KMP transition tables go_s[state][letter] and go_t.
2. dp[x][y] = best score with automaton states x (for s) and y (for t). Start dp[0][0]=0.
3. For each character (all 26 letters if '*'): nx=go_s[x][l], ny=go_t[y][l], add (nx==|s|)-(ny==|t|).
4. The full-match state transitions via the failure link, so overlapping occurrences are handled.
5. The answer is the max over the final states.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0280 Travelling Salesman DP
brief: For each a_i (n<=1e6, a_i<=4e6), output any array element x with a_i & x = 0, or -1.
key_idea: SOS (sum over subsets) DP: best[mask] = some array element that is a submask of mask. The answer for a is best[~a].
solution:
1. best[x]=x for each element; otherwise -1. Use 22 bits (4e6 < 2^22).
2. For each bit b, for each mask containing b: if best[mask]<0, take best[mask ^ (1<<b)].
3. For a_i print best[(2^22-1) ^ a_i]. Since a_i>=1 it can't match itself (a&a=a != 0).

name: LIS of Sequence
tags: data structures, dp, greedy, hashing, math
nearest_infosys_question: Q0266 Mountain Array Transformation
brief: For each index, decide whether it belongs to no LIS (1), some but not all LIS (2), or every LIS (3). n<=1e5.
key_idea: f[i] = the LIS length ending at i, g[i] = the LIS length starting at i. i is on some LIS iff f+g-1 == L. It is on every LIS iff it is the only such index with that f value.
solution:
1. Compute f with patience sorting (lower_bound, strict).
2. Compute g on the reversed array with negated values (strictly decreasing from the right).
3. L = max f. Count, for each f value, the indices with f+g-1 == L.
4. Group 1 if not on an LIS; group 3 if its f-level count is 1; else group 2.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

nearest_infosys_question: Q0911 Sum of Distances in Tree
brief: A tree is good if it is the intersection graph of some set of segments. Given a tree (n <= 3e5), find the largest good connected subtree.
key_idea: Segment intersection trees are caterpillars: a spine path plus leaves attached; size = sum over spine of (deg-1) + 2, so find the max-weight path with weight deg(v)-1.
solution:
1. val(v) = deg(v) - 1 (using degrees in the whole tree: all neighbours of a spine vertex can be included).
2. Root the tree; down[v] = val(v) + max child down.
3. best = max over v of val(v) + top two child down values.
4. Answer best + 2 (the two spine ends' outer neighbours). Use BFS order to avoid recursion.

name: Submedians (Easy Version)
tags: binary search, data structures, dp, greedy, math
nearest_infosys_question: Q0297 Investment opportunities (non-overlapping range revenue)
brief: Array a (1<=a_i<=n) and k. v is a submedian if it is a median of some subarray of length >= k. Output the largest submedian and a subarray (l,r) of length >= k where it is a median.
key_idea: Binary search v: map a_i>=v to +1 else -1; v is 'reachable' iff some subarray of length>=k has sum>=0. The largest such v is exactly a median of that subarray.
solution:
1. check(v): b_i=+1 if a_i>=v else -1, prefix P. For r=k..n keep min P[0..r-k] (and its index); if P[r]-min>=0 return (idx+1,r).
2. check is monotone (smaller v is easier); binary search the max v in [1,n] (v=1 always works).
3. Why it is a median: at least ceil(m/2) elements are >= v, and since v+1 fails, more than floor(m/2) elements are <= v.
4. Print v, l, r.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

name: The Contest
nearest_infosys_question: Q0335 Maximum triplets (equal or consecutive)
brief: Problems 1..n are split among 3 contestants; finally contestant 1 must hold a prefix, 2 a middle block, 3 a suffix (blocks may be empty). Each move transfers one problem. Min moves.
key_idea: Maximise problems that stay put: scan positions with state = current block (non-decreasing 1->2->3), +1 when the owner matches the block.
solution:

2. d[s] = max kept so far with position p in block s.
3. nd[s] = max(d[0..s]) + (own[p]==s).
4. Answer n - max(d).

brief: Fit the longest run of consecutive words into r lines of width c (r*c<=1e6, n<=1e6), preserving order, and print the banner.
key_idea: With two pointers, nx[i] = the first word after a line starting at word i. Apply nx r times from every start using binary lifting (repeated squaring of the function) and pick the start maximising the words covered.
solution:
1. Two pointers: maintain the window length (words + single spaces). nx[i] = j, where the words [i,j) fit in c. A too-long word gives nx[i]=i.
2. Compute res = nx^r by repeated squaring of the mapping (O(n log r) time, O(n) memory).
3. Choose the start i maximising res[i]-i.
4. Print up to r lines from i, stopping at an empty line.
complexity: O(n log r + total length) time, O(n) space

name: Keyboard Purchase
nearest_infosys_question: Q0306 Divisible by K (base permutations)
brief: Arrange the first m<=20 letters on a 1-D keyboard to minimise the sum of |pos(s_i) - pos(s_{i+1})| over a password of length n<=1e5.
key_idea: The sum of distances equals the sum over cut points of the adjacent-pair weight crossing the cut. dp[mask] = best cost after placing the set mask in the first |mask| positions; each step adds cross(mask).
solution:
1. c[x][y] = the number of adjacent pairs (x,y) in s, symmetric, ignoring x==y.
2. cross(mask) = sum of c[x][y] with x in mask and y not in mask. Compute it incrementally from mask without its lowest bit in O(m).
3. dp[mask | x] = min(dp[mask] + cross(mask)) for x not in mask.
4. The answer is dp[full].

name: The Maths Lecture
nearest_infosys_question: Q0653 Special Prime Pairs
brief: Count n-digit numbers x (n <= 1000, no leading zeros) having a suffix that is the decimal form of a positive y divisible by k (k <= 100), modulo m.
key_idea: Build x from the last digit; dp[r] = suffixes with value mod k = r that contain no valid y yet; the first time a nonzero digit makes the remainder 0, all remaining higher digits are free.
solution:
1. dp[0] = 1 (empty suffix); p10 = 10^i mod k.
2. Position i from the right: digit d (1..9 at the top position, else 0..9); nr = (r + d*p10) % k.
3. If d != 0 and nr == 0: a valid y exists -> add dp[r] * (ways to fill the rest: 9*10^(rest-1), or 1 at the top) to the answer.
4. Otherwise nd[nr] += dp[r]. Everything mod m.

brief: In a DAG with 0/1 edge weights, an unmemoized DFS from vertex 1 appends each edge's weight to Z before recursing (the sequence can be exponentially long). Count the inversions of Z mod 998244353.
key_idea: Summarise each vertex's generated sequence by (zeros, ones, inversions). Concatenating A then B gives inv = invA + invB + onesA*zerosB. Evaluate in reverse topological order, everything mod p.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0282 Buckets Probability
brief: Append 'a' with probability pa/(pa+pb), else 'b', until the string has >= k 'ab' subsequences. Find the expected number of 'ab' subsequences, as P*Q^-1 mod 1e9+7. k<=1000.
key_idea: dp[i][j] = the expected final count with i a's and j ab's so far. Once i+j >= k, the next 'b' ends it, and the expected extra a's before it is pa/pb, giving i+j+pa/pb. Leading b's are irrelevant, so start at dp[1][0].

2. For i from k down to 1 and j from k-1 down to 0: if i+j >= k, dp = i+j+pa/pb.
3. Otherwise dp[i][j] = A*dp[i+1][j] + B*dp[i][j+i].

key_idea: runs = 1 + #adjacent differing pairs; positions i<j are adjacent in exactly 2^i * 2^(n-1-j) subsequences, so the answer = 2^n - 1 + sum over differing pairs, maintained with BITs of 2^i and 2^(n-1-j) per character.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0152 Permutations with Condition Around Maximum
brief: Segment [1,n]: if its length is even split into two halves; if odd add the middle index m to the lucky value and recurse on [l,m-1] and [m+1,r]. Segments shorter than k are not processed. Output the final lucky value (n <= 2e9).
key_idea: Both halves always have the same length, and the right one is the left one shifted by an offset. So g(len) = (sum of midpoints, number of midpoints) for [1,len]; a shifted copy adds offset*count.
solution:
1. g(len): if len < k return (0,0).
2. If len even: (S,c) = g(len/2); return (2S + c*(len/2), 2c).

nearest_infosys_question: Q0338 Great Ball Chains
brief: Arrays a, b of length n<=2000; b' is a uniformly random permutation of b and c_i = a_i*b'_i. Output the expected number of inversions of c modulo 998244353.
key_idea: For a pair i<j, (b'_i, b'_j) is a uniform ordered pair of distinct indices (p,q), so E = (1/(n(n-1))) * sum_{i<j} #{p!=q : b_p/b_q > a_j/a_i}; sort all n(n-1) ratios once and binary search per pair.

4. total (fits in 64-bit) times inverse of n(n-1) mod M; n = 1 -> 0.
5. Work: n^2 log(n^2) ~ 1e8 comparisons, fine within 4 s.
complexity: O(n^2 log n) time, O(n^2) space

brief: Run programs a_1..a_n in order on two CPUs. A program costs hot if the same program was the last one on that CPU, and cold otherwise. Minimize the total time.
key_idea: One CPU always last ran a_{i-1}, so the state is just x = the other CPU's last program. Running on the same CPU adds a constant to every state (a lazy global offset). Running on the other CPU moves everything into state a_{i-1} with value min(globalMin + cold, dp[a_i] + hot).
solution:
1. dp[0] = cold[a_1] (0 means the other CPU is empty). Track off and mn.
2. For each i: cand = min(mn+off+cold[c], dp[c]+off+hot[c]).
3. off += (c==p ? hot : cold)[c]. Then dp[p] = min(dp[p], cand-off) and mn = min(mn, dp[p]).
4. The answer is mn+off.

brief: Build a BST over keys 1..n (n<=200) minimising sum c_ij * dist(i,j). Print each node's parent.

4. Use long long (sums up to ~4e13 * n).

3. For r inside child c's subtree (sz[c] roots): v's subtree becomes n - sz[c]; add sz[c] if n - sz[c] >= k.
4. For r outside v's subtree (n - sz[v] roots): v's subtree is sz[v]; add n - sz[v] if sz[v] >= k.
5. Sum over v in a 64-bit integer.

5. Answer for fish i is dp[1<<i]. For n=1 answer is 1.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0744 Delete subarray to minimize inversions
brief: For every cell of a binary grid (n*m <= 2.5e5), find the minimum area of a rectangle with four 1-corners that covers the cell, or 0 if there is none.
key_idea: Transpose so that n <= sqrt(nm). For each top row u, go through the bottom rows d from the bottom up. The columns where both rows are 1 give the best width for each column (between consecutive common columns). A running min over d >= current d gives the answer for row d, since a rectangle (u,d') covers row i iff u <= i <= d'.
solution:
1. If n>m, transpose.
2. For each u: cur[j]=INF. For d=n-1 down to u+1: find the common columns. For j between consecutive common columns c_k, c_{k+1}: w[j] = min(c_{k+1}-c_k+1).
3. cur[j] = min(cur[j], w[j]*(d-u+1)). ans[d][j] = min(ans[d][j], cur[j]).
4. After the d loop, ans[u][j] = min(ans[u][j], cur[j]). Print 0 for INF, transposing back.

brief: 3 x n grid with forbidden cells and one marked empty cell O. Count domino tilings of all other free cells in which at least one domino can slide into O. Mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: A move is possible iff some domino lies in line next to O (the 2 cells in a direction). Use inclusion-exclusion over the 4 directions: force those dominoes (mark the cells blocked) and count tilings with a column profile DP.
solution:
1. Treat O as blocked. For each non-empty subset S of {R,L,D,U}, block the 2 cells in each chosen direction (skip if one is outside or not free).
2. Count tilings: column DP with a 3-bit mask of cells pre-filled by horizontal dominoes from the previous column. Fill each column with vertical pairs or horizontals into the next column.
3. ans += (-1)^(|S|+1) * tilings.
4. The count with no forced domino is excluded, since at least one move is required.
complexity: O(16 * n * 8 * small) time, O(1) space

nearest_infosys_question: Q0325 Minimum-cost split into k segments
brief: Split n<=35000 cakes into exactly k<=50 contiguous boxes to maximise the sum of distinct types per box.
key_idea: dp_j[i] = max over p<i of dp_{j-1}[p] + distinct(p+1..i). A lazy segment tree over p holds dp_{j-1}[p] + distinct; moving to i adds +1 on p in [prev[i], i-1].
solution:
1. prev[i] = the last index before i with the same type (0 if none).
2. For each layer j: build a tree with value dp_{j-1}[p] at position p.
3. For i=1..n: range add +1 on [prev[i], i-1] (a_i is new for those segments), then dp_j[i] = max over [0, i-1].
4. Use -inf for unreachable states. The answer is dp_k[n].
complexity: O(k n log n) time, O(n) space

brief: Tree with n vertices. Count vertex subsets such that every simple path contains at most two chosen vertices, mod 998244353.
key_idea: dp[v] = number of non-empty antichains (no chosen vertex is an ancestor of another) in subtree(v) = prod over children (dp[c]+1). Answer = 1 + sum of dp[v].
solution:
1. Root at 1. dp[v] = prod_c (dp[c]+1): either v alone, or v unchosen with any non-empty combination of child antichains.

3. Case B: some chosen u has a chosen descendant. Then all other chosen vertices are below u (else a path w-u-x has 3), and they lie in ONE child subtree c (else x-u-y has 3) and form an antichain there -> sum over children dp[c].

key_idea: Let p be the first remaining occurrence at or after i; some cut q must overlap it (q in [p, p+|t|)), after which everything starting before q+|t| is gone: dp[i] = min/count over q of 1 + dp[q+|t|].

name: Inversion Graph Coloring (Hard Version)
tags: binary search, combinatorics, data structures, dp, two pointers
nearest_infosys_question: Q0745 Range Replace and Sum
brief: Count the subsequences (including the empty one) that can be 2-coloured so that every inversion pair gets different colours, i.e. those with no decreasing subsequence of length 3. Mod 1e9+7, sum n <= 2000.
key_idea: State (A = max so far, B = the largest element that is already below some earlier element). Appending x is allowed iff x >= B: if x >= A the state becomes (x,B), else (A,x). Use Fenwick trees per row and per column to sum the states quickly.

1. dp[A][B] counts subsequences. Start with dp[0][0]=1 (empty).
2. For each x: new (x,b) for b<=x gets the sum over A<=x of dp[A][b] (a column Fenwick).
3. New (A,x) for A>x gets the sum over B<=x of dp[A][B] (a row Fenwick).
4. Collect all deltas first, then add them (to both Fenwicks and the total).
5. The answer is the total count.

name: Simons and Beating Peaks

nearest_infosys_question: Q0917 Count tree colorings with B nodes at distance >= K
brief: Permutation a. Array is cool if no interior element is larger than both neighbors. Op: pick a peak (larger than both neighbors) and delete one of its neighbors. Min ops to make array cool.
key_idea: Recurse on the Cartesian tree (max-rooted): in a segment, its max must end up at one side, so delete everything on one side of it and recurse into the other.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0653 Special Prime Pairs
brief: Count integers in [l,r] (up to 1e18) whose binary representation is periodic with a proper period k | n.
key_idea: count(X) = sum over lengths n and divisors k<n of the numbers whose smallest period is exactly k. Count blocks <= the prefix bound, then use Möbius-like subtraction over the divisors of k.
solution:
1. For each length n <= len(X) and divisor k<n of n: c(k) = the number of k-bit blocks p (leading 1) with p repeated n/k times <= X.
2. If n < len(X), c(k) = 2^(k-1). If n == len(X): P = the top k bits of X, so c = P - 2^(k-1) + 1, minus 1 if rep(P) > X.
3. Exact smallest period: g(k) = c(k) - sum over d|k, d<k of g(d). Add g(k) for every proper k.
4. Answer = count(r) - count(l-1).

brief: In a tree you can jump up to distance k (k<=5). Sum the minimum number of jumps ceil(dist/k) over all pairs.
key_idea: ceil(d/k) = (d + (k - d mod k) mod k)/k. The sum of d comes from edge contributions sz*(n-sz). The correction term needs the number of pairs in each residue class of dist mod k, which you count at the LCA with per-node residue arrays c[v][r].
solution:
1. Root the tree. c[v][r] = number of nodes in v's subtree at depth ≡ r (mod k), relative to v.
2. When merging child v into p: shift c[v] by 1. For each pair r1, r2: extra += c[p][r1]*sh[r2]*((k-(r1+r2)%k)%k). Then add sh into c[p].
3. dsum += sz[v]*(n-sz[v]) for each edge.
4. The answer is (dsum + extra)/k.

nearest_infosys_question: Q0864 Longest Prefix which is also Suffix
brief: For a fixed s (|s|<=1e6) and q<=1e5 queries t (|t|<=10), output the prefix function of s+t at t's positions.

3. Root the tree. sub[v] = number of good vertices in v's subtree. G = total number of good vertices.
4. For each non-leaf q and each neighbour v with adj[v]: add the number of good p on v's side, which is sub[v] if v is a child of q, else G-sub[q].

brief: Rooted tree with n <= 2e5 and values a_i. For each k = 1..n, partition the vertices into k groups, each a chain (pairwise ancestor-related). Maximize the sum of group maxima, or -1 if impossible.
key_idea: (Per the editorial.) The minimum is k = #leaves. Bottom-up, each vertex joins the child chain with the smallest maximum x: the chain max becomes max(x, a_u) and min(x, a_u) becomes a 'spare'. Merge the min-heaps small-to-large. Larger k add the spares in descending order as singletons.
solution:
1. For i = n..1 (p_i < i): if heap[i] is empty push a_i; else pop x, push max(x, a_i), and record min(x, a_i) as a spare.
2. Merge heap[i] into heap[p_i] small-to-large.
3. L = |heap[1]|, ans[L] = the sum of heap[1].
4. Sort the spares descending; ans[k] = ans[k-1] + spare[k-L-1] for k > L; -1 for k < L.

brief: Given m and k, find any n ≤ 1e18 such that exactly m of the numbers n+1..2n have exactly k ones in binary.
key_idea: cnt(n) = f(2n) - f(n) is non-decreasing in n, and it increases by at most 1 per step, because moving to n+1 adds 2n+1 and 2n+2 and removes n+1, where popcount(2n+2) = popcount(n+1). f(x) counts the numbers ≤ x with popcount k through a digit-DP sum of binomial coefficients. 4. Print n.

2. Same for s2.

brief: Over all tree paths u..v (n<=2000), find the longest palindromic subsequence of the path's letters.
key_idea: Use the interval-LPS DP on paths. dp[u][v] = max(dp[next(u)][v], dp[u][next(v)], and dp[next(u)][next(v)]+2 if s_u==s_v), where next(u) = the neighbour of u toward v, which is par_v[u] when rooted at v. Process the pairs by increasing distance.

1. Root at every r to get par[r][x] and dist[r][x]. That is O(n^2).
2. Bucket the pairs (u<=v) by distance.

name: Even Number Addicts
nearest_infosys_question: Q0667 Golden Divisor Game
brief: Alice and Bob alternately remove one integer from a sequence (n <= 100), Alice first. Alice wins if the sum of the numbers she took is even. Who wins with optimal play?
key_idea: Only parities matter: state (odd count, even count, parity of Alice's sum, whose turn). Memoized win/lose DP of size 101*101*2*2.
solution:
1. Count o = #odd, e = #even.
2. A(o,e,s): Alice to move. If o=e=0 return s==0. Win if (o>0 and B(o-1,e,s^1)) or (e>0 and B(o,e-1,s)).
3. B(o,e,s): Bob to move. If o=e=0 return s==0. Alice wins only if every Bob move leads to an Alice win: (o==0 or A(o-1,e,s)) and (e==0 or A(o,e-1,s)).
4. Print Alice if A(o,e,0) else Bob.
dry_run:
Sample 1 2 3 4: o=2, e=2.
Whatever Alice takes, Bob can mirror so Alice ends with exactly one odd.
DP gives A(2,2,0) = false -> Bob.
Sample 1 3 5: o=3 -> Alice (takes 2 odds total).

name: Staircases
tags: brute force, combinatorics, data structures, dfs and similar, dp, implementation, math
nearest_infosys_question: Q0861 Multiply two strings
brief: n x m grid (<= 1000x1000), all cells free; q <= 1e4 queries flip a cell. After each query count staircases: zigzag paths (right,down,right... or down,right,down...) on free cells, single cells included.
key_idea: Count initially with DP; each flip changes the answer by the number of staircases through that cell = f1*b1 + f2*b2 - 1, found by walking the two zigzag lines in O(n+m).
solution:
1. Initial: R[i][j] = 1 + D[i][j+1], D[i][j] = 1 + R[i+1][j] (staircases starting at cell with first move right/down); ans = sum(R + D - 1).
2. Each cell lies on two maximal zigzag lines. For each line count free cells forward (f) and backward (b) from the cell, stopping at a locked cell.
3. through(cell) = f1*b1 + f2*b2 - 1 (single cell counted twice).
4. Locking: subtract through(cell) while it is still free; unlocking: free it then add through(cell). Use long long.
dry_run:
Sample 1, 2x2 all free: 4 single cells + 4 two-cell + 2 three-cell = 10 initially.
Query 1 locks (1,1): f1=3 (right,down), b1=1, f2=3, b2=1 -> 3+3-1 = 5; 10-5 = 5 (matches).
Query 2 unlocks -> 10, query 3 locks -> 5 (matches).

name: Another Sith Tournament
nearest_infosys_question: Q0668 Minimum subset with LCM equal to array LCM
brief: n<=18 Sith fight in sequence (the winner stays, the loser is replaced). Ivan (participant 1) chooses the starting pair and every replacement. Maximise Ivan's survival probability given the pairwise win probabilities.
key_idea: dp[mask][i] = Ivan's best survival probability when the set mask has already fought and i is the current champion. Choose the next challenger j optimally.
solution:
1. dp[full][0] = 1 (only Ivan remains); other dp[full][i] = 0.
2. For masks in decreasing order and champion i in mask: dp[mask][i] = max over j not in mask of p[i][j]*dp[mask|j][i] + p[j][i]*dp[mask|j][j].
3. Answer = max over i of dp[{i}][i]. This covers starting with i against the best j. For n=1 the answer is 1.
complexity: O(2^n * n^2) time, O(2^n * n) space
dry_run:
Sample: the best plan starts with 2 vs 3, and Ivan fights the winner.
2 wins with 0.4, then Ivan beats 2 with 0.5: 0.2.
3 wins with 0.6, then Ivan beats 3 with 0.8: 0.48.
Total 0.68.

name: Bear and Floodlight
nearest_infosys_question: Q0323 Cake recipes with 3 units each ingredient
brief: n <= 20 floodlights at (x_i, y_i > 0), each lighting an angle a_i <= 90 degrees that can be aimed freely. Starting at l, how far toward r can the bear walk with the segment continuously lit?
key_idea: dp[mask] = the farthest lit point using the lights in mask. To add light i at frontier p, aim one edge at (p,0) and rotate by a_i toward +x; the other edge hits the axis at a new frontier (or r if the ray no longer points down).
solution:
1. dp[all] = l.
2. For each mask and unused i: th = atan2(-y, p-x) + a.
3. If th >= 0 the light reaches r; else t = y/(-sin th), nx = x + t cos th.
4. dp[mask|i] = max(dp, min(nx, r)).
5. Print dp[full] - l.
dry_run:
Sample 2: light (1,1), 30 degrees, from p=0: angle -135 + 30 = -105 degrees.
t = 1/sin(105) = 1.035, nx = 1 - 0.268 = 0.732.
Output 0.732050808 (matches); all 4 samples match.

name: Array Shrinking
nearest_infosys_question: Q0269 Matrix Chain Multiplication Variant
brief: Array (n<=500). Replace two adjacent equal elements v,v by one v+1, any number of times. Minimum final length.
key_idea: val[l][r] = the single value segment l..r can collapse to (or -1); then the minimum number of collapsible pieces covering the array.
solution:
1. val[i][i] = a_i.
2. val[l][r] = val[l][k]+1 if some split k has val[l][k] == val[k+1][r] != -1.
3. dp[i] = min over j<i with val[j][i-1] != -1 of dp[j] + 1.
4. Answer dp[n].

name: Rarity and New Dress
tags: dfs and similar, dp, implementation, shortest paths
nearest_infosys_question: Q0299 Gold mine round trip (Cherry Pickup)
brief: Count the single-color diamonds (squares rotated 45°) that fit inside an n x m letter grid (n,m<=2000).
key_idea: Let t = min(left run, right run) of the same color at each cell, the half-width allowed in that row. up[i][j] = min(t, up[i-1][j]+1) when the cell above has the same color, and down is symmetric. The number of diamonds centered at (i,j) is min(up, down).
solution:
1. Compute the horizontal runs L and R. t = min(L,R).
2. up[i][j] = same color as above ? min(t[i][j], up[i-1][j]+1) : 1.
3. dn[i][j] = same color as below ? min(t[i][j], dn[i+1][j]+1) : 1.
4. ans = sum of min(up,dn) over all cells, as long long.
dry_run:
Sample 3x3 all 'a': the centre has t=2, up=2 and down=2, so it contributes 2. The other 8 cells contribute 1 each.
Total 10 (matches). The other samples give 12 and 31 (verified).

name: Game on Sum (Easy Version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0282 Buckets Probability
brief: Over n turns Alice picks a real x in [0,k], and Bob adds or subtracts it but must add at least m times. Alice maximizes and Bob minimizes. Find the final score mod 1e9+7.
key_idea: dp[i][j] = the value with i turns left and j adds still required. If j==i, Bob must add every time, so dp=i*k. If j==0, it is 0. Otherwise Alice picks x so that Bob is indifferent, giving dp[i][j] = (dp[i-1][j-1] + dp[i-1][j]) / 2.
solution:
1. dp[i][0]=0 and dp[i][i]=i*k.
2. For 0<j<i: dp[i][j] = (dp[i-1][j-1] + dp[i-1][j]) * inv2 mod p.
3. The answer is dp[n][m].
4. The sum of n is <= 2000, so O(n*m) per test is fine.
dry_run:
Sample (3,3,2): dp[3][3] = 3*2 = 6 (matches).
Sample (2,1,10): dp[2][1] = (dp[1][0] + dp[1][1])/2 = (0+10)/2 = 5 (matches).
All 7 samples were verified.

name: Subtangle Game (Easy Version)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0299 Gold mine round trip (Cherry Pickup)
brief: Players alternately pick cells holding a_1, a_2, ... in order, each strictly below and to the right of the previous pick. A player who cannot pick, or whose turn comes after the array has ended, loses. Who wins?
key_idea: win[k][i][j] = the player who must pick a_k inside the submatrix starting at (i,j) wins. Either they skip row i or column j (inherited from (i+1,j) or (i,j+1)), or they pick (i,j) when b=a_k and the opponent then loses at (i+1,j+1).
solution:
1. win[l][*][*] = false (the array has ended), and empty submatrices are false.
2. For k=l-1..0, with i and j going down: win = win[i+1][j] || win[i][j+1] || (b[i][j]==a_k && !next[i+1][j+1]).
3. Keep only two layers.
4. Print T if win[0][0][0], else N.
dry_run:
Sample 1: a=[1,2]. Tsovak's only 1 is at (1,1), and then Narek finds the 2 at (2,3) after which the array has ended, so N (matches).
All 3 samples give N T N (verified).

name: 0-1-Tree
tags: dfs and similar, divide and conquer, dp, dsu, trees
nearest_infosys_question: Q0374 Minimum spanning tree based problem
brief: A tree with 0/1 edges. Count the ordered pairs (x,y) whose path never uses a 0-edge after a 1-edge. n<=2e5.
key_idea: Valid paths are all-0, all-1, or 0s then 1s with a switch vertex v. Use a DSU over 0-edges and one over 1-edges: pairs in the same 0-comp, same 1-comp, plus (s0(v)-1)*(s1(v)-1) for each v.
solution:
1. Union the 0-edges in DSU0 and the 1-edges in DSU1.
2. Add s*(s-1) for every component of each DSU (ordered pairs inside it).
3. For each vertex v: add (size0(v)-1)*(size1(v)-1) (x in v's 0-comp, y in v's 1-comp, switching at v).
4. Use long long.
dry_run:
Sample: 0-components {2,3,5} (size 3). 1-components {1,2,4,7,6} (size 5).
3*2 + 5*4 = 26, and for v=2: (3-1)*(5-1) = 8.
Total 34.

name: Short Colorful Strip
nearest_infosys_question: Q0328 Vaccine dose scheduling count
brief: Strip of m = n unit cells, initially color 0. For i = 1..n, paint a segment that is currently one color with color i. Given the final coloring (a permutation), count painting processes mod 998244353 (n <= 500).
key_idea: In a segment whose colors all exceed the current background, the smallest color c (at position p) is painted first over an interval [a,b] containing p; left and right parts become independent subproblems.
solution:
1. f(l,r) = ways to produce c[l..r] on a single-colored background; f(empty)=1.
2. p = position of the minimum color in [l,r].
3. A = sum over a in [l,p] of f(l,a-1) * f(a,p-1); B = sum over b in [p,r] of f(p+1,b) * f(b+1,r).
4. f(l,r) = A * B mod p; answer f(1,n). Memoize.

name: Two Digit Strings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0231 LCS with extra conditions
brief: Two digit strings a and b; an operation replaces two adjacent digits of either string by their sum mod 10. Maximize the common length after making them equal, or -1.
key_idea: A final string = partition into segments; segments match iff cut points have equal prefix sums mod 10, so it's LCS of prefix-mod sequences.
solution:
1. Pa[i] = (a_1+...+a_i) mod 10, Pb likewise.
2. If Pa[n] != Pb[m] -> -1 (total sum mod 10 is invariant).
3. Choosing cuts i_1<...<i_k=n and j_1<...<j_k=m with Pa[i_t]==Pb[j_t] gives equal strings of length k.
4. Answer = LCS(Pa[1..n-1], Pb[1..m-1]) + 1 (the final pair always matches).
5. O(n*m) LCS with a rolling 1D array (sum of lengths <= 1e4 so at most 25e6 cells).

name: Bombing
nearest_infosys_question: Q0282 Buckets Probability
brief: Find the min blast radius R so that at least K of N objects are destroyed with failure probability <= eps (per mil). Objects at distance D<=R are destroyed surely; farther ones with P = e^(1 - D^2/R^2).
key_idea: The success probability is monotone in R. Binary search R and compute P(fewer than K destroyed) with a 'number of successes' probability DP.
solution:
1. Compute each distance D_i.
2. check(R): p_i = 1 if D_i<=R, else exp(1-D_i^2/R^2) (0 if R=0). dp[j] = P(exactly j destroyed), updated per object in O(N).
3. Feasible iff sum_{j<K} dp[j] <= eps/1000.
4. Binary search R in [0,3000] for ~100 iterations.
dry_run:
Sample 1: D=5, need P>=0.5: e^(1-25/R^2) = 0.5 gives 25/R^2 = 1+ln2 = 1.693.
R = sqrt(14.765) = 3.8426. Output matches.

name: Kaavi and Magic Spell
nearest_infosys_question: Q0302 Split string into K palindromes with swaps
brief: Characters of S (n<=3000) are taken in order and each is pushed to the front or back of A. Count the operation sequences (of any length) after which T is a prefix of A. Mod 998244353.
key_idea: A after len operations occupies some window [l,r] of the target, where positions >= m match anything. dp[l][r] = ways that the first r-l+1 chars of S form exactly the window [l..r].
solution:
1. match(pos,c) = pos >= m or T[pos] == c.
2. dp[i][i] = 2 if match(i, S[0]) (front and back both count).
3. For len>=2 with c=S[len-1]: dp[l][r] = (match(l,c) ? dp[l+1][r] : 0) + (match(r,c) ? dp[l][r-1] : 0).
4. Answer = sum over r>=m-1 of dp[0][r].
dry_run:
abab with T=ba: windows starting at 0 of length >= 2.
The count from the DP is 12 = 6 distinct ways x 2 (the first char's front/back choice).

name: Dot
nearest_infosys_question: Q0667 Golden Divisor Game
brief: Dot at (x,y); players alternately add one of n vectors (non-negative components) or reflect over y=x (once per player). Whoever moves the dot beyond distance d loses. Who wins?
key_idea: Reflection is useless (the opponent can reflect back), so it is a plain win/lose DP over points within distance d.
solution:
1. win(p) = exists vector v with |p+v|<=d and !win(p+v).
2. Vectors are non-negative and non-zero, so positions never repeat -> memoized recursion terminates.
3. Offset coordinates to index the memo array.
4. Print Anton if win(start).

name: Lena and Matrix
tags: data structures, dp, geometry, shortest paths
nearest_infosys_question: Q0389 Almost-equal matrix with minimum increments
brief: For an n x m grid of W/B cells, find a cell that minimizes the maximum Manhattan distance to any black cell.
key_idea: Use |dx|+|dy| = max(|(x+y)-(a+b)|, |(x-y)-(a-b)|). The farthest black cell is determined by the extremes of x+y and x-y over the black cells, so evaluate every cell in O(1).
solution:
1. Over the black cells, record the min and max of x+y and the min and max of x-y.
2. For each cell (a,b): far = max(a+b-minS, maxS-(a+b), a-b-minD, maxD-(a-b)).
3. Output the cell with the smallest far value.
4. Any optimal cell is accepted.
dry_run:
Sample 1: black cells (1,1) and (3,2). S is in [2,5], D is in [0,1].
Cell (2,1): S=3, D=1, far = max(1,2,1,-1) = 2.
This is optimal, so print 2 1 (matches).

name: Vittorio Plays with LEGO Bricks
nearest_infosys_question: Q0269 Matrix Chain Multiplication Variant
brief: Purple 2x2 bricks at (x_i, height h) with x_i increasing (gaps >= 2); add the minimum number of bricks (centers on y=0) so every brick off the ground rests on another with positive overlap.
key_idea: Each brick needs a column of h supports; two columns can share a brick once they meet: a group l..r merges at depth t = ceil((x_r - x_l)/2), saving the h - t + 1 bricks below; interval DP over merges plus a partition DP into groups.
solution:
1. dp[i][i] = h.
2. For l < r with t = ceil((x_r - x_l)/2) <= h: dp[l][r] = min over split m of dp[l][m] + dp[m+1][r] - (h - t + 1).
3. best[r] = min over l of best[l-1] + dp[l][r] (groups that never merge).
4. Answer best[n]. (Verified on all four samples; not proven here.)
dry_run:
Sample 2 (h=1): 11 and 13: t=1 <= 1 -> dp = 1+1-1 = 1.
Bricks 2 and 7 stay separate: 1 each.
Total 3 (matches); h=100 gives 107, sample 4 gives 8 (match).

name: Catching Cheaters
nearest_infosys_question: Q0276 Minimum cost string transformation with inverted mode
brief: Strings A,B (<=5000). Maximize 4*LCS(C,D)-|C|-|D| over substrings C of A and D of B.
key_idea: Kadane-style LCS: dp[i][j] = best score for substrings ending exactly at A[i], B[j]; extending a substring costs 1, a match gains 4-2=2.
solution: 1) dp[i][j] = max(0, dp[i-1][j]-1, dp[i][j-1]-1). 2) If A[i]==B[j]: dp[i][j]=max(dp[i][j], dp[i-1][j-1]+2). 3) Answer = max dp over all cells (0 for empty). 4) Rolling rows to save memory.
dry_run: Sample abba/babab: C=abb, D=abab, LCS 3: score 3 matches*2 = 6 minus 1 unmatched char in D = 5. Max dp = 5.

name: Alyona and Strings
nearest_infosys_question: Q0302 Split string into K palindromes with swaps
brief: Choose k non-empty substrings that appear in the same order, without overlapping, in both s and t (lengths <= 1000). Maximize their total length.
key_idea: Use an LCS-like DP with a piece count. e[l][i][j] = best when the l-th piece ends exactly at (i,j), so it can be extended diagonally. g[l][i][j] = best within the prefixes.
solution:
1. Initialise e and g to -inf, and g[0][*][*] = 0.
2. If s_i == t_j: e[l][i][j] = max(e[l][i-1][j-1], g[l-1][i-1][j-1]) + 1, meaning extend the piece or start piece l.
3. g[l][i][j] = max(g[l][i-1][j], g[l][i][j-1], e[l][i][j]).
4. The answer is g[k][n][m]. The two int arrays of 11*1001*1001 take about 88 MB.
complexity: O(k n m) time and space
dry_run:
Sample abc / ab, k=2: e[1] at (1,1) = 1 for 'a'.
Then 'b' at (2,2): start piece 2 from g[1][1][1] = 1, giving e[2][2][2] = 2.
g[2][3][2] = 2 (matches). Sample 2 gives 7 (verified).

name: Vlad and Avoiding X
tags: bitmasks, brute force, dfs and similar, dp, implementation
nearest_infosys_question: Q0146 Minimum Inversions via XOR
brief: 7x7 black/white grid: minimum cell flips so that no black cell has all four diagonal neighbours black (t <= 200).
key_idea: An X only involves cells of one (i+j) parity, so the two parity classes are independent; for each, iterative-deepening search: find a violating X and try whitening each of its 5 cells.
solution:
1. For parity p in {0,1}, find the minimum d such that dfs(d) succeeds.
2. dfs(d): find any black center (i+j)%2 == p with 4 black diagonals; none -> true; d == 0 -> false.
3. Try setting each of the 5 cells to white, recurse with d-1, restore.
4. Only black->white flips are useful. Answer = sum over both parities (each needs at most 4).
complexity: O(5^d * 25) per class with d <= 4, tiny
dry_run:
Test 2: black block rows 2-4, cols 1-5 (0-based) gives X centres (3,2),(3,4) of one parity and (3,3) of the other.
Centres (3,2),(3,4) share corners (2,3),(4,3): whitening (2,3) kills both -> 1 flip.
(3,3) needs 1 flip. Total 2 (matches).

name: Encryption (medium)
nearest_infosys_question: Q0257 Grid one cell per row with column-transition bonus
brief: Split N<=2e4 numbers into exactly k<=50 contiguous parts; score of a part = sum mod p (p<=100). Maximise the total score.
key_idea: dp[j][i] only depends on dp[j-1][t] through pre[t] mod p, so keep best[r] = max dp[j-1][t] with pre[t] == r: O(k*N*p).
solution:
1. pre[i] = prefix sum mod p.
2. For each j: sweep i, adding dp[j-1][i-1] into best[pre[i-1]].
3. dp[j][i] = max over r of best[r] + (pre[i]-r) mod p.
4. Answer dp[k][N].

name: Minimizing the Sum
nearest_infosys_question: Q0256 Alpha/Beta safe zone partitioning
brief: Array a; one operation sets an element equal to an adjacent element. With at most k<=10 operations, minimize the array sum.
key_idea: Final array = segments each filled with its own minimum; a segment of length len costs len-1 operations.
solution:
1. dp[i][j] = min sum of the first i elements using j operations.
2. Transition: the last segment is a[i-len+1..i] (len <= j+1), all set to its minimum m: dp[i][j] = min dp[i-len][j-len+1] + len*m.
3. Compute m incrementally while extending len backwards.
4. Answer = min over j<=k of dp[n][j]. Use long long.

name: Yet Another Number Game
nearest_infosys_question: Q0667 Golden Divisor Game
brief: Game on n<=3 numbers (<300): subtract any positive x from one number, or subtract the same x from all numbers (x <= min). The player who cannot move loses. Who wins?
key_idea: n=1: the first player wins iff a>0. n=2: Wythoff's game (compute win/lose with an O(300^3) DP). n=3: the first player loses iff a1^a2^a3 = 0 (known result).
solution:
1. n=1: a>0 means BitLGM wins.
2. n=2: win[i][j] is true if some move (decrease i, decrease j, or decrease both by x) reaches a losing state. Fill in increasing order.
3. n=3: the losing positions are exactly those with xor 0. This can be verified by brute force, since the 'subtract from all' moves never help.
4. Print BitLGM if the first player wins, otherwise BitAryo.
dry_run:
(1,1): subtract 1 from both to reach (0,0), a loss for the opponent, so BitLGM.
(1,2): every move reaches (0,2), (1,1), (1,0) or (0,1), and all of those are wins for the mover, so BitAryo.
(1,2,1): xor = 2 != 0, so BitLGM.

name: Number Deletion Game
nearest_infosys_question: Q0322 Listing Products (insert second group)
brief: k rounds: Alice picks a non-maximum number a, Bob picks a larger number b, both are removed and b-a is scored. Alice maximises, Bob minimises. n<=400 distinct numbers.
key_idea: After sorting, the game value equals the best choice of disjoint contiguous blocks of even length 2L (total k pairs). Each block scores (sum of its top half) - (sum of its bottom half). (Verified against a brute-force minimax.)
solution:
1. Sort a and build prefix sums P.
2. d[i][j] = best value using the suffix from i with j pairs still to form. d[i][0]=0.
3. d[i][j] = max(d[i+1][j] (skip a_i), max over L<=j of block(i,L) + d[i+2L][j-L]), where block = (P[i+2L]-P[i+L]) - (P[i+L]-P[i]).
4. The answer is d[0][k].
dry_run:
Sample 1: sorted 1..5, k=2.
The block [1,2,3,4] (L=2) scores (3+4)-(1+2) = 4, and the block [2,3,4,5] also scores 4. Two blocks [1,2],[4,5] give only 2.
Answer 4.

name: Changing a String
nearest_infosys_question: Q0318 Partition by Increasing Beauty
brief: Turn string s into t (lengths <= 1000) with the minimum number of INSERT/DELETE/REPLACE operations, and print the operations with their positions.
key_idea: Use the standard edit-distance DP. Backtrack from (n,m) and emit ops right-to-left, so the positions of earlier characters never shift.
solution:
1. d[i][j] = edit distance between s[0..i) and t[0..j).
2. Backtrack from (n,m). On a match or replace diagonal, emit REPLACE i t[j-1] if the characters differ. Delete emits DELETE i. Insert emits INSERT i+1 t[j-1].
3. Ops are produced from the right end of the string to the left. Each affects only positions >= i, so the indices stay valid in emission order.
4. Print the count, then the ops in that order.
dry_run:
ABA to ABBBA: d=2.
Backtrack: A=A (diagonal), then insert B at position 2, insert B at position 2, then match B and A.
Output 2 ops, "INSERT 2 B" twice, giving ABBBA (a valid alternative answer).

name: Erase Subsequences
nearest_infosys_question: Q0317 Optimal run-length encoding after deletions
brief: Can t be formed by taking at most two disjoint subsequences of s in order (the first then the second, concatenated)? |s| <= 400.
key_idea: Try every split t = a + b. dp[j] = the max prefix of b matched while j chars of a are matched, scanning s once. Greedy matching of b is safe for a fixed j.
solution:
1. For each split k: a = t[0..k), b = t[k..).
2. dp[j] = max matched of b (-1 if unreachable). Initially dp[0]=0.
3. For each char of s, j descending: if s_i == a[j], set dp[j+1] = max(dp[j+1], dp[j]); if s_i == b[dp[j]], dp[j]++.
4. YES if dp[|a|] >= |b| for some split.
dry_run:
s=ababcd, t=abcba: split into 'abc' + 'ba'.
Take 'abc' from positions 1,4,5 (a,b,c). The rest 'b a d' (positions 2,3,6) contains 'ba'.
The DP reaches dp[3] >= 2, so YES.
